News.title: Moment drunk man, 34, on speed boosted e-bike yells ‘yeehaw woohoo’ in front of cops before being arrested
News.content:
Next

THIS is the reckless moment a drunk man riding a speed-boosted e-bike yells “yeehaw woohoo” in front of cops, before being arrested.

Sahil Sahil, 34, of Bilston, West Midlands, appeared at Norwich Magistrates’ Court on November 9.



He pleaded guilty to driving while disqualified, drink driving and having no insurance.

The offences took place on November 7 at around 9.15pm.



Sahil, who was riding an illegal e-bike, was stopped by officers on George Pope Road, Norwich.

The clip begins as Sahil rides along on his e-bike and yells out “yeehaw” as he goes past the cops and stops.

An officer then says hello and orders him off the bike.

The footage cuts to the police checking the bike over and examining the throttle.



An officer said: “That is very illegal.”

Sahil is then questioned by the police who ask if he has a driving licence, which he admits he doesn’t.

He’s then told he is under arrest.

Sahil is then breathalysed and found to be over the limit.

He is also arrested for that offence and read his rights.



A check of the bike showed it was propelled by a throttle and capable of reaching speeds of up to 21.7mph, above the legal limit for an electrically assisted pedal cycle (EAPC) which is 15.5mph.

Officers asked Sahil to provide a roadside breath test, which he failed.

He was arrested on suspicion of drink driving and driving without a licence and taken to Aylsham Police Investigation Centre for questioning.

While in custody, he provided an evidential breath sample of 67 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, nearly double the legal limit of 35 micrograms.

He was subsequently charged for the offences and remanded into custody.



During his appearance at Norwich Magistrates’ Court, Sahil was sentenced for 18 weeks and was disqualified from driving for 49 months.

He was also ordered to pay £85 in costs and surcharge of £154.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In June 2026, Sahil was sentenced to 24 weeks in prison, suspended for 12 months. This was for a separate driving offence.

He has now been ordered to serve this sentence so will therefore be serving 42 weeks in total.

News.title: Thrill-seeker, 21, dies in freak paragliding accident after crashing into field as tributes pour in for ‘selfless’ man
News.content:
SKY TRAGEDY Thrill-seeker, 21, dies in freak paragliding accident after crashing into field as tributes pour in for ‘selfless’ man







Next

A YOUNG thrill-seeker has died in a freak paragliding accident after he crashed into a field, as tributes pour in.

Giovanni Lopez, 21, was killed on Saturday afternoon in Plainfield, a town some 35 miles southwest of Chicago, Illinois.

The Plainfield Police Department says they responded to reports of the crash at around 2.57pm.



The Kendall County Coroner’s Office was summoned to the crash site around 3.40pm and formally pronounced Lopez dead.



He was publicly identified by the coroner’s office later that day.

His official cause and manner of death is pending on the results of an autopsy.

Read More on US News HORROR PLUNGE Bodycam vid shows moment student, 21, who fell 65ft out window found by pals

The Plainfield Police Department is investigating the cause of the crash.

Lopez was a big fan of paragliding and often posted photos and clips of himself in the air to his social media pages.

While some pictures and videos show him cruising along and taking in the surrounding view, others though feature him doing spins and acrobatic maneuvers.

Lopez’s pal and fellow paraglider Curtis Haley, 33 told the Daily Mail that “Gio” was “a selfless, kind individual who would do nothing but help people.”

Haley added that they had been close friends for around a year after the two met while paragliding.



He said that Lopez’s death had been extremely difficult both for himself and the tight-knit paragliding community.

Haley said: “This whole circumstance and situation is hard to believe, and I’m at a loss for words,” he said, adding that the last time the two flew together was on Tuesday.

He said: “I literally couldn’t sleep last night at all. I’ve been up since 3am. I might’ve gotten 15 to 30 minutes of sleep.”

Haley said that after the crash had been reported but before his friend had been identified, he had called various friends checking they were okay.

But, he said, he got no answer when he called Lopez, saying he tried to call 15 to 20 times.



His fiancée went to the crash site and spotted Lopez’s glider on the ground, confirming to them he had crashed.

He called the horror accident “a wakeup call”.

Haley added that the paragliding community was in “disbelief” and many had been discussing the tragedy in group chats.

While Haley said he had been paragliding for about four years, Lopez had started in May 2025.

They had both had training at flight school and he described Lopez as “a skilled pilot”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added both were taught “the right way” and always flew as safely as possible.

Haley wouldn’t speculate on what may have happened to cause the crash but added: “Anything can happen”.

News.title: Student, 21, breaks silence after drunken 65ft fall from window as bodycam video reveals moment terrified pals found her
News.content:
Next

A STUDENT who survived an eight-storey fall from a window while drunk told cops in her first words after waking up that no one had pushed her.

Dramatic bodycam clips showed Kristin Sargent, 21, being found with several broken bones as terrified pals raced downstairs fearing she was dead.



The University of Georgia student was celebrating after her college team, the Bulldogs, beat the Oklahoma Sooners 41-13 in September.

In the newly surfaced bodycam video, stunned friends told cops how they could not believe she had survived the terrifying plunge.



Kristin was also heard telling emergency services later on in hospital: “No one did anything bad to me.”

A roommate told officers the student had been drinking beer and dancing on a couch while singing The Climb by Miley Cyrus when she fell.

READ MORE US NEWS CLASS HORROR High schooler dies after falling from 4th floor 'as he fled classroom fight'



She plummeted backwards and through a window from her eighth-floor five-bedroom apartment in Athens, Georgia.

Apartment security camera clips showed Kristin falling, with the window screen following behind her.



A friend said to police in the clip: “I thought I was coming down here to see her dead.”

He told cops: “We were dancing, and we were singing ‘The Climb’ by Miley Cyrus.

“We had our glass up, but the screen was down. She was dancing and fell backward…



“Have you seen anything like this before? I think it was a miracle the fact that she wasn’t dead.”

One officer could be heard saying Kristin had an open femur fracture and blood coming from a wound in her chest.

Despite suffering severe injuries, Kristin managed to survive the steep drop.

Police suspect the student was so drunk that she may have forgotten to brace her body for the fall, thereby lessening the severity of the impact as she landed.

Kristin was found on top of a metal bench with a cushion that had its armrest broken.



A hospital administrator later described Sargent as “drunk” when she arrived at the hospital.

“I would die if I fell from that. She’s just a beast.

“We were all like, if anyone’s gonna come back from this, it’s Kristin.”

Kristin, who had friends over at her apartment when the fall took place, had been out at bars before going home to drink more with mates.

She now faces a lengthy recovery period following the harrowing drop in September, her loved ones said.

News.title: Calculated killer dyed his hair red as tried to evade cops after stabbing man, 40, to death just days before Christmas
News.content:
RUTHLESS MURDER Calculated killer dyed his hair red as tried to evade cops after stabbing man, 40, to death just days before Christmas







Next

A MURDERER dyed his hair red and shaved off his beard to evade a police manhunt after stabbing a stranger outside his flat just days before Christmas.

Leon Douglas, 45, drastically changed his appearance in an effort to avoid detection after fatally wounding Khalid Marchoud with a kitchen knife in North London.



Khalid, 40, was found collapsed outside a ninth-floor apartment on Tollgate Gardens in Maida Vale on December 19 last year.

He was taken to St Mary’s Hospital in Paddington but was declared dead later that evening.



Witnesses recalled how Douglas had arrived at the block of flats to visit a former housemate.

But the thug became involved in an altercation after yelling through Khalid’s letterbox, demanding to be granted entry.

After he was let in, Douglas armed himself with a knife from the kitchen and pursued Khalid out of the flat before stabbing him.

He then made an escape by throwing the knife at a window before climbing out of the building onto the roof.

The vile killer was then seen walking towards Kilburn High Road.

Cowardly Douglas then changed his clothes before spending the evening with friends at a pub.



Douglas then discarded all the clothes he had worn during the incident before dying his hair and shaving his beard as police launched a search.

But he was tracked to an address in Cricklewood where he was arrested by officers four days later, despite again trying to escape via a rear ground-floor window.

The knifeman was taken into custody and charged with murder on Christmas Eve last year.

Following a nine-day trial at Harrow Crown Court, he was found guilty on Tuesday.

He is to be sentenced at a later date.



Detective Inspector Sarah Philippe, who led the investigation, said: “This was a senseless and brutal act of violence which resulted in the tragic death of Khalid Marchoud.

“Our thoughts remain with Khalid’s family and loved ones, who continue to live with the devastating consequences of Douglas’ actions.

“I would like to thank the witnesses who came forward and supported our investigation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Their assistance was invaluable in helping us build the case that secured this conviction.

“This verdict reflects the strength of evidence presented to the court and demonstrates our determination to pursue those responsible for serious violence and bring them to justice.”

News.title: Spain declares emergency in Canary Islands as 2,200 migrants flood tourist hotspot in just TWO days after Ceuta crisis
News.content:
Next

SPAIN has declared an emergency in the Canary Islands after 2,200 migrants flooded the tourist hotspot in just two days.

A record number of people arrived in the archipelago from Africa over the weekend – sparking fears of a Ceuta-like immigration crisis.



Over the last month, the number of migrants trying to reach the Canaries has ballooned.

Many have come from countries in Africa including Senegal, Gambia, and Guinea.



Skyrocketing figures come after some 80,000 people crossed the border into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in late July.

Over the weekend, the tiny Canary island of El Hierro was overwhelmed by another massive influx – putting intense strain on their immigration facilities.



They declared a state of emergency and have asked Madrid for urgent assistance to tackle the spiralling problem.

In the last two weeks, over 3,300 migrants have arrived on the volcanic island.



At least 30 boats have been recorded on the shores of the picturesque holiday hotspot.

The head of government in the Canaries, Fernando Clavijo, said: “The Canary Islands cannot continue to face, practically on their own, a situation that requires the involvement of the Spanish government and Europe.”

Spain’s maritime rescue service said almost 2,200 migrants reached the archipelago over the weekend.



Many of the migrants travelling from the coast of West Africa got off at El Hierro, which has a population of just 11,000 people.

At least 12 boats arrived at El Hierro, one at Gran Canaria, and another at Tenerife.

On Saturday alone, nearly 1,500 migrants came to the islands – the highest number in a single day since 2020.



So far this year, 13,000 migrants have arrived in the Canary Islands – representing about half of the total number who entered Spain.

The rate of boat crossings usually picks up in autumn due to calmer seas and more predictable weather.

But that doesn’t mean the journey is by any means safe.

Whatever the weather, the crossing between west Africa’s coast and the Canaries is one of the world’s most dangerous migration routes.



The islands are roughly 65 miles from the closest point in Africa, but to avoid police vessel patrols, many migrant boats take longer routes.

The perilous journey to reach the Spanish territories can take up to three weeks.

The Canary migrant crisis comes just two weeks before Spaniards head to the polls for a general election.

According to recent polling, socialist PM Pedro Sanchez could be on his way out – with his party trailing behind the Right.



Sanchez offered amnesty to around one million illegal migrants already living in Spain – a decision some experts say has backfired.

El Hierro is the second smallest of the Canary islands – an idyllic tourist favourite boasting volcanic landscapes, hiking trails and historic towns.

The recent surge comes as Ceuta continues to grapple with its migration crisis after tens of thousands of people stormed its borders in July.

Most returned to Morocco in the following days, but the government said 5,000 remain, angering residents and straining resources.

Following the Ceuta border rush in July, the Spanish government has been facing mounting pressure over its handling of the migration crisis.



Despite its claims that only 5,000 are still in the enclave, Ceuta’s mayor says as many as 15,000 remain.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Many migrants, including unaccompanied minors, remain sleeping in the streets despite local efforts to shelter, register and deport people back to Morocco.

News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'DO NOT APPROACH'

'DO NOT APPROACH' Urgent manhunt after jailed leader of drug gang, 32, walks out of prison as public issued warning







Next

COPS have launched an urgent manhunt after a jailed leader of a drugs gang walked out of prison.

Gwent Police have appealed for information in their search for Dwayde Stock, 32, after he absconded from HMP Prescoed on November 14.

He was last seen on Malpas Road, Newport at 6pm that day.



Stock is described as a white man about 5’9” tall of a slim build, wearing his hair tied back in a ponytail.



He was last seen wearing a grey jacket, a grey tracksuit top, black tracksuit bottoms, black trainers and a black watch.

He has links to Newport, Cardiff, Lancashire, Swansea and Neath, Port Talbot.

Cops have issued a “do not approach” warning as he is no longer in the custody of the prison service.



Police added the prison is co-operating fully with them.

Stock was serving a sentence for drug supply and modern-day slavery offences.

He recruited a vulnerable 15-year-old boy in a phone call he made from prison.

Stock was sentenced to nine years behind bars.



Stock, then 28, was recorded speaking to the teenager on a prison phone while he was on remand in April 2022.

Five other members of the Newport-based “county lines” drugs gang were jailed.

The gang members exploited the boy to sell drugs to teenagers in Neath.

Members of the public are advised not to approach Stock and to instead call police if they see him or have any information on 101, quoting 2600372425, you can send a direct message on Facebook or X, or online.

Alternatively, you can call Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111 or visit http://www.crimestoppers-uk.org.

News.title: Shock footage ‘shows BMW driving erratically in cop chase’ before crash that killed woman, 23, & man, 22 – as 4 arrested
News.content:
Next

SHOCKING footage appears to show a BMW driving erratically moments before a horror crash that killed two people.

A 23-year-old woman and a man, aged 22, died in a tragic collision in Leeds in the early hours of Sunday morning that saw four arrested.



West Yorkshire Police said a blue BMW failed to stop for cops at 12.44am this morning, so officers gave chase.

A 39-year-old man, two boys aged 16 and 17 and a 16-year-old girl were inside the car.



A white Volkswagen was turning onto the road where the chase was taking place when the horror crash unfolded.

Footage has since emerged of a dark blue vehicle appearing to travel erratically at speed not long before the fatal crash in Leeds.



The motor – believed to be a BMW – was seen careering wildly at a roundabout as other stunned drivers watched on.

However, it is unclear if the shocking footage is related to the horror crash on Sunday just before 1am.

Today’s early morning incident tragically saw the driver of the Volkswagen, a 22-year-old man from York, die at the scene.

Meanwhile, the passenger in the car, a woman, 23, was rushed to hospital but sadly died a short time later.



The three other people in the BMW, two boys aged 16 and 17 and a 16-year-old girl, were taken to hospital.

The teenagers in the BMW were taken to hospital for treatment to injuries that were not considered life-threatening.

It comes after cops arrested a man, 39, on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving while over the prescribed limit for cannabis.



The three teenagers have each been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving, said cops.

A referral has been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct which has declared an independent investigation.

West Yorkshire Police said in a statement: “We are appealing for witnesses following a road traffic collision in Leeds which has tragically resulted in the deaths of two people.

“At 12.44am this morning a blue BMW 123D failed to stop for a police vehicle in Gelderd Road.

“A pursuit was commenced and the BMW was involved in a collision with a white Volkswagen Scirocco which was turning into Gelderd Road from Lowfields Road.



“The driver of the Volkswagen, a 22-year-old man from York, was sadly pronounced deceased at the scene, and a passenger in the same car, a 23-year-old woman from York, was sadly pronounced deceased at hospital a short time later.

“A 39-year-old man from Harrogate has been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving while over the prescribed limit for cannabis in relation to the incident and remains in custody.

“Three other occupants of the BMW, two boys aged 16 and 17 and a 16-year-old girl, were taken to hospital for treatment to injuries that were not considered life threatening.



“They have each been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

“A scene and road closure remain in place in Gelderd Road, and drivers are advised to avoid the area and seek alternative routes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A referral has been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct which has declared an independent investigation.

“Anyone who witnessed the collision or saw either vehicle in the time leading up to it, particularly anyone with relevant dashcam, mobile phone or CCTV footage, is asked to contact officers via 101 or online via http://www.westyorkshire.police.uk/livechat quoting reference 13260649342.”

News.title: Fury as neighbours ‘imprisoned in the dark’ by ‘oil tanker-like’ car garage built within ‘touching distance’ of gardens
News.content:
SHED OF HORRORS Fury as neighbours ‘imprisoned in the dark’ by ‘oil tanker-like’ car garage built within ‘touching distance’ of gardens







Next

LOCALS are in uproar after their homes were engulfed in the shadows of an “oil tanker-like” garage built within inches of their gardens.

Residents in Shurdington, Gloucestershire, say the huge metal structure has stolen their daylight and ruined their views.



Many claim it is impossible to sleep due to the tinny vibrations of the flags on their masts, especially in blustery conditions.

Business owner Peter Davidson, 61, applied to redevelop Shire Cars back in 2022 – spending an eye-watering £1.5million on the project.



He insists he has “not done anything wrong” and the structure follows the original plans that were approved.

After the garage was finished, neighbours complained about its looming presence which “imprisoned them in the dark”.





Homeowner Mark Welsh, 55, said the workshop was “absurdly large” and came so close to the boundary he was able to touch it.

The married dad-of-two, who runs a product and business design company, said: “When the planning application was first submitted, I was completely unconcerned.

“I couldn’t believe Shire Cars would apply for something so obviously inappropriate.

“It’s the largest building within a half-mile radius and it’s so close you can stand in our garden and reach out and knock on the wall.”

Describing it as an “oppressive” 7.1m tall and 33m wide metal “shoebox”, he said it has “ruined” his family bungalow and that living in the gloom is “depressing”.



“From the moment the walls went up, we have been shut off and imprisoned in the dark,” he said.

“Our garden is now towered over by walls and we had to drain the pond because it was being covered in algae.

“We can’t get a phone signal in some places, we can’t install solar panels and we have to have the heating on more.

“And living in gloom is depressing.

“So now we face another long, dark and winter, while Shire Cars continue trading in their giant premises”.



Davidson claims he was granted full approval to undertake the monster development and insists he has done nothing wrong.

Mark said he objected to the proposal when it was first submitted in 2021 – along with 36 other people.

He claims the building has ended up 1.2 times bigger than initially agreed.

“It grew taller and they changed the design of the roof, so it ended up blocking out even more light,” he said.

“The whole thing was badly designed, and even more badly managed.”



Reflecting on the impact on his property, he said: “This is our pension, our long-term investment, and we can’t allow it to be trampled like this.

Other residents complained that the flagpoles erected on the site create “excessive noise”.

One local wrote: “Large flagpoles with flas installed on the site generate excessive and persisten noise which impact significantly, especially during windy conditions.

They likened it to bins being struck repeatedly, with it being particularly disruptive during quieter periods.

Peter claims he has done his utmost to stick to the approved plans but unexpected deviations have violated certain planning permissions, meaning the future of Shire Cars now hangs in the balance.



“The strain on my family and I is phenomenal, I’ve cashed every pension I have, re-mortgaged our home and sold my cars,” said Peter.

“If I’m not successful I’ll be bankrupt.”

He said that various requirements were introduced after planning had begun, like a rear fire escape door and an air movement system – meaning he had to change the dimensions of the place halfway through.

Sarah Hands, from Tewkesbury Borough Council, said: “Councillors refused the application as they felt the size, height and position of the development would have an unacceptable impact on a neighbouring property, by reducing light and affecting its outlook.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The applicant has the right to appeal to the Planning Inspectorate, which would independently review the case.”

News.title: Bird flu is suspected at poultry farm in Northern Ireland as restrictions imposed
News.content:
Bird flu is suspected at poultry farm in Northern Ireland as restrictions imposed

The Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Daera) said veterinary officials went to the premises on Sunday, where they imposed restrictions and took official samples for testing

View Image A sign is seen at the entrance to a farm after a previous suspected case of bird flu in Surrey (Image: PA)

A suspected case of bird flu is currently being investigated at a commercial poultry site in Northern Ireland, according to the agriculture department.

‌



‌



Controls have been placed on the flock following substantial mortality levels and clinical symptoms consistent with avian influenza being detected. The Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Daera) confirmed veterinary officers attended the site in County Tyrone on Sunday, and they implemented the restrictions and collected official samples for analysis.

‌



The samples have been sent to the UK National Reference Laboratory at Weybridge, Surrey, with results anticipated on Monday. Agriculture Minister Andrew Muir said: "I recognise the impact this situation is having on the affected flock-keeper, alongside the concern and uncertainty it creates for the wider poultry sector. While the disease has not yet been confirmed, we are treating this situation with the utmost seriousness."

‌



Free-range eggs to remain on supermarket shelves despite new bird flu chicken lockdown READ MORE :

Gardeners' World shares one food to attract robins to British gardens READ MORE :

What is Bird Flu? H5N1 detailed by health expert

He added: "My officials have acted swiftly to investigate the reported case at a commercial poultry premises in Co Tyrone and place the premises under restriction.

‌



"We have robust contingency plans in place and stand ready to implement the measures required to respond at the affected premises should highly pathogenic avian influenza be confirmed.

"In light of these findings, we are actively considering the need for further disease control measures across Northern Ireland, informed by the latest veterinary and epidemiological advice and assessment of risk."

‌



Chief veterinary officer Brian Dooher said: "Disease control arrangements have been activated, and contingency planning is under way should highly pathogenic avian influenza be confirmed.

"The premises remains under restriction and Daera veterinary officials continue to oversee the situation on site. I urge all poultry keepers to remain vigilant, maintain good biosecurity and report any concerns about the health of their birds to Daera without delay."

Article continues below

The department confirmed that further updates would be issued once laboratory results become available. Should the disease be confirmed, the appropriate disease control measures would be put in place immediately.

"Further communications will be issued to keep the industry, wider stakeholders and the public informed," a department spokesman said.

News.title: Russell Brand's wife Laura Gallacher shares first chilling message from rapist husband since sentence
News.content:
Russell Brand's wife Laura Gallacher shares first chilling message from rapist husband since sentence

Laura Gallacher, who married Russell Brand in 2017, has shared a message claiming to be from her husband via their YouTube podcast - days after he was jailed for rape and sexual assault

View 3 Images Jailed Russell Brand's wife reads statement from him and claims 'something strange is happening' (Image: YouTube)

Russell Brand's wife Laura Gallacher has shared a chilling message claiming to be from her husband - speaking publicly for the first time since he was given a 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence for rape and sexual assault.

The disgraced comedian was jailed after being found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others during his career.

Earlier this year Brand and Gallacher began releasing a weekly YouTube podcast called Sunday Service, which they carried on recording throughout his trial.

View 3 Images (Image: Getty Images)

On Sunday, Gallacher released another episode which began with her reading a passage from Brand’s bible, PA reports.

The 39-year-old, who is the daughter of Ryder Cup winning golfer Bernard Gallacher, said during the episode: “Russell has asked me to read something to you.”

Reading the message from a notebook, she went on: “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support.

“As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.

“The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do.

“I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey, little as in small, and hey as in hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe.

“The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated.

“And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone.

“I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us.”

View 3 Images Laura is sanding by her husband (Image: Getty Images)

Gallacher choked up as she said: “Please support my treasured wife and family. I feel your prayers, your brother in Christ. Russell.”

She began the episode by saying she is here to “continue the good work that was being established here in this Sunday service community, something very, very close to mine and Russell’s heart”.

‌



“It may look different, but the ambitions are very much the same, and we trust God, and we trust his plan, and we trust everything he’s doing right now,” she added.

“Even though it’s painful, and obviously, will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me, but I want to continue, and I’m grateful for the support.”

‌



Gallacher said she is speaking to her husband, adding: “He’s okay, and he’s praying.”

According to The Sun on Sunday, Brand was moved out of HMP Wandsworth and transported to the category C prison HMP Littlehey on Friday.

‌



The prison offers a large variety of extra-curricular activities for its inmates, including yoga, choir and indoor bowls.

Brand was sentenced to a 10-and-a-half-year prison term on Monday afternoon.

He is expected to serve two-thirds of his prison sentence before being released on licence.

He will be on the sex offenders’ register for life.

News.title: Met Office urges Brits in 38 areas to prepare emergency kit - full list
News.content:
Met Office urges Brits in 38 areas to prepare emergency kit - full list

A yellow warning for ice and another one for snow will affect dozens of areas across England and Scotland, with people advised to take measures

View 3 Images Snow will affect 23 areas (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

Dozens of areas across England and Scotland will be hit by ice and snow in the next two days as people have been urged to plan ahead.

‌



‌



This comes as a yellow weather warning for ice will stay in place until 10am on Monday, followed by a yellow warning for snow on Tuesday, between midnight and midday. A total of 38 areas are forecast to be affected by the two warnings, with people told to prepare "emergency travel kits".

‌



In relation to both warnings, the Met Office said: "Before you head off in winter, it’s best to be prepared. Pack an emergency travel kit. Check your lights and tyres and clear your windscreens of any ice or snow."

‌



The kits should include de-icer spray, an ice-scraper, a torch, spare batteries, a high-vis jacket, spare warm clothes and a blanket. People should also always have a first aid kit, jump start cables, an empty fuel can, water and food, a shovel and a phone backup battery.

The ice warning will cause icy stretches to develop overnight, which are "likely" to lead to difficult driving conditions. Some injuries from slips and falls are also to be expected, the Met Office added.

View 3 Images A map of the ice warning (Image: Met Office)

‌



The warning states: "An area of rain and hill snow (snow mainly above 200 m but not expected to be impactful) will clear to the southeast tonight with skies then at least partially clearing. This will result in temperatures falling below freezing and some icy stretches developing on untreated surfaces.

"This is likely to lead to difficult driving conditions. These conditions will probably not develop across northern England and southeast Scotland until the end of the night.

‌



"Across northern Scotland, icy conditions are likely to be exacerbated by some wintry showers, with snow falling to low levels for a time before becoming mainly confined to higher ground late in the night. No more than 1-2 cm is likely at lower levels, with higher ground perhaps seeing up to 4 or 5 cm from these wintry showers."

People have also been urged to leave their homes at least five minutes early to avoid rushing, which could lead to accidents. The ice will mainly affect Scotland, but some areas in northeastern and northwestern England will also be impacted.

‌



The Met Office said: "Whenever you’re planning to travel, don’t be in a rush. During winter months, conditions can be tricky – if you’re running late, it might be tempting go faster than is safe in the conditions. Make the journey as smooth as possible and get there in plenty of time."

Fourteen hours after the conclusion of the ice warning, the snow warning will come into place, bringing up to 15cm of snow on high ground. Roads and railways are likely to be affected and there will also be a "small chance" of power cuts and poor mobile service.

‌



View 3 Images A map of the areas covered by snow (Image: Met Office)

The warning states: "A band of rain is expected to head northwards across the UK through Monday night and Tuesday morning. As it encounters colder air across the highlighted region, it is likely to turn to snow for a time, mainly affecting locations at 100 m altitude or higher.

‌



"Any snow falling below this level will more likely be temporary and quickly melt. Where snow does accumulate, depths of 1-5 cm are likely; some locations above 300-400 m could see 5-15 cm.

"This may cause travel disruption on higher level routes, particularly in combination with a strong easterly wind which could also cause some localised drifting. Some accretion of ice onto infrastructure such as power lines is also a possibility. Snow will gradually turn back to rain both from the south and through the morning on Tuesday."

News.title: M62 shut westbound and air ambulance at scene with major delays
News.content:
The M62 westbound was closed between junction 21 at Milnrow Interchange and junction 20 at Thornham Interchange, with a diversion route in place

A major motorway near Manchester was closed westbound after a lorry struck the central reserve.

Emergency services, including an air ambulance, were called to the scene on the M62, which remained closed on Sunday evening between junction 21 at Milnrow Interchange (Milnrow, Shaw A640) and junction 20 at Thornham Interchange (Rochdale, Oldham A627(M)).

There were delays of up to 70 minutes in place, National Highways said, with about five miles of congestion. A statement from National Highways reads: "The M62 in Greater Manchester is closed westbound between J21 Milnrow Interchange (Milnrow, Shaw A640) and J20 Thornham Interchange (Rochdale, Oldham A627(M)).

"A lorry has struck the central reserve. Greater Manchester Police, an Air Ambulance and National Highways Traffic Officers have attended. Traffic was held eastbound. The eastbound carriageway now has 1 lane (of 3) open."

A diversion route was in place.

UK weather maps show 23 areas set for snow this week — see full list

News.title: Iran's horror war threat to target US military bases in Europe with five in UK
News.content:
Iran's horror war threat to target US military bases in Europe with five in UK

Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary, General Mohsen Rezaei, said any US attack on Iran would see American military facilities 'particularly in European countries' targeted

View 2 Images TEHRAN, IRAN - NOVEMBER 9: (âRESTRICTIONS: NO Access Israel Media/Persian Language TV Stations Outside Iran/Strictly No Access BBC Persian/VOA Persian/Manoto TV/Iran International TVâ) Iran displays its military arsenal, including ballistic and hypersonic missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), satellite launch vehicles and air defense systems, in the capital Tehran, Iran, on November 9, 2026. The military equipment, exhibited at the Permanent Exhibition Center of the Aerospace Park affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, includes missiles with different ranges and capabilities, as well as air defense vehicles. (Photo by Fatemeh Bahrami/Anadolu via Getty Images) (Image: Getty)

Iran has warned it will target US military installations across Europe in retaliation for any American strike, heightening security concerns at major bases in the UK.

‌



‌



Delivering the stark threat this week amid escalating Middle East tensions, General Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, stated that any US attack on Iranian territory would trigger reprisals against American assets, "particularly in European countries."

‌



He cautioned Washington against making what he called a "mistake," pointing to the risk of a wider regional and international conflict, reports The Express.

‌



General Rezaei said: "If the Americans make a mistake and attack us, we will not limit ourselves to targeting nearby bases; we will also target their distant bases, particularly in European countries.

"We may target some islands that they believe our missiles cannot reach."

The warning comes just 24 hours after US commanders relocated several aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk due to a credible Iranian threat. According to flight-tracking data, nine Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers and three Ospreys were moved from the base. US reports indicate that security levels have since been raised at both RAF Mildenhall and nearby RAF Lakenheath, while the Wall Street Journal notes that American officials are still evaluating the exact nature of the threat.

‌



The United States operates 16 major Air Force facilities across Britain, with RAF Lakenheath serving as its largest hub. Located near Brandon and Lakenheath in Suffolk, the base houses F-35 and F-15E fighter squadrons and supports over 5,000 active-duty personnel alongside thousands of civilian workers and family members.

View 2 Images This photograph shows a surface-to-air missile system displayed at an exhibition of missiles and drones at the National Aerospace Park outside Tehran on November 12, 2026 (Image: Getty)

‌



In response to the aircraft relocation, Downing Street affirmed that British bases remain secure and that their protection is a "top priority." Asked about bilateral discussions concerning the safety of American military assets in the UK, the Prime Minister’s official spokesman emphasised that the US remains "one of our top security partners."

"We're in constant communication with them, sharing intelligence and accessing threats together.

Article continues below

"Aircraft and other assets move regularly according to operational requirements."

The development emerged just hours after President Donald Trump declared the war in Iran was "militarily over". During an unexpected press conference, he said: "Iran militarily is effectively over. We're just keeping it the status quo."

News.title: Girl, 7, faces life-changing treatment abroad after 22 surgeries for rare condition that left her neck purple
News.content:
Girl, 7, faces life-changing treatment abroad after 22 surgeries for rare condition that left her neck purple

Kinley Gluch, aged seven, has had dozens of surgeries and procedures for a rare vascular condition which affects her face, lip, neck, mouth and airway

View 6 Images Kinley Gluch continues to be treated for a rare vascular condition (Image: @purpleprincessvm/Cover Images)

Moments after baby Kinley Gluch was born, her parents realised something was wrong when her neck suddenly swelled and turned purple as she cried for the first time.

‌



‌



Her mother Cristen Gluch had barely had the chance to hold her when doctors rushed the newborn away. Cristen said: "I was in shock. One minute I had this beautiful healthy baby, and the next something was terribly wrong."

‌



Thankfully, Kinley's vital signs were normal but doctors had no immediate answers. Her mum added: "We were terrified when they sent us home. We had no idea how this would impact her life, or if this could potentially be fatal. There were so many fears and unknowns."

‌



6 View 6 Images The little girl has had 22 operations in seven years (Image: @purpleprincessvm/Cover Images) 6 View 6 Images Mum Cristen Gluch spoke about her brave daughter (Image: @purpleprincessvm/Cover Images)

Now seven, Kinley has undergone more than 22 surgeries and procedures for a rare vascular condition that affects her face, lip, neck, mouth and airway. Her family is preparing to travel to Italy in the hope of receiving a groundbreaking treatment they believe could finally change her future.

When Kinley was a month old, she was referred to an interventional radiologist, who diagnosed her with extensive venous malformations, abnormally formed blood vessels that lack normal muscular walls and allow blood to pool inside them.

‌



The diagnosis was overwhelming but the family hoped treatment could help. Instead, doctors soon discovered just how dangerous and unusual Kinley's condition really was.

Aged just one, Kinley underwent her first planned sclerotherapy procedure to treat her veins. During the operation doctors discovered the malformation was far larger and more complex than anyone had realised, with blood flowing rapidly towards her jugular vein.

‌



Had they proceeded with the treatment, the medication could have travelled directly towards her heart and lungs. Cristen, from Utah, said: "I will never forget the interventional radiologist coming out of surgery looking so discouraged. He was astonished by how large and high-flowing her malformation was."

6 View 6 Images Despite her continued treatment, Kinley remains a brave and happy youngster (Image: @purpleprincessvm/Cover Images) 6 View 6 Images Kinley, from Utah, has been diagnosed with extensive venous malformations (Image: @purpleprincessvm/Cover Images)

‌



Even more frightening was watching one of the country's leading specialists struggle to find answers. She added: "Seeing the expert in these malformations not know what to do was terrifying.

Traditional treatments that normally work for venous malformations were considered too dangerous because of the size of the growth and the sheer volume of blood flowing through it.

‌



Then, when Kinley was three years old, the situation became even more serious. She began developing blood clots within the malformation.

Because the abnormal veins were directly connected to her jugular vein and major blood vessels leading to her heart and lungs, doctors feared the consequences could be catastrophic.

‌



To buy time, Kinley was placed on blood-thinning injections while her medical team consulted specialists across multiple disciplines. Eventually, they reached a difficult conclusion.

The only option was an extraordinarily high-risk operation to surgically remove the large malformation from her neck. Cristen said: "The risk of her bleeding and it not being able to be stopped was significant. These malformations can bleed a lot, and Kinley's was so large and had such high-pressure blood flow running through it."

‌



Surgeons brought in a microvascular specialist to assist and even removed part of Kinley's collarbone to gain access to the malformation. Cristen continued: "They wanted everything open so that if a bleed happened, they could find it quickly."

Doctors even discussed the possibility of sacrificing Kinley's jugular vein if complications occurred. For Cristen and her husband Jordan, an electrical engineer and certified flight instructor, it was the culmination of years of uncertainty and fear.

‌



"During that eight-hour surgery, we genuinely thought we might lose her. It was the most terrifying day of our lives," said Cristen.

Thankfully, the operation was a success. Surgeons safely removed the malformation and Kinley survived with only one blood transfusion. Cristen said: "It was after that surgery that I knew our baby was going to be okay. The worst was finally behind us."

‌



View 6 Images The family hope to take little Kinley abroad for further treatment (Image: @purpleprincessvm/Cover Images)

Yet Kinley's journey is far from over. She continues to undergo treatments every few months to control the remaining venous malformations throughout her face, lip, neck, mouth and airway.

‌



She also suffers from severe obstructive sleep apnoea caused by malformations in her airway and wears a CPAP machine every night while she sleeps, to deliver a steady stream of pressurised air.

Despite everything she has endured, Kinley refuses to let her condition define her. Cristen added: "She doesn't like the extra attention and just wants to get back to being a normal kid. I've had kids ask her about her venous malformations and then tell her they think it's her superpower. Most children have been incredibly kind and accepting of Kinley."

‌



Although she sleeps with a CPAP machine every night, Kinley rarely complains. Her mum added: "Just like everything else she has faced, it's no big deal to her."

Kinley plays football every spring and autumn and is also a dedicated member of a dance team. Cristen continued: "We feel so lucky she's still able to participate in the activities she loves. She might miss a practice because of surgery, but you can usually count on seeing her right back there the next day."

‌



But, because the venous malformations on Kinley's face and neck often resemble bruising, they naturally attract attention from strangers. Cristen said: "Kinley gets a lot of attention because of her venous malformations."

Rather than becoming frustrated by the questions, Kinley has developed her own simple explanation. Her mum said: "She tells people she has extra blood vessels."

‌



One of Kinley's favourite reactions comes when people mistake the purple marks for something entirely different. Cristen laughed: "Sometimes people ask if she's been eating something blue or chewing on a marker. She just giggles and politely explains."

Kinley currently undergoes bleomycin sclerotherapy every few months in the US. Electrosclerotherapy combines the same medication with electrical pulses that help it penetrate the abnormal blood vessels far more effectively.

‌



While doctors are careful not to promise a cure, Cristen says the treatment is the closest thing currently available for children with vascular malformations.

One of the reasons the family is so hopeful is because of Lily, who was originally expected to need a second procedure. Instead, the treatment proved so successful that she is currently showing no signs of disease.

‌



Although traditional sclerotherapy has helped shrink and control Kinley's malformations, it has never been able to eliminate them completely. Doctors have warned that the abnormal blood vessels can continue to stretch over time and may worsen during puberty and other hormonal changes.

Without another solution, Kinley is expected to require ongoing procedures for years to come. The medication used in her current treatments, bleomycin, also has lifetime dosage limits because excessive exposure can carry health risks.

Article continues below

Although the family has health insurance, Kinley's extensive medical needs mean they reach their annual limit by February every year. The Italy treatment will not be covered and must be paid for entirely out of pocket. The family has launched a GoFundMe campaign to help cover the cost of Kinley's treatment in Italy. To donate, use this link.

News.title: Staggered age of consent to be discussed after Brand case, minister says
News.content:
A discussion over a staggered age of consent is to take place, the work and pensions secretary has said, as the government faces calls to change the law following the case against Russell Brand.

Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Pat McFadden said that "appalling" stories of "abuse of power by powerful men" have emerged this week.

A woman who alleges she was raped by jailed comedian Brand when she was 16 is now campaigning to see the law changed so that relationships between 16 and 17-year-olds and adults would be illegal.

Questions over a staggered age of consent have "been raised and will be discussed" McFadden said, adding: "[I] can't tell you what the conclusion of that would be, but the last week has certainly put that up in lights."

Adults of any age are legally able to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds, under UK law.

Mia Latter, who has waived her right to anonymity, told the Sunday Times that she wants the age of consent to be staggered.

Latter is one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation.

Brand denied the allegations at the time and none of the six women were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.

At Southwark Crown Court on Monday, Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half-years imprisonment after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, involving four women between 2004 and 2009. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.

Latter said she was 16 when she met the comedian, then 30. She told the Sunday Times: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power].

"I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other.

"If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to.

"But...if you're in your thirties, forties and fifties and you're trying to have a relationship with someone under the age of 18, it [should be] a criminal offence."

Latter told the Sunday Times the CPS decided not to include her as part of Brand's criminal trial but police wanted her to be part of "subsequent" proceedings.

She told the paper she was "devastated" by the decision and that police had said they didn't want the trial "to become 'the Alice show'", a reference to her pseudonym in the stories published in 2023.

It is understood the Met Police has apologised for the language officers used in a meeting with Latter about her case.

A Met spokesperson said: "This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence."

Layla Stone, founder of the campaign group Close the Consent Gap, said bringing in a staggered age of consent was about addressing a "power imbalance" in relationships involving 16 and 17 year-olds and adults. She urged ministers to commit to such a change.

Stone, a child protection social worker, told the BBC that 16 and 17 year-olds were seen as children in "every single framework of the law" and "we don't believe [they are] old enough to consent to having sex with much older adults".

Close the Consent Gap is proposing that 16 year-olds would not be able to have a sexual relationship with anyone older than 19, and that someone aged 17 would be prohibited from a relationship with anyone older than 20.

Further allegations of sexual misconduct in the entertainment industry came in the same week Brand was convicted.

ITV News and the Guardian published a story alleging that comedian David Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.

One woman said she now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault". Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.

Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour when he was a judge at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.

Walliams said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.

The Metropolitan Police said on Friday it has launched an investigation into Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences", after the ITV News and the Guardian story. The Met said that the allegations it is investigating are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian but that it was "also proactively reviewing that reporting".

Speaking to Sky News, the work and pensions secretary said: "I do think that between Russell Brand, David Walliams, what's been put out there, people are looking at these issues in a new light."

News.title: Man and woman die and four arrested after police pursuit crash in Leeds
News.content:
Two people have been killed after their car was hit by a vehicle fleeing from police in Leeds.

West Yorkshire Police said it happened at 00:44 GMT, when a blue BMW 123D failed to stop for officers in Gelderd Road and then crashed into a white Volkswagen Scirocco.

The driver of the Volkswagen, a 22-year-old man, died at the scene. His passenger, a woman, 23, died later in hospital. Both were from York.

The occupants of the BMW, a 39-year-old man from Harrogate, two boys aged 16 and 17 and a 16-year-old girl, have been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

The 39-year-old is also being held on suspicion of driving while over the prescribed limit for cannabis, the force confirmed.

The teenagers in the BMW were taken to hospital for treatment to injuries that were not considered life-threatening.

A spokesperson for West Yorkshire Police said a referral had been made to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), which confirmed it had started an investigation.

News.title: Ex-Met Police inspector lied about wife's death in Barbados hotel room, BBC learns
News.content:
An inquest in the UK later found that Rebekah's organs had been inexplicably "chopped up" into small pieces by a pathologist in Barbados.

This served no medical purpose and destroyed vital evidence, according to a UK pathologist who examined her body after it had been repatriated.

The inquest also established that key toxicology and histology tests - to look for signs of disease, injury or other changes in the body - were not conducted.

The coroner, Andrew Harris, said this raised the prospect of "deliberate concealment or obstruction of further investigation".

He also said that while bloodstains on bedclothes may be consistent with vomiting, he could not accept the cause of death determined by Barbadian authorities, aspiration pneumonitis - inflammation of the lungs - and delivered an open verdict.

He concluded that Rebekah's death likely involved intoxication and said unlawful killing could not be ruled out.

The inquest did not, however, consider Arter's alleged sexual exploitation of several other women whose cases he had investigated, to be within its scope.

Police in Barbados have previously said no marks of violence were found on Rebekah's body and there was nothing to suggest anything untoward - adding that they did not order toxicology tests because they believed she died from natural causes.

A week after Rebekah died, Arter flew back to the UK where he was arrested at Heathrow in connection with alleged sexual offences against another woman whose case he had investigated as a police officer in 2010. He was found dead in Wandsworth prison three days later.

In response to the BBC, Metropolitan Police Commander Simon Messinger said: "Our thoughts at this time remain with Rebekah Arter's family, who understandably have questions about the circumstances of her death.

"We would urge any victim survivors of rape and sexual offences - no matter how long ago a crime may have occurred - to reach out."

Elliot says his two young children will never know their grandmother.

"My daughter, my son - they're never gonna actually have any memories of her," he says.

"For the rest of my life, I'm never going to know how she's passed away."

News.title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people
News.content:
The work and pensions secretary has backed the idea that the government should legally guarantee young people help to get into employment.

Pat McFadden told the BBC that job support should be given a "legislative underpinning", adding the level of assistance on offer was currently "vague".

McFadden also confirmed that some current benefit claimants would see their current entitlement to benefits reduced when they are reassessed.

But his Conservative counterpart Helen Whately said the idea of legally guaranteeing support "doesn't make sense" and ministers should focus instead on reducing taxes paid by employers.

It comes ahead of a long-awaited review by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn, which will recommend on Tuesday that under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work.

His report is also expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales.

Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to health conditions, under the plans.

Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Milburn said the government should divert money away from the benefits system to boost work support, adding he wanted to see "billions" extra spent on help over the next decade.

However, the idea of reducing the entitlement of existing benefit claimants could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who scuppered a previous benefits-cutting plan under Sir Keir Starmer last year.

Milburn said the reduced entitlement for some should be accompanied by a new "duty on government" to provide jobs support to young people, such as apprenticeships, college places, job coaching, or a job.

He added that the temporary nature of previous job support schemes, including the Kickstart programme during the Covid pandemic, meant that they had been less effective as reducing long-term joblessness.

How the new guarantee would work in practice is not yet clear, with McFadden adding it would have to be "carefully" drafted.

Although local councils have some specific legal duties, including in the areas of child protection and homelessness, duties on central government currently tend to be much broader, such as operating a "comprehensive" health service.

News.title: Thousands of US flights still cancelled or delayed two days after grounding of planes nationwide
News.content:
Thousands of US flights were cancelled or delayed on Sunday as the US air-traffic control system continued to recover from a technical failure that led to a rare national ground stop.

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said normal operations may not be restored until Monday.

"We have airplanes and crews that are out of position, so it takes a little bit of time," he told the BBC's US partner CBS. More than 5,000 flights were delayed and 2,000 cancelled on Sunday.

President Donald Trump urged Congress on Sunday to approve more money to modernise the air-traffic control system. The grounding of all aircraft scheduled to depart the US on Friday caused chaos at airports across the country.

More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air when the FAA announced at 15:54 EST (20:54 GMT) that flights would be grounded until further notice. Some were diverted to other airports and others flew on to their destinations.

In the aftermath, 8,500 flights were delayed and another 8,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware.

The stoppage left passengers stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to their gates. Others were stranded in airports, sleeping on the floor and desperately trying to get in touch with their airline. The ground stop also had a knock-on effect on schedules around the world, with some flights out of the UK and Europe cancelled.

News.title: Trident submarine returns home after record-breaking undersea patrol
News.content:
A Royal Navy submarine carrying Trident nuclear missiles has returned to its Scottish base after a record-breaking 217 days spent submerged on patrol.

The 140-strong crew of HMS Vengeance have spent the tour in almost total isolation beneath the surface after setting out from Faslane, near Helensburgh, Argyll and Bute, on 12 April.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting was at HM Naval Base Clyde to welcome them home after the longest deployment at sea for a British vessel.

The typical patrol length for the UK's Vanguard-class ballistic missile submarines has more than doubled in recent years, with six-month durations now routine due to a shortage of seaworthy vessels.

Crew members could be seen standing on HMS Vengeance as it travelled up Gare Loch earlier, accompanied by some smaller Naval support vessels and tug boats.

The vessel was encrusted in marine growth and some of its sound-absorbing tiles were missing.

HMS Vengeance was expected back at Faslane last weekend, but that was reported to have been delayed, external when the submarine replacing it on patrol had to return to base to fix a technical fault.

The head of the navy, First Sea Lord Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, praised the dedication of submariners in keeping Nato safe at a conference last week in Oslo, but said the UK must do better at maintaining the fleet.

News.title: Tearful McIlroy dedicates record-equalling win to ill dad
News.content:
DP World Tour Championship final leaderboard

-15 Hatton (Eng); -10 McIlroy (NI); -8 Chacarra (Spa), Lindell (Fin); -7 Olesen (Den), Reitan (Nor), Laporta (Ita), Lindberg (Swe), Perez (Fra)

Selected others: -4 Wallace (Eng); -3 Rahm (Spa), Schaper (SA); Level Fleetwwod (Eng), Reed (US), Fox (NZ); +1 Rai (Eng)

Full leaderboard

Rory McIlroy wiped away tears as he dedicated his eighth Race to Dubai victory to his ill father, Gerry.

Moments after matching Colin Montgomerie's record of season-long European tour titles on Sunday, the Northern Irishman was asked about the health of his father.

An emotional McIlroy revealed Gerry has been in hospital for two months after "a huge operation" - a double lung transplant - at the end of September.

"He's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy told the DP World Tour.

"But before I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him. He said to me: 'Go win The Race to Dubai'.

"This one's for him."

It came after a thrilling climax at the traditional season-ending DP World Tour Championship with Tyrrell Hatton securing a commanding victory, while McIlroy pipped Spaniard Eugenio Chacarra to the overall crown.

Hatton's closing six-under-par 66 helped him romp to a five-shot victory on 15 under par but most eyes were on the thrilling battle that went down to the final hole.

It is the fifth successive year that McIlroy has won the award and it has drawn him level with Montgomerie, the Scot who set a mark 21 years ago that few thought would ever be matched.

"Yeah, double digits," smiled McIlroy when asked what would be his final target of Race to Dubai victories.

"I'd love to surpass Monty next year and we'll go from there."

McIlroy's confidence in going along with a target shouted out by the fans surrounding the 18th green at the Earth Course in Dubai on Sunday was refreshing to hear.

But he appears to be playing and talking with a little more freedom in recent years - the sort of freedom that comes as a result of finally completing the career Grand Slam and winning successive Masters titles - and leads to declarations of winning 10, or more.

"Winning eight Order of Merits (Race to Dubai titles) was never in my list of goals growing up," said McIlroy, who closed with a bogey-free 67 to finish on 10 under and must surely now be considered Europe's greatest golfer.

"I remember Monty being a stalwart of the European tour and playing with him at the London Club in 2008, so to pull up alongside him and win eight of these means the world to me."

News.title: Hannah Fry feels 'unbelievably lucky' after cervical cancer treatment
News.content:
Prof Hannah Fry has described feeling "unbelievably lucky" after being treated for cervical cancer.

The mathematician and BBC presenter, who recently took part in the second season of the Celebrity Traitors, said cancerous cells were discovered after she attended a cervical screening in 2020.

She underwent a hysterectomy, describing the experience to BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs as "horrific".

"As awful as that was, it had a full stop at the end of the sentence," the 42-year-old added. "I had my five-year clear the other day. I feel so unbelievably lucky."

In Sunday's episode, Fry told show host Lauren Laverne that she had delayed a cervical screening examination for months in 2020. After she attended one, the results "didn't come back for a few weeks," she said.

"Then I got a call from my GP telling me they needed me to come back and do another test, and they did a biopsy.

"I was trying hard not to panic but when they found it was in the lymphatic systemâ¦ that was when it really started to come down."

The broadcaster said she was told that her chances of survival depended on the cancerous cells not having spread to her lymph nodes, although it was not clear "how bad it was at that point".

"It's all about, basically, how far into your lymphatic system has it got. If it had not got into any lymph nodes, then the odds were in my favour and I had a really good chance of survival," she said.

Fry explained that this meant "if it was in one it would drop to a 60% chance of survival and two â the odds would go against me and it would be a 40% chance".

News.title: Schoolboy imposter subjected ex-professor and wife to 'terrifying ordeal'
News.content:
An imposter who made headlines around the world for posing as a school pupil in his 30s has appeared in court and admitted hiding in the home of his former university professor before subjecting him to a "terrifying ordeal".

Brian MacKinnon targeted Prof Brian Whiting, 87, as he lay in bed with his wife, the day after a BBC docudrama on his ruse was broadcast.

My Old School chronicled MacKinnon's return to Bearsden Academy, as Brandon Lee, a 16-year-old who had supposedly just moved to Scotland from Canada.

MacKinnon hatched the plan so he could pursue his dream of becoming a doctor having been thrown out of Glasgow University, when Prof Whiting was dean of the medical school.

News.title: Eleven officers convicted of crimes still on Police Scotland payroll, chief confirms
News.content:
Eleven officers who have been convicted of crimes - including eight who have been violent towards women and girls - are still on the Police Scotland pay roll.

In a letter, external to the Scottish Parliament's justice committee, Chief Constable Jo Farrell said there were other cases with "incontrovertible evidence" against officers, but they cannot be sacked quickly enough.

Farrell also said the Â£4.5m annual cost of the 80 officers who are currently suspended was down to "sluggish" conduct arrangements, as well as the time necessary for cases to go through courts.

She described the state of affairs as "intolerable" and called for a modernisation of the police conduct regime.

The revelation follows a number of high-profile cases of police officers who have been exposed as rapists this year alone.

Derek McNee, Campbell Petrie, Carmichael John Williamson and Cameron Ross have all been convicted and are no longer on the payroll.

Meanwhile, Alan Greer, who was named as a violent serial rapist by a BBC investigation, took his own life in May after police raided his home.

It also emerged last month that 45 serving officers are currently suspended over allegations of violence against women and girls.

News.title: Man dies after being hit by ambulance
News.content:
A man has died after being struck by an ambulance transporting a patient near Sunderland, police have said.

Northumbria Police said the crash occurred on the A19, between the junctions for the A1018 and A690, shortly after 02:00 GMT.

The ambulance was travelling on the northbound carriageway and did not have its blue lights on when it hit the man, who was in his 30s and died at the scene.

Neither the patient nor their partner who were travelling in the ambulance were injured in the collision, while the vehicle's driver, a man in his 40s, was also not hurt and remained at the scene to assist police with their inquiries.

The North East Ambulance Service (NEAS) said the patient in the ambulance and their partner were transferred to another ambulance.

Officers from Northumbria Police's roads unit have launched an investigation into the collision.

Sgt Ben Rutherford said: "Our thoughts are firmly with the family and loved ones of the man who has tragically died following this collision.

"We will continue to support them in any way that we can at this incredibly difficult time."

Anyone with CCTV or dashcam footage of the incident itself or the moments leading up to the collision has been urged to contact the force.

Rutherford said anyone with information, no matter how insignificant it may seem, "could prove key to our investigation and help provide answers for the man's loved ones".

News.title: Sea of phones at Christmas event prompts backlash
News.content:
When BBC London uploaded a video, external of the Carnaby Street Christmas lights being switched on last week, the comments section filled with thousands of people reacting to what they saw.

But, it wasn't the bright lights or the pretty fireworks that they were reacting to, it was the sea of spectators filming on their phones.

"Remember when we used to look at stuff directly with our eyes? Those were the good old days," said one comment. Another simply said: "It's such a sad sad sight."

Former EastEnders actress Natalie Cassidy commented: "Why is this piece not mentioning the fact that no-one is looking through their eyes at this beautiful display? It's really scary and depressing."

Many of the comments questioned why people would film the fireworks rather than watch them in real life, with one saying: "Nice to see everyone living in the moment, there's a 90% chance they will never watch the video again too."

News.title: What happened after a small town introduced a balaclava ban
News.content:
National headlines were made this autumn when Nottingham became one of the UK's first cities to bring in a balaclava ban, with neighbouring towns and cities now looking to follow suit.

Since September, authorities in the city have had the power to request face coverings are removed and to issue fines if they "reasonably believe" they are being used to cause trouble - although to date, no fines have been handed out in Nottingham.

But 12 miles (19km) away, one small town in Derbyshire has been quietly pioneering a ban for more than two years.

Heanor, a market town with a population of more than 24,000, took action after an increase in reports of anti-social behaviour.

As in Nottingham, Heanor's balaclava ban is part of a modified public spaces protection order (PSPO), which was drawn up in the face of rising problems of anti-social behaviour in early 2024.

It allows police and community protection officers to ask people to remove face coverings if worn in an attempt to conceal their identity to cause harassment, alarm or distress.

This includes scarves, masks, and balaclavas, but not coverings worn for religious or cultural purposes.

Amber Valley Borough Council, the authority responsible for Heanor, said concerns had been raised at the time over "group-related anti-social behaviour", which included people wearing face coverings" in a way that was causing alarm among residents and visitors".

Other incidents included reports of eggs being thrown at members of the public, along with "reckless" and intimidating behaviour on bikes and scooters.

PSPOs are not uncommon. So much so, they largely follow a template when introduced - no begging, no drinking, no urinating and defecating in the street, among other measures.

But in Heanor, Derbyshire Police's beat officers brought a wishlist of ways to amend the order.

These included restrictions on cycling, skateboarding and scootering in the PSPO area, playing "unreasonably loud" music, gathering in groups, and face coverings.

"We said these are what we would like to put forward as conditions, what do your legal team say about it?" PC Levi Tabbron said.

"And to our disbelief, they actually got approved."

News.title: Man in life-threatening state after shop robbery
News.content:
A jewellery store employee is in a life-threatening condition after a robbery in broad daylight at a shop in Peterborough.

Cambridgeshire Police said six men raided Lala Jewellers on Gladstone Street at about 11:50 GMT on Saturday.

A senior councillor later said it was believed that the victim had been stabbed, external.

The city's MP described it as a "horrific and violent act", while police have appealed for witnesses to come forward.

They said shelves were emptied and two employees behind the counter were assaulted, before the thieves fled in separate vehicles.

Two of the robbers were wearing white, traditional Pakistani clothing, officers added.

One employee, a 50-year-old man, suffered serious injuries and was taken to hospital, where he remains in a life-threatening condition.

News.title: Banton hits century and bowlers sparkle for England to level ODI series against Australia
News.content:
Second one-day international, Adelaide

England 355-6 (50 overs): Banton 121, Cox 67, Root 62

Australia 220 all out (44.3 overs): Green 64, Renshaw 63; Atkinson 4-28

England won by 135 runs; series level at 1-1

Scorecard

Tom Banton scored a century and Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson impressed with the ball as England's wildly inconsistent one-day team hammered Australia to set up a series decider.

Banton scored a fine 121 â pushing his case for selection further with a second ODI hundred â in England's 355-6.

After being knocked over for 131 two days ago in Perth, England's total was their highest in one-day internationals in Australia.

And then their bowlers, who failed to defend 430 against Sri Lanka last month and were undone by an improbable last-wicket partnership against Pakistan, reduced Australia to 29-4 inside seven overs and easily closed out a 135-run victory.

The win ends a seven-match losing run against Australia across formats in Adelaide - and a run of six consecutive defeats by Australia in 50-over cricket away from home.

But, more significantly, it corrects their course after those damaging defeats against Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Australia and offers positives amid the frustrations going into the decider on Wednesday (03:30 GMT) in Hobart.

News.title: Milder day in store before more cold health alerts take effect
News.content:
Another round of cold health alerts is set to come into force on Sunday following a brief break from the weekend's subzero temperatures.

After readings dipped as low as minus 7C early on Saturday, most places on Sunday morning were milder and free of frost.

Widespread rainfall will put a dampener on any outdoor plans, however, with hail and thunderstorms possible for parts of Wales and southern England.

Into the new week, the wintry chill is set to return with UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) cold-health alerts beginning for the north-east and north-west of England and Yorkshire and the Humber from 21:00 GMT on Sunday.
