News.title: Russell Brand’s wife shares message from disgraced comedian in prison
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Disgraced comedian Russell Brand has issued his first message from behind bars after being jailed for 10 and a half years for rape and sexual assault.

Laura Gallacher, Brand’s wife, shared a message after the 51-year-old served the first week of his prison sentence. He was found guilty earlier this month of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others during his career.

Earlier this year Brand and Gallacher began releasing a weekly YouTube podcast called Sunday Service, which they carried on recording throughout his trial.

On Sunday, Gallacher released another episode which began with her reading a passage from Brand’s bible.

open image in gallery Russell Brand outside Southwark Crown Court (James Manning/PA) ( PA Wire )

The 39-year-old, who is the daughter of Ryder Cup winning golfer Bernard Gallacher, said during the episode: “Russell has asked me to read something to you.”

Reading the message from a notebook, she went on: “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support.

“As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.

“The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do.

“I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey, little as in small, and hey as in hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe.

“The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated.

open image in gallery Russell Brand and his wife Laura Gallacher outside Southwark Crown Court (Jonathan Brady/PA) ( PA Wire )

“And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone.

“I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us.”

Gallacher choked up as she said: “Please support my treasured wife and family. I feel your prayers, your brother in Christ. Russell.”

She began the episode by saying she is here to “continue the good work that was being established here in this Sunday service community, something very, very close to mine and Russell’s heart”.

“It may look different, but the ambitions are very much the same, and we trust God, and we trust his plan, and we trust everything he’s doing right now,” she added.

open image in gallery Court artist drawing of Russell Brand in the dock at Southwark Crown Court (Elizabeth Cook/PA) ( PA Wire )

“Even though it’s painful, and obviously, will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me, but I want to continue, and I’m grateful for the support.”

Gallacher said she is speaking to her husband, adding: “He’s okay, and he’s praying.”

According to The Sun on Sunday, Brand was moved out of HMP Wandsworth and transported to the category C prison HMP Littlehey on Friday.

The prison offers a large variety of extra-curricular activities for its inmates, including yoga, choir and indoor bowls.

Brand was sentenced to a 10-and-a-half-year prison term on Monday afternoon.

He is expected to serve two-thirds of his prison sentence before being released on licence.

He will be on the sex offenders’ register for life.

News.title: Man arrested for allegedly posing as decorated combat veteran to steal $80k
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A New York man has been arrested for posing as a decorated and wounded combat veteran to steal more than $80,000 from the veterans’ organization where he worked, according to prosecutors.

David Agtsteribbe, a 58-year-old from Hampton Bays on Long Island, is accused of Grand Larceny, Criminal Possession of a Forged Instrument and several other charges for funneling money from a local American Legion into his personal bank account to pay for bills, clothes, travel and Amazon purchases, Suffolk County District Attorney Raymond A. Tierney announced earlier this week.

“Our veterans earned their honors through sacrifice and service. This defendant allegedly exploited those sacrifices for his own selfish gain. It is a shameful abuse of trust, and one that we will prosecute,” Tierney said in a statement.

Agtsteribbe enlisted in the Army in 1986, but a year later, he was court-martialed and pleaded guilty to stealing money from another soldier. He left the Army in 1988 after receiving a bad-conduct discharge.

open image in gallery David Agtsteribbe, a 58-year-old from Hampton Bays, New York, has been arrested for posing as a decorated and wounded combat veteran to steal more than $80,000 from the veterans’ organization where he worked, according to prosecutors ( Suffolk County Police Department )

In 2021, Agtsteribbe became the Hampton Bays American Legion’s finance officer by using fake military credentials, including a wounded-in-combat designation and a Purple Heart award given to soldiers who are injured or killed in action, according to prosecutors.

The American Legion does not allow veterans with a bad-conduct discharge to join, but Agtsteribbe claimed to have been honorably discharged.

From September 2022 to this past August, Agtsteribbe stole nearly $81,800 to pay his personal expenses, according to prosecutors.

Agtsteribbe was arrested Monday and ordered during his arraignment Tuesday to remain in custody as his case plays out. He faces 25 years to life in prison if convicted on the top count of Grand Larceny in the Second Degree.

open image in gallery ‘Our veterans earned their honors through sacrifice and service. This defendant allegedly exploited those sacrifices for his own selfish gain,’ Suffolk County District Attorney Raymond A. Tierney said ( AFP via Getty Images )

Agtsteribbe, who had already been in jail twice for grand larceny, pleaded not guilty to the new charges Tuesday, NBC New York reported.

Bill Coderre, Suffolk County’s American Legion commander, said it was “a case of stolen valor” and a “serious breach of our trust” in a statement shared by the outlet.

"It's bad theft. Especially for people who need it, and there’s a lot of people who do need it, especially vets,” veteran Rodney Smith told CBS News New York.

Simone Scotto, who owns Scotto's Pizza in Hampton Bays, told the outlet, "I feel bad for the American Legion of Hampton Bays because they do a lot of things for the community.”

The Independent has reached out to the Hampton Bays American Legion for comment.

News.title: Sean Duffy refuses to apologize for nationwide travel nightmare — but he’s happy to point fingers
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Travelers who were ensnared in the national ground stoppage that upended air travel throughout the country this weekend better not hold their breath for an apology from President Donald Trump’s transportation secretary — because he refuses to offer one.

Sean Duffy was on Sunday’s Meet the Press, where he talked about the air travel nightmare that began Friday, and he made it clear a mea culpa was not in the cards.

“It happened on my watch, but we have to be clear: I am moving at an incredible speed that no one has done at the FAA or in decades, and I’m proud of the work we’re doing, the attention we’re bringing to this issue,” Duffy told the NBC News show. “But I can’t apologize for what was passed off to us, and I can’t blame Republicans or Democrats because it’s all of them.”

Duffy followed in the footsteps of Trump, who broke his silence over the debacle on Sunday via Truth Social, blaming one of his favorite targets: former President Joe Biden.

“The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” he said.

open image in gallery Duffy also said he ‘can’t cancel’ using L3Harris, the contractor blamed for the Federal Aviation Administration’s outage, because it owns the network that operates communications for the FAA ( Reuters )

The president added, “We have the knowledge and plan for the Flight Control Systems, we need Congress to give the money, FAST! Our FAA is doing a great job, and is ready to go.”

The secretary expanded that blame scope and said the mess was “30 years of a lack of investment,” from the previous administrations, adding, “Why they didn’t do that I don’t know, but they gave me a system that needs to be fixed, and President [Donald] Trump and I are going to fix it.”

Duffy also said he “can’t cancel” using L3Harris, the contractor blamed for the FAA outage, because it owns the network that operates communications for the FAA.

“Which is why I’m asking for billions of dollars from Congress to build a brand-new architecture of a network, by the best companies in the world including AT&T, Verizon and [Lumen Technologies],” he added.

More than 9,000 flights were delayed Friday, which resulted in more than 6,000 cancellations on Saturday.

News.title: 32 Americans named as Rhodes scholars have variety of interests, from space junk to art history
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A college senior who wants to clean up debris pollution in Earth's orbit and a student who has researched AI use in healthcare are among the 32 Americans named as 2027 Rhodes scholars.

The winners, who were announced on Saturday, have a variety of interests, from bioelectronics to water scarcity to art history. They were chosen from 238 finalists who emerged from more than 1,000 candidates who received formal endorsements from their colleges and universities for the honor.

The students will attend the University of Oxford in England as part of the Rhodes scholar program, which awards more than 100 scholarships worldwide each year for students to pursue two to three years of graduate studies.

Two students are the first-ever Rhodes scholars from their schools — Prairie View A&M University in Texas and The Citadel — The Military College of South Carolina. Harvard University led the way with four 2027 Rhodes scholars, followed by Yale and Princeton with three each.

The winners include:

Evan Garrison, of Webb City, Missouri, a senior at Mississippi State University majoring in aerospace engineering and mathematics. His research includes designing ways to detect objects in space, with an interest in cleaning up orbital debris known as “space junk.” He plans to study mathematical modeling, scientific computing and global governance and diplomacy at Oxford.

Asuka Koda, of New York City, a senior at Yale University majoring in mathematics and philosophy. She has researched AI adoption in healthcare and has been a health and science writer for CNN. She plans to study social science of the internet and international health and tropical medicine at Oxford.

Michael Bueker, from Wellesley, Massachusetts, a senior at Dartmouth College majoring in biomedical engineering. His research has focused on biodegradable, implantable neural stimulators and other ultrathin bioelectronic devices. He also grows giant pumpkins. At Oxford, he intends to study engineering science.

Elizabeth Koenck, of Aurora, Colorado, a senior at Georgetown University majoring in foreign service. Her research has examined water scarcity problems across the Middle East, North Africa and the Colorado River Basin. She plans to pursue degrees in migration studies and water science, policy and management at Oxford.

Sabrina Soriano, of Azusa, California, a senior at Yale University majoring in art history. Her research includes 19th-century French painting, with a focus on the relationship between art, religion and cultural identity. She plans to study history of art and visual culture and visual, material and museum anthropology at Oxford.

Named after British imperialist and benefactor Cecil John Rhodes, the scholarships were established at Oxford in 1903. The program has more than 8,000 alumni, many of whom have pursued careers in government, education, the arts and social justice.

News.title: Seventh couple eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing after judge brands routine ‘plonky’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Will Best and professional partner Dianne Buswell have been eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing, narrowly missing out on a place in Blackpool week.

The 41-year-old Big Brother presenter and Buswell, 37, repeated their paso doble to Smalltown Boy by Bronski Beat on Sunday, having scored 27 during Saturday's live broadcast.

They had been left at the bottom of the judges’ leaderboard alongside Graeme Hall and Lauren Oakley, as well as Lacey Turner and Vito Coppola, before the public votes were tallied.

Best and Buswell found themselves in the dance-off against actress Jaime Winstone and Carlos Gu, who held third place on the leaderboard after scoring 33 for their Charleston to Catherine Zeta-Jones’s “I Can’t Do It Alone”.

Judge Motsi Mabuse, Craig Revel Horwood and head judge Shirley Ballas voted to save Winstone and Gu, sending them through to Blackpool, while Anton Du Beke cast his vote for Best and Buswell.

Best was told by Ballas on Saturday’s live show that he was one of the programme’s “most consistent” dancers.

Will Best and Dianne Buswell repeated their paso doble to Smalltown Boy by Bronski Beat on Sunday’s results show after scoring 27 on Saturday’s live show ( PA )

However, Revel Horwood called the routine “plonky”.

The professional dancers performed a romantasy-inspired group number on Sunday’s results show, which featured the voice of The Traitors US host Alan Cumming.

Celebrity Traitors winner Sebastian “Bash” Croft performed his new single, “Everything Always Now”, accompanied by a routine from dancers Julian Caillon and Jowita Przystal.

Best has presented shows for Channel 4, ITV and the BBC and in 2023 began co-hosting the ITV revival of Big Brother alongside AJ Odudu, herself a Strictly contestant in 2021. They hosted a Celebrity Big Brother spin-off in 2024.

He is also a presenter on Hits Radio and last month became a father to Sonny with his partner Tobi Rose.

Best and Buswell will join Ellie Taylor on Strictly – It Takes Two on Monday at 6.30pm on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer.

Strictly Come Dancing continues with is Blackpool Tower Ballroom special on Saturday at 6.35pm on BBC One.

News.title: I’m A Celebrity stars forced to drink blended fish eye cocktails in ITV series opener
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Contestants on the new series of I’m A Celebrity…Get Me Out Of Here! are forced to consume fermented prawns and blended fish eye cocktails before even reaching camp in the opening episode.

Hosted by Anthony McPartlin and Declan Donnelly, the ITV1 reality show features a group of famous figures competing in trials to secure food while living in the Australian jungle, returning to screens on Monday.

This year's line-up features former footballer Wayne Rooney, actress Joanna Page, model Leomie Anderson, Kaiser Chiefs singer Ricky Wilson, Paralympian and TV presenter Ade Adepitan, YouTuber and content creator Sharky, TV presenter AJ Odudu, and comedian Jack Skipper.

They are joined by TV personality and radio DJ Chloe Burrows, soap actor Claire Sweeney, and broadcaster Mariella Frostrup.

The launching episode begins with Gavin and Stacey star Page travelling through the Australian wilderness in a buggy before meeting up with Wilson and Sharky, who remarks that he has "just been in the car from hell".

Sweeney and Anderson subsequently join them shortly before hosts Ant and Dec make their entrance.

open image in gallery Coronation Street star Claire Sweeney, 55, who rose to fame on Brookside and has appeared on stage extensively ( ITV )

Addressing the group, Dec says: "The niceties end here, because from this moment on you’re all in direct competition with one another. You’re about to face a challenge where there will be serious consequences for the loser."

Ant then informs them: “This truck is about to become your worst nightmare, because one at a time, you each have to scale it, scramble around the outside of it, whilst locating and igniting three flares, all whilst going around these tracks at speed. If you complete it you’ll win a meal for camp tonight.”

Meanwhile, over on the Gold Coast, the remaining six celebrities kick off the experience – some with buggy rides down the beach, while Rooney hovers above in a helicopter before undertaking a skydive.

Visibly shaking in the helicopter, Rooney says: “Of my whole career, this is probably my most vulnerable…out of the whole show this is my biggest fear.”

Adepitan, who is a wheelchair user, then explains his attitude going into the series: “My everyday life I live out of my comfort zone, why is the jungle going to be any harder? I’ll give it everything I’ve got.”

After he also skydives, he kisses the ground and declares: “That’s for my son.”

open image in gallery Two years after his wife Coleen came second on I’m a Celebrity , footballer and pundit Wayne Rooney, 41, is following in her footsteps ( ITV )

The six celebrities all then meet up in a rooftop bar at a luxury hotel – and are given their own challenge.

Waiters are summoned who are carrying trays of huge cocktails, which are revealed to be “prawn-star martinis”, made of fermented prawns and blended fish eyes served in a gigantic fish bowl glass.

Ant explains: “At the bottom of each glass is a different safe word, you have to drain your glass using your straw to suck out the fluid and spit it into the bucket next to the glass.”

Last year’s season was won by social media star AngryGinge, real name Morgan Burtwistle.

I’m A Celebrity…Get Me Out Of Here! starts on Monday at 9pm on ITV1, STV and ITVX.

Spin-off show Unpacked will air nightly after the main show on ITV2, STV and ITVX, presented by Sam Thompson and Kemi Rodgers.

News.title: Scotland’s ugly win seals weekend of domination for northern hemisphere
News.content:
This was far from pretty. In fact it was downright ugly. If Wales’s historic win over New Zealand on Saturday will be spoken of for generations, this turgid 15-12 victory for Scotland over Australia had probably been forgotten, even by the 65,095 who witnessed it, by the time they caught the tram home. But it capped a spectacular weekend for northern hemisphere rugby.

One should never read too much into results one year out from a World Cup; different conditions, home advantage, different stages in teams’ development cycles, and so on. But it was difficult not to feel at least some encouragement from a weekend in which France ended a five-match losing streak against world champions South Africa in one of the most thrilling Test matches of recent times, Wales ended their All Blacks hoodoo with an epic display of defensive resolve, and Scotland won a grim arm-wrestle against Australia. With England and Ireland thrashing Japan and Fiji respectively, only Italy’s loss in a tight one against Argentina prevented a clean sweep.

It will be interesting to see how the southern hemisphere responds over the next couple of weekends, but you have to say, this new Nations Championship format has breathed a bit of life into the global game. Even if it was in very short supply at Murrayfield on Sunday.

After the barnstorming games in Paris and Cardiff, expectations were high heading into the match, but it proved to be a messy, attritional affair, not helped by a greasy pitch and two teams absolutely desperate for a win. First-half tries from Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey put Scotland 12-5 up at half-time, with Harry Potter having replied for the visitors.

News.title: Record-breaking England hammer Australia to force series decider
News.content:
Good morning from Adelaide Oval. For England fans waking up back home, things are a going a little better now than they were in Perth 48 hours ago.

Having been asked to bat first again, they are 102 for one after 18 overs, and going nicely. Tom Banton has made a fine fifty, while Joe Root is doing what he does. You know the drill: look up and he’s on 30, and so on.

The man to go was Ben Duckett, whose tough times in Australia continued, when he picked out a fielder in the offside ring for nine. The ball was short and wide, and the stroke pretty ugly. Anyway, without him, England have managed to build a bit of a platform. The pitch is classic Adelaide, lacking the pace and bounce of Friday in Perth, and it helps that Australia have left out their new find, Mahli Beardman, who is being “managed”.

Naturally, there is also still a lot of chat about sandpaper. David Warner was supposed to be here for Fox but is not, having attended to a family commitment in Sydney last night, according to the station.

More significant, though, was the intervention of Chadd Sayers, a one-cap seamer who was on the sandpaper tour. He is commentating for SEN and has backed Khawaja up strongly. He believes all players knew that sandpaper was being used in two Tests and says there was a 60-90 minute meeting involving all players about taking collective responsibility. Cummins said the opposite.

News.title: Ireland stay in hunt for final place despite complacent display
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Nations Championship fifth-round Test between Ireland and Fiji at Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

Ireland are third in the Northern Hemisphere standings, having played a game less than England and France above them, but a point bonus victory this evening would put Andy Farrell’s side level with Steve Borthwick’s men and keep them in the mix for top spot. Meanwhile, Fiji are rock bottom of the South Hemisphere table, with a miserable points difference of -133, and lost 54-17 to France last time out.

Tadhg Beirne, who is poised to captain his country for the first time on home soil this evening, said Ireland are aiming to carry on the positive momentum following their 42-12 win over Argentina eight days ago, but feels his side can still improve. “The big focus for us is to continue building on our performance, particularly from last week,” he remarked.

“We laid down a foundation of how we want to play, but we’re certainly not satisfied with that. I think there were patches of us playing really well there, but there were also patches where we weren’t to the standard that we’re going to hold ourselves to.”

News.title: Botham’s grandson inspires Wales to historic win over All Blacks
News.content:
The second half of Wales’ Nations Championship started with a hard-fought 28-21 bonus point victory over Japan last Saturday. Steve Tandy’s side sit fifth in the Northern Hemisphere table, but just five points separate them from second-place England, and they still have a tonne of pride to play for as they aim to finish as high as possible in the group.

Speaking ahead of the encounter, Tandy said: “We’re excited for the opportunity we have against New Zealand. It was good to get the win last Saturday, but some elements of our execution weren’t where we wanted.

“We have to go up another level this weekend and be more ruthless. We have one of the best teams in the world coming. We want to be better and put in an 80-minute performance.”

Meanwhile, New Zealand arrive in the Welsh capital in imperious form, having won their opening four Nations Championship matches and boasting a +73 points difference. South Africa’s defeat has opened the door for the resurgent All Blacks to pounce, and they’ll be brimming with confidence following their eye-catching 43-21 triumph against Scotland at Murrayfield a week ago.

As for the team news, Tandy has made four alterations to the starting XV that overcame Japan. Taine Basham is poised for his first international appearance since the 2024 Six Nations, while James Botham, Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Adam Beard also begin the contest. The influential Aaron Wainwright is out with a minor calf problem.

All Blacks Head Coach has ordered 10 changes to the 23-man squad that brushed Scotland aside. Forwards including George Bower, Asafo Aumua, Josh Lord, Anton Segner and backs such as Richie Mo’unga, Anton Lienert-Brown and Fehi Fineanganofo all start for the heavily rotated visitors. Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time, in his 149th Test, while Will Jordan is unavailable because of a hamstring issue.

Kick-off is at 14:10, with team news following now.

News.title: Joseph a star in the making as England revel in role of bullies
News.content:
England have made wholesale changes, with only five members from the starting XV against Australia remaining. Henry Pollock starts at eight, Will Joseph earns just his second cap on the wing and Archie McParland is set for his international debut off the bench.

“Japan are a very well-coached side who will challenge us in different ways, and we know we will need to bring intensity throughout the game,” said Borthwick. “The atmosphere at Allianz Stadium last week was incredible. The players really fed off the energy in the stadium, and we are really looking forward to being back on Saturday [today].”

Japan’s first game of this month’s fixtures ended in defeat as they lost 28-21 against Wales in Cardiff last weekend. That defeat means they have just one win from their first four games of the Nations Championship, which came against Italy in the opening game, and they sit second bottom in the southern hemisphere standings.

“We have had really good training to prepare us for the game we are expecting against England,” Jones said. “We had two days of very settled and pretty training but Wednesday was quite dirty. We had to adapt to certain situations and in the end we did it really well. I was really pleased with the players, really pleased with their effort, really pleased with the way they adapted to the situations. I am looking forward to going to Twickenham with this young Japanese team that is going to play the house down.”

Kick-off from Allianz Stadium is at 4.40pm.

News.title: France pull off one of their greatest wins as Erasmus mind games backfire
News.content:
Given Les Bleus’ injuries, only the 1999 World Cup semi-final victory over New Zealand can come close to this win over the back-to-back world champions, South Africa. The Nations Championship, with the Springboks previously unbeaten, has been blown wide open. Crikey, given these two could meet in a World Cup semi-final next year, rugby’s blue-riband event in Australia has been blown wide open.

And how lucky are we. France did not score a point in the second half and South Africa’s comeback befitted a champion side, but these audacious hosts regaled their Parisian audience with a rugby feast. Rassie Erasmus, the Springboks’ head coach, said that he was nervous before the game and so he should have been. Fabien Galthié, his counterpart, had promised some fun and games, but Erasmus could not help himself: not long before kick-off, he pulled the coup de théâtre, switching his starting and replacement front rows. Time will tell whether such a move was legal.

“We didn’t play well,” said Erasmus. “I can’t find a lot of excuses. They were on top of their game and we were a little bit off. It was one point here and there. They took their opportunities and we didn’t. We weren’t just outplayed, we were outsmarted.”

“I think we’ve killed our dreams for the Nations Championship with this result,” he added, suggesting he thinks New Zealand will beat England next week.

Demons were present for both sides, mainly France. South Africa lost Jasper Wiese to a 20-minute red card for a nasty ruck clear-out – just as Lood de Jager had received in the visitors’ win last year – and, at the end, there was a reverse of that utterly compelling World Cup quarter-final on the same turf. This time, it was South Africa desperately searching for victory, having dominated the scrum and scoring all three of their tries from close range or mauls.

News.title: England’s batting capitulates in defeat to lift Australia’s spirits
News.content:
“We weren’t quick enough to adapt to the conditions, we talked extensively leading into the game about the surface here at Optus,” Brendon McCullum, England’s coach, said. “It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline, there are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away.”

McCullum called for his team to scrap a bit more, and at least acknowledged this time that driving on the up was unwise.

“KP has got such a nice manner about him,” he said. “He sees his role to get the talent to perform on the world stage. His message will be measured but firm – adapting to conditions, what could we have done, trying to drive the ball on the up is not wise. Next time we hit a surface like this we have to try and work it better.”

After a quiet start, both openers fell tamely. Ben Duckett prodded Johnson to point, then Banton had a booming drive at Bartlett and was caught behind.

Enter Beardman. When he came on to bowl the 10th over of the innings, there was palpable excitement from his home crowd, who had watched another West Australian, Mike Hussey, present his ODI cap before the toss. Later in the day, Hussey was probably glad he rebuffed England’s recent approach to work with their Test batsmen.

Beardman, who is a mentee of Dennis Lillee and has a gorgeously rhythmical action that helped him touch 90mph, started with a maiden to Root, then found just another movement away from Brook to invite the edge. On the occasion of his 200th ODI, Root had been dropped badly on three off Bartlett, and his only boundary came when Beardman found his an inside edge and the ball flew past his stumps.

The pressure told, and Root edged a big drive behind, where Josh Inglis took the third of his five catches. That sparked a collapse of five for 10, with Jordan Cox edging behind prodding in defence, before Curran was caught on the fence hooking for nought. Beardman’s five-fer was completed when Liam Dawson – selected ahead of Adil Rashid again – skewed a flat-footed drive to backward point. Overton followed in the next over, leaving England 65 for eight, with their lowest ever ODI score, 86, inevitably recorded against Australia in 2001, appearing a distant possibility.

A stand of 37 from Will Jacks and Gus Atkinson averted that particular indignity, and the fear of being bowled out for double figures. But the total was never enough and, despite Atkinson bowling Head first ball, the chase was painfully routine thanks to Marsh’s early barrage.

News.title: Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

Sports.content:
Next

LAMINE YAMAL was handed a brutal reminder of his Ballon d’Or snub by England fans.

The Spanish sensation is taking on Harry Kane‘s Three Lions in Madrid and won an early free-kick after drawing a foul from Declan Rice.



Arsenal star Rice was shown a yellow card, but it was golden orbs on the mind of visiting supporters after their captain was named the best player on the planet.

Chants of ‘Harry Kane, the best in the world’ and ‘where’s your Ballon d’Or‘ rang out around the Wanda Metropolitano.



One viewer noted: “The Spain vs. England match is really a showdown between Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane to prove who deserved the Ballon d’Or.”

Kane missed a free header at the back post from Rice’s corner as England started brightly.

But he was at his clinical best as his won and converted a penalty to put his side ahead just before the break.

It was an eighth goal in just six Nations League outings.

Before the game, Rice predicted that Yamal would get his hands on multiple Ballons d’Or, but backed his pal.

He said: “For me and for everyone in England, Harry deserved the Ballon d’Or.”

Sports.title: Why is Martin Zubimendi wearing a mask against England?
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND are taking on Spain tonight in a huge Nations League clash.

La Roja midfielder Martin Zubimendi is wearing a protective mask against the Three Lions.



SPAIN VS ENGLAND LIVE COVERAGE

The World Cup winners hold a perfect record in the competition and sit top of Group C.



However, Thomas Tuchel‘s side can leapfrog the Spaniards if they win tonight in Madrid.

Why is Martin Zubimendi wearing a mask against England?

Martin Zubimendi is wearing a face mask because he broke his nose in Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton on October 24.



The Spaniard came on as a substitute in the comfortable Gunners’ victory.

Zubimendi, 27, appeared to be caught in the face by Toffees striker Thierno Barry when challenging for the ball.

The Spaniard was forced to come off for treatment as blood was pouring from his nose.

He was able to finish the game, but only by having tissue shoved up his right nostril.



Zubimendi’s nose is understood to be broken and it means he will require a protective mask to play.

He has made only three starts this season against Ipswich and Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup, plus Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

The midfielder was a regular for Arsenal last season, but has been knocked down the pecking order by summer signing Bruno Guimaraes.



The form of Myles Lewis-Skelly has also limited his minutes and he will be eager to play tonight.

Zubimendi has had rotten luck with injuries this term and earlier this month picked up an ankle knock during the warm-down after a 2-1 win over Leeds.

Sports.title: Why do Spain not sing their national anthem?
Sports.content:
Next

SPAIN face England in the Nations League tonight – but fans have noticed something strange when the national anthem plays.

Unlike almost every other nation at the tournament, none of the players sing along to the music. Here’s everything we know about why.



Why does Spain’s national anthem have no official lyrics?

The Marcha Real (Royal March) is one of just four national anthems in the world with no official lyrics, alongside those of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo and San Marino.

It dates back to 1761, when it was composed by Manuel de Espinosa de los Monteros and documented in a book of military calls for the Spanish infantry, where it appeared under the title Marcha Granadera.



It was adopted as a state anthem in 1770, and later became the national anthem during Queen Isabella II’s reign (1833-68).

Has the Spanish national anthem ever had lyrics?

The anthem briefly had competition during Spain’s Second Republic between 1930 and 1939, when the Himno de Riego was used instead.



After taking power in 1939, General Francisco Franco reinstated the Marcha Real, this time with updated lyrics by the poet Jose Maria Peman, celebrating the “rebirth” of Spain under his rule.

Those lyrics were dropped not long after the dictator died in 1975, and the anthem has remained wordless ever since.

Attempts to bring back official lyrics have repeatedly failed.

In 2007, the Spanish Olympic Committee ran a public competition and selected a winning entry from over 7,000 entries.



But it was scrapped within days following a public backlash to the proposed lyrics, which opened with “Viva Espana”.

What do Spain’s players and fans do during the anthem?

With no words to sing, Spain’s players simply stand in silence as the anthem plays.

Supporters in the stands sometimes hum or sing “lo lo lo” along to the melody.

The lack of lyrics has occasionally sparked confusion among fans unfamiliar with the anthem.

Some viewers have even mistakenly accused Spanish footballers of disrespecting their own country.



Spain have impressed on their way to the last four, building on their Euro 2024 triumph, where they beat England in the final.

When is the Nations League quarter-final draw?

The Nations League quarter-final draw will take place on Friday, November 20 at 11am GMT, following the conclusion of the group stage.

Fans can live stream the show on Uefa TV.

The draw will be conducted at Uefa‘s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

In addition to the quarter-final draw, the draw for the League A/B and League B/C promotion and relegation play-offs will also take place.



When will the Nations League quarter-finals take place?

The quarter-finals will be two-legged ties, with the first match on March 25-27 and the return leg on March 28-30.

The four nations that are victorious will then progress to the Nations League Finals.

The semi-finals, third-place play-off and final are scheduled for June 9-13 2027.

The Three Lions claimed their fourth win from five in the competition on Thursday night, beating Croatia 2-1.



Harry Kane marked his record 126th appearance for his country by scoring the winner from the penalty spot.

The win confirmed England‘s qualification to the quarter-finals ahead of a tough trip to Madrid.

Who can England face in Nations League quarter-finals?

Although England have already booked their spot in the Nations League quarter-finals, their final position in Group A3 could still change.



Thomas Tuchel’s men need to beat Spain on foreign soil to win the group, as that would level the points tallies and head-to-head between the two nations.

If the Three Lions are victorious, they would go to the summit, as they have a superior goal difference.

Sports.title: Why are England and Spain wearing black armbands in Nations League clash?
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND head to Spain tonight for the final group stage game of the Nations League!

Both sides will observe a minute’s silence before the game in Madrid and will wear black armbands.



SPAIN VS ENGLAND LIVE COVERAGE

They last met in the opening match of group C, where the World Cup winners emerged victorious in a thrilling clash at Wembley.



Lamine Yamal scored inside two minutes before Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put the Three Lions ahead before the break.

However, Alex Baena scored to level the match before Mikel Oyarzabal -who scored the winning goal in the Euro 2024 final – came back to haunt England and netted the winner at Wembley.



Now, they face off in the final match of the group stage with top spot on the line.

Why are England and Spain wearing black armbands in Nations League clash?

England and Spain players will honour the life of tragic footballer Jesus de Miguel when they face each other tonight.

Both teams will wear black armbands during their Nations League clash.

While there will be a minute’s silence held before kick-off at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium.



It is to pay tribute to both late Tenerife striker De Miguel and the victims of October’s Madrid train crash, which claimed the lives of at least 68 people.

De Miguel lost his life at just 30 following an on-pitch collision with an opposition goalkeeper during a match against FC Andorra earlier this month.

He was struck with a heavy blow to the head and chest area while contending a 50-50, and later died in hospital.

It plunged the football world into mourning and it is set to be an emotional stadium later when his memory, along with those who were killed in the train crash, will be honoured.

England face Spain in their capital at 8pm UK time, with Thomas Tuchel’s side needing a win to top Group 3A.



Before kick-off, Spain will also present their World Cup trophy to the crowd, along with the Fifa Under-15 World Cup which La Roja also won this year.

Sports.title: Arsenal's wait for home WSL win goes on after Earps masterclass
Sports.content:
Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win continues as they drew 1-1 against London City Lionesses on Sunday - their fifth draw in a row at the Emirates this season - with an inspired Mary Earps denying the Gunners victory.

While the result extends Arsenal's unbeaten home run to 24 league matches, it is becoming an increasing concern and a spectre on the shoulder that the Gunners have been unable to secure three points at the Emirates this year.

Giving her view to Sky Sports after the game, Renee Slegers - managing her 50th Arsenal game - said: "We spent more time than we normally do without the ball; partly the game plan and partly them asking questions of us on the pitch.

"We create big chances, could have done more with those. That's the frustrating part. This is the fifth [home game] and we couldn't give the fans the win. Unfortunately we couldn't do it for them."

Image: Mary Earps made a string of spectacular saves to keep London City Lionesses on level terms at Arsenal

It was two early goals that decided the fixture too. Frida Maanum scored for a second game in a row - having netted against Barcelona in the Champions League in midweek - slotting home from an Alessia Russo cross to put Arsenal ahead.

But a minute later, London City were level. Leah Williamson lost the run of the lively Izzy Goodwin, and the striker lashed into the roof of the net.

From then on, it was a goalkeeping masterclass from former England No 1 Earps especially that kept Arsenal from scoring another with her counterpart Misa Rodriguez also making her fair share of saves, albeit not as frequently.

The Gunners simply could not find a way past the inspired London City stopper as Lionesses boss Sarina Wiegman watched on from the stands.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player London City Lionesses were not behind for long as Isobel Goodwin cancelled out Frida Maanum's opener

The pick of her string of world-class saves came when she tipped a Maanum shot onto the crossbar. It came shortly after substitute Delphine Cascarino had also rattled the woodwork at the other end.

The result does little to improve either side's WSL standings, and Arsenal's hopes of finishing in the Champions League places takes another hit. They are sixth on 14 points - already six behind London City in third.

"We were happy with the one point, we wanted and needed three today," Slegers added. "Every game is three points for Arsenal when we play for this club.

"At the moment, with our position in the table and how we need to stay connected and compete for the top three positions for the Champions League, this one was very important for us.

"With that being said, the season isn't over. It's still November and we have to look at what it looks like in May."

10: GOAL! A sweeping move is finished by Maanum after Russo's cutback to give Arsenal the lead.

11: GOAL! London City immediately equalise as Goodwin fires into the roof of the net.

22: SAVE! Earps makes a good stop to deny Lisa Baum, who cuts in from the right-hand side.

27: SAVE! Misa Rodriguez on hand this time to deny Alexia Putellas.

29: SAVE! Again from Earps! This time it's a flying effort to keep out another Baum shot.

68: CROSSBAR! Cascarino pings an effort off the top of the woodwork.

77: DOUBLE SAVE! Earps pulls off another brilliant double save, first to deny Smith then Maanum.

85: CROSSBAR! Earps fingertips a Maanum shot onto the crossbar.

How's your luck? Arsenal face dazzling Earps as home woes continues

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mary Earps reflects on a hard-earned point for the London City Lionesses, as former England team-mate Millie Bright heaped praise on the goalkeeper

Analysis from Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh at the Emirates:

Before Sunday's game, Sky Sports asked whether Arsenal have lost their fear factor at the Emirates this season.

The answer surely has to be yes - although after the game, Slegers was adamant that the fear factor has not gone, despite being without a win.

Teams have come to the Emirates and sat in a low block that the Gunners have been unable to break down more than once.

London City were never going to do that. It's not in their DNA. They closer resemble the Barcelona team Arsenal faced on Thursday where, funnily enough, they drew 1-1.

But what they might not have been banking on was an ingenious performance from Earps. While Arsenal did not have to worry about defenders sitting back, they did face a goalkeeper putting in one of the performances of the season. How's your luck?

Image: Isobel Goodwin celebrates after equalising for London City Lionesses at the Emirates

She made eight saves as Arsenal continued to pepper her goal - her most in the WSL since 2017 - and the second-most in the WSL this season after the goalkeeper that replaces her at Man Utd, Phallon Tullis-Joyce.

When asked how she found the game, Earps told Sky Sports: "Tiring. It's a big point away from home.

"Either team could have won it in terms of chances. Happy with the point - would have liked three. All the girls put their bodies on the line. I love defending. It was tough today and I thought we did a good job."

It was perhaps made all the sweeter for her that her former England boss Sarina Wiegman was watching on. It is well-documented how she departed the national team, but it certainly showed the Lionesses head coach what she was missing.

Earps has had to bide her time at London City, with Elene Lete continuing to be the No 1 until recently. The former England No 1 has now started in three games, and while she is yet to keep a clean sheet, she will have staked a huge claim to the permeant spot with her performance on Sunday.

"Mary is amazing," her boss Eder Maestre said after the game. "It's not just because of the talent she has, she delivers the commitment and the togetherness that she can bring to the team because of her experience. Watching her in that performance was a pleasure."

Slegers: Players left everything on the pitch

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers to Sky Sports:

"Two good teams going against each other. I think we started the game well, score a very good goal, but we let them come back into the game too easily.

"I must say the players left everything on the pitch. They were absolutely dedicated, playing with hunger and focus. There are things in our game we must do better. We want to be dominating the ball. Being more ruthless. It's very basic but that's what it's about."

On Maanum: "She was very big for us against Barcelona and good for us tonight again. You can always count on her with runs into the box. The finish was very good."

On 50th Arsenal game: "I'm proud to represent Arsenal. I want to do everything I can for Arsenal."

Maestre: Our targets are bigger than a draw with Arsenal

London City Lionesses boss Eder Maestre to Sky Sports:

"We are happy because this kind of environment is always difficult to cope with, but at the same time, we want to win every game so we cannot be [too happy] just because it's the first time we've drawn against Arsenal.

"Our targets are even bigger. We have the hop to have the performance. We improve quite well in the second half. We had the chances, and they did as well.

"They're one of the best teams in the world and playing knowing that they need the points to push for the Champions League positions. We already knew how close it was going to be."

Sports.title: Scotland edge out Australia in Nations Championship
Sports.content:
Scotland eked out a hard-fought 15-12 win over Australia but were unable to get the bonus point they craved in a Nations Championship match that failed to catch fire.

First-half scores from Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey gave the Scots the edge at the break, with Harry Potter responding for the Wallabies.

Finn Russell's late penalty eventually gave the Scots some breathing space before Max Jorgensen's 80th-minute try offered the visitors a glimmer of hope but the Scots held on for a win that elevated them above Wales into fourth place in the Northern Hemisphere table.

Image: Australia's Harry Potter breaks free to score his side's first try of the game.

"When we saw the rain half an hour before kick off, you still hope you'll be able to move the ball. You could tell defences were coming off the line a bit quicker, knowing they could pressure the ball carrier," Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend told ITV,

"Both teams had to adjust and I thought we did that well. Defensively, that's one of the best performances I've seen in the last couple of years. Set after set we were putting them under pressure.

"We were on that edge of physicality but disciplined, hitting hard in the tackle, putting pressure on, listening to the referee, getting back onside. That makes it hard for the opposition to get into our 22m, which was a learning from last week.

"It was just constant effort. Today, we showed we can play another game, too."

Sports.title: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at Cheltenham
Sports.content:
Pioneer Pete could have the County Hurdle back at Cheltenham in March as a target after continuing his charge up the two-mile hurdling rankings in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle.

Posting a fourth win on the spin and backing up his impressive Welsh Champion Hurdle win at Chepstow, the likeable five-year-old was always in the front rank under Jonjo O'Neill Jnr and came clear to win by six and a half lengths at 7-2 from Tennessee Tango.

Victory for O'Neill, winning on the horse for the fifth time and riding for his father-brother training combination of Jonjo and AJ O'Neill, put welcome gloss on a day in which he had fallen twice from three previous rides.

"I thought Chepstow was his limit, but he is an amazing little horse," said O'Neill senior. "I have no idea how much more is left in the locker, but he is a horse in form and you would have to look at all those options like the County Hurdle now."

The training duo landed the County Hurdle with Wilful last March and AJ O'Neill admitted they are hoping the five-year-old may be good enough to chart a similar path.

"That is the dream. Wilful was a massive improver through the season and this fellow seems to be doing the same," he said.

"We didn't know how he would handle the ground exactly, but he seemed to handle it very well and hopefully he can continue to keep improving in the same respect.

"He is a horse that keeps improving. He is a horse that has improved every time he has run, then he comes back home and works like an improved horse which is nice to see. Hopefully he can continue to do that.

"I thought he winged the first and Jonjo had him in a lovely position. He switched him out for the slightly fresher ground and when he did that I thought, 'here we go'.

"He missed the last which doesn't help, but the horse tries really hard, you can guarantee he will always put in his best effort and then hopefully they are good enough on the day."

He also paid tribute to his brother, adding: "Jonjo is as resilient a jockey as you could find and that is just a good show of it today. The day hadn't worked out up until now, but he has given him an absolutely beautiful ride and it is testament to the jockey."

It was all smiles for winning connections, with Pioneer Pete being bred by Anthea Leigh, daughter of the late Peter Beaumont and named in honour of her Gold Cup-winning father.

"I think someone was looking down on us," said Leigh, who is racing manager and raceday clerk of the course at York. "It would have been his thing altogether, give him time and lots of education.

"I can't believe it, I had go into the stands and watch it on my own! This business is all about dreams and this is a dream."

The race did see another apparent slip on the level at the meeting, however, this time with The Hardest Geezer coming a cropper on the bend entering the straight under Ben Jones. Both horse and rider appeared to emerge unscathed.

Sports.title: Fisher wants fight with AJ dangerman Prenga early next year
Sports.content:
Johnny Fisher is looking to return to action early in 2027 and wants to fight Kristian Prenga, the man who almost derailed the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua mega-fight.

In July, Prenga boxed Joshua in what was meant to be a tune-up fight for the former world champion. Instead Prenga put him down heavily twice in their first round. He was on the edge of victory only for Joshua to storm back and knock him out in the second round.

Prenga caught the eye of the boxing world in that fight and Fisher would like the man who almost beat Joshua to be his next opponent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher discusses a potential return to the ring at the end of February, with provisional talks already under way

"Prenga would be good. That's a good sort of stepping stone to where I want to be. Someone who's fought one of the best heavyweights we've had in Great Britain in recent years, or in memory in general," Fisher told Sky Sports.

"So to be in the ring with someone like that, who carries knockout power, carries the ability to drop people, like Anthony Joshua, at the top of the division - so let's see what I can do."

Fisher added: "He almost did [beat AJ]. That's the fine margins of professional heavyweight boxing and there's jeopardy in it, I said that in the build up to the last one. It definitely is exciting."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Zuffa Boxing 11 fight between Johnny Fisher and Michael Pirotton

Fisher wants to box early next year, even though his last fight, against Michael Pirotton in September, turned into a gruelling battle.

"We're looking at February time," he said. "It'll be here before you know it. I want to start my camp on January 1. I want to build some good foundations.

"Dillian Whyte has been thrown in the hat, but maybe that's something for a summer showdown if I come through another test before then."

He has every intention of improving on that last performance. "I felt like I'd been through the mill a little bit, it was a tough, tough fight. Credit to Pirotton, he was a tough operator. I knew it was going to be," Fisher said.

"When he gave me a death stare I knew this was his World Cup final. He's a tough man, never been stopped and I boxed very well in the first four rounds and just that second wind never came. That was to do with things we can adjust and make better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Pirotton mocks Johnny Fisher after he got hit with a huge right hand!

Fisher did sting Pirotton in the 10th and final round. "I don't know where I found that energy in the last round but I've dug deep before to get to the final bell and I know I've always got that in me. But I don't want to always rely on it every time," he said.

"Me and Tony [Sims, his trainer] are still gelling, there's things that we can change in the camp.

"I couldn't have trained any harder but it didn't look that way because I probably left a tiny bit in that last week.

"That's why it's exciting as well," he added, "because we still haven't seen the best version of me."

Sports.title: One for the World Cup? England's new-ball switch to Baker pays dividends
Sports.content:
As England impressively levelled their three-match ODI series against Australia with a 135-run win in Adelaide, might they have stumbled upon the perfect bowling formula with one eye on the 2027 Cricket World Cup?

Tom Banton (121 off 99 balls) was rightly named Player of the Match for his second ODI hundred that helped turn things round after a dismal defeat in Perth - from 131 all out to 355-6 in the space of 48 hours - but the bowling was equally impressive.

Image: England's Tom Banton celebrates his second ODI century against Australia in Adelaide

Gus Atkinson (4-28) claimed career-best ODI figures as he and Sonny Baker (1-45) helped set the tone early on by reducing Australia to 29-4 in the opening seven overs of their run-chase as they were ultimately bowled out for 220.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australian cricketer Chadd Sayers, who was involved in the 'sandpapergate’ Test, believes everyone knew about it, stating there were numerous conversations about it at the time. Pictures courtesy of Sports Entertainment Network.

"The way England's bowlers attacked the first 10 overs, they didn't allow [Mitch] Marsh and [Travis] Head to get away, in terms of giving them any freebies," former England captain Sir Alastair Cook said on TNT Sports.

"They knew they'd come after them - Head hit a brilliant shot for six off a decent ball - but the way Atkinson and Baker bowled, they were made to work for their runs.

"I really liked how Baker got some movement out of the ball, that's his role in the side.

"You've got Archer and Atkinson who will hit the pitch hard - Archer, in this game, serving as the enforcer in the middle overs - so Baker using his swing up front was impressive.

"The [four] wickets early on made such a difference to the game. It was pretty much done early on, unless there was an extraordinary innings from one of the Aussies.

"Full credit to England for the way they adapted and used their bowlers in the right places."

Cook added: "Australia is a really hard place to go 1-0 down in any format. They're great front-runners, so to turn that round like they did after only 48 hours is absolutely superb.

"The leadership group should take a lot of credit for managing to get those players in the right frame of mind after the drubbing they got in Perth."

Baker-Archer switch grants 'England 'two bites at the cherry'

Baker - playing in just his fifth ODI - taking the new ball over Atkinson's usual accomplice, the more experienced Archer, was a bold move but one that paid off for England.

Image: England fast bowler Gus Atkinson took ODI career-best figures of 4-28 in Adelaide

Though Atkinson was the standout, Baker arguably deserved greater reward for his own probing opening spell, in which he dismissed Marsh (2) and had Josh Inglis dropped - Joe Root taking a stunning catch to dismiss the Australian skipper before he was then the guilty party in putting down Inglis.

"Baker's enthusiasm, you can tell he just loves playing cricket for England," former England wicketkeeper Matt Prior added on TNT Sports.

"I'm with Cooky. I'm really pleased that he was given the new ball, where he bowled full and tried to swing it.

"Brook has to take some credit as captain for making that decision."

England have 14 further ODIs scheduled ahead of the start of the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa in 11 months' time, and so might the Baker and Archer new-ball switch something they look to run with from here?

Image: Jofra Archer took 1-26 from 8.3 overs as he operated in a new role with the ball in the middle overs

"The change in using Jofra Archer through the middle [overs], I like that move," Australia batting consultant Mike Hussey told TNT Sports.

"It gives England two bites at the cherry. They get to attack with Baker and Atkinson at the start and, if things go well, they've got Archer to come in behind that and continue to build pressure.

"Even if things don't go well at the start, it's nice to know you've got someone of world-class quality to come in to arrest some of the momentum."

As for who has the edge going into Wednesday's series decider in Hobart (3.30am UK start time), Hussey fears the worst for Australia.

"England go into the final game with momentum because they've managed to turn things around [from Perth] straight away," he added.

"I think England will certainly take a lot of confidence away from this game. If they take the right attitude again into the final match in Hobart and start well, they'll be on their way towards a series win."

16m ago 15.18 EST 28 min Tuchel’s performance against Argentina is surely one of the great managerial eff-ups; which others spring to mind? Those in my head: Pep Guardiola, Man City v Chelsea in the 2021 Champions League final; Alex Ferguson, Man United v Chelsea 2010. Any more for any more? Share Updated at 15.18 EST

18m ago 15.16 EST 26 min Cucurella and Baena combine down the left and Ruiz’s subsequent cross is a goodun, but Quansah does really well to head clear, the ball landing on Porro’s laces … and ensuing volley landing I don’t even know where. Share

20m ago 15.15 EST 25 min Simon takes a liberty, drilling a hopeful pass through the middle of the pitch to which Konsa is first. He meets the ball with a solid header, finding Bellingham, who I think is offside, and once the shot slides by the near post, the flag is raised. Share

21m ago 15.13 EST 23 min We’re into that 4-4-2-block stage, Spain pinning them back into their shape, and Lamine slipping a pass into Baena, through the legs of Barcelona teammate Gordon; I doubt this is the last he’ll hear of a shameful episode. Share

23m ago 15.11 EST 22 min Lamine runs at Hall, who maybe just about fouls him. The requested yellow card does not follow, and the free-kick eludes Porro. Share

24m ago 15.10 EST 21 min Yup, Pedro Porro replaces Pubill – a change I think may actually help Spain, the new man’s first-phase excellence, ability to invert and goal-threat of greater use than the physicality they’re losing. Share

25m ago 15.09 EST 19 min Pubill is hurt, clattered by Simon when the keeper came to punch that second England corner; I don’t think he can carry on. Share

26m ago 15.08 EST 18 min And here comes Hall, picking a diag that takes him from touchline to box, beating two men with Rogers bumrushing the near post. The cross, though, is blocked behind then, when the corner comes in, another inswinging brute from Rice, Kane heads past the far post. He’ll be relieved the flag goes up, for that was a chance. View image in fullscreen Harry Kane of England reacts after missing a chance. Photograph: David Ramos/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.29 EST

28m ago 15.07 EST 17 min The game has settled after that rabid England start, Spain much more of a factor now, but here come England again, Anderson megging Merino and Kane moving the ball on. Nothing comes of it, but England step on to them again! Share

29m ago 15.05 EST 15 min The free-kick is swung out, but Oyarzabal can’t get enough on it and Quansah, who’s started well, imparts enough of a touch to see it away. Share

30m ago 15.04 EST 15 min The first flash of Lamine, who runs at Hall, moves inside via nutmeg – ouch – then Rice clips him from behind and is booked. Share

31m ago 15.03 EST 14 min Already, the inclusion of Merino is giving Spain a problem – when he drops, Quansah is following him, and he’s not able to make the extra man in midfield. Share

32m ago 15.02 EST 13 min So far, England have had 62% possession. Do not adjust your television sets, this is not a misprint. Share

34m ago 15.01 EST 11 min England’s press is excellent, its latest application forcing Simon to kick long; Wimblespain! Of course, at some point, the pass-and-move is likely to assume control, but if Tuchel’s men can grab a goal, they’ve the ability on the counter to add to it. Share

36m ago 14.59 EST 9 min This is the best nine minutes England have played under Tuchel and probably Southgate too, bristling with confidence, intensity and menace. Gordon gets Pubill squared, barges by on the outside … but his cut-back is into traffic. Share

37m ago 14.58 EST 8 min England move the ball about, a long diag finding Hall, who crosses low, first time. No one is in the middle for it, but Bellingham applauds the idea, presumably a tactic. Share

38m ago 14.57 EST 7 min Yup, led by Rice, England jump on Zubimendi, the ball squirts free, and the best 15-22 yard finisher of all time, Harry Kane, swishes a low sweep … just past the near post. View image in fullscreen Harry Kane of England goes close. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock Share Updated at 15.11 EST

39m ago 14.55 EST 5 min I bet England have given themselves a serious talking-to before coming out tonight. They’ve started like they mean it, the pain of their World Cup subsidence still raw. They won’t want to experience that sense of loss and desolation ever again; they’ll be experiencing it until the day they die. Share

41m ago 14.53 EST 3 min Gosh, am I dreaming? England win the ball high with Rice, securing a second corner … and this time, Simon comes to punch clear. Share

42m ago 14.52 EST 2 min The corner is an excellent one, met on the volley and on the run by Bellingham … this must be! But somehow, Simon extends an arm to prang the ball away! So England recylce quickly, finding Gordon inside the box, and he opts to pass a finish he might’ve driven … allowing Laporte to block! Tremendous start from England, but might they already regret these missed opportunities? View image in fullscreen England's Jude Bellingham (right) attempts a shot on goal. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share Updated at 15.31 EST

44m ago 14.51 EST 1 min The camera in the Metropolitano is vertiginously high, but not bad for watching how Spain pass and move. But it’s England into it immediately, the ball fizzing between Gordon, Bellingham and Kane and out to White, who wins a corner off Pubill. Share

45m ago 14.49 EST Casillas, along with Fernandos Llorente and Torres, lay flowers in memory of Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died so tragically, and in tribute to the victims of the recent high-speed train crash. There’s a moment of silence. Share

48m ago 14.47 EST “So Konsa and Quansah pair up as centre-halves,” writes Charles Antaki. Very good; the first pair of players whose names end with a schwa since, I reckon, Terry Butcher and Des Walker. Vaguely interesting, but sadly no guarantee that the quality will match up. Nevertheless, good lads both.” I’ve learnt a word. Ferdinand de Saussure has nowt on me. Share

50m ago 14.45 EST Spain’s go now, their underrated banger offering no lyrics. Share

51m ago 14.44 EST Anthem time, the pashun side-contest won convincingly by Rice. Share

52m ago 14.43 EST And now Iker Casillas presents the World Cup to Unai Simon, who raises it aloft for what must be the 79,043rd time. I doubt it gets boring. Share

53m ago 14.41 EST Our teams are tunnelled … and here they come! Share

53m ago 14.41 EST Ah, I forgot to note that James Trafford has been given the start in net. Maybe it’s to keep Jordan Pickford on his toes, but it won’t have escaped Tuchel’s attention that his no 1 got nowhere near Enzo Fernandes’ equaliser in Atlanta – not did it escape Bellingham’s, caught on camera saying “It was in the middle of the goal”, perhaps with added expletive. Pickford has been decent for England, but that doesn’t mean better isn’t possible. Share

1h ago 14.38 EST I’m really looking forward to seeing how Hall does against Lamine. He’s an excellent builder of play and a pretty good defender too, but does he have the explosion and recovery pace to get close? Share

1h ago 14.32 EST When did Vogue become Shoot become Mizz? The December edition not only features Jude Bellingham as its cover star – I can’t say my wife was impressed when it arrived through the letterbox – but with a gatefold poster, signed “Jude X”. And of course the “Hey Jude” headline is stone-cold genius; how do they think of these things?! Branding it like Beckham: how Jude Bellingham is future-proofing his fame Read more Share

1h ago 14.23 EST Spain, meanwhile, will want to circulate the ball, pulling England’s midfielders out wide to open that space in the middle Tuchel knows they mustn’t vacate; easier said than done. Ruiz will look to attack the box, Merino too – with both adding set-piece threat – while Lamine and Baena will both fancy themselves to have the better of their full-back, both inside and out. Oyarzabal will, I think, play off Quansah, fancying his nous to create space, while I’d not be surprised if Rice is the pressing trigger, the front players looking to jump when the ball goes into him. Share

1h ago 14.16 EST So, where is the game? I actually think Spain’s XI gives England a good chance. I’d not be at all surprised if Anthony Gordon is under orders to get about Martin Zubimendi – the way Alex Ferguson once did with Park Ji-Sung and Andrea Pirlo – a lovely passer but, by the standard a little weak. Mikel Arteta signed him because Declan Rice isn’t a first receiver, able to turn on the ball and punch into midfield, only to find the physicality of the Premier League was too much, hence the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, so Gordon – and Morgan Rogers – can worry him, allowing England to take possession high up the pitch. I also think they’ll use Kane dropping deep to thread passes in behind Spain’s high line, Gordon and Rogers looking to attack the space with Bellingham also joining the last line. Meantime, Anderson and Rice will seek to carry the ball forward, with the former also seeking to unfurl long passes and get the home defence turned to face their own goal. Share

1h ago 14.09 EST I should add that, while England could have won that Wembley game –they’d have been close to impregnable at 3-1 – they might easily have been 3-0 down before they scored. Share

1h ago 14.08 EST Tuchel speaks, telling ITV that “it’s a beautiful match”. They’ve qualified, done their homework and now can try and top the group. Quansah keeps his place for doing well, while he wants to see White under pressure and cites his club partnership with Konsa as a reason for picking him, just as last game, he went for the Newcastle understanding between Burn, Hall and Gordon down the left side. Otherwise, he wants to see “patient defending” when in a 4-4-2 or deep block, adding that, “under no circumstance” can they “open the middle” as, if you do, Spain will “go right through you” as they did to score their third when winning 3-2 at Wembley – a game in which Harry Kane missed a penalty to put England 3-1 up. Finally, they must avoid ball-losses in their own half. Share Updated at 14.11 EST

2h ago 14.03 EST Taking a closer look at the England side, there’s no getting away from it: the defence isn’t up to standard. Lewis Hall, mind-bogglingly omitted from the World Cup squad, is in – Tuchel’s problems were not just reflective of a panic at a crucial moment, but that he picked a group able to play one way only, without difference-making options. Otherwise, though, Konsa is now an automatic choice, but Quansah callow and lacking elite potential, while White is a decent Premier-League player and nothing more. Share

2h ago 13.58 EST Email! “Thanks for putting up the squad list,” says Edan Tal. “Delighted that Clint Hill finally managed his long awaited call up.” Shaun Derry next. Or Dan Burn. Share

2h ago 13.57 EST Back to the teams, the thing that strikes me about Spain’s – the thing that always strikes me about Spain’s – is the absence from it of Pedri. I’m not sure there’s another midfielder in the world I’d prefer to have, but De la Fuente likes the balance without him, even with Rodri absent. I do wonder, though, if they’ll be able to exert their usual midfield control, given he’s gone for Merino, who offers goal-power but not loads else. Share

2h ago 13.54 EST What’s on the line? Er, not much. Both sides are into the last eight, but the group-topper – England if they win tonight, Spain if they don’t – will play an unseeded team in the quarters, with the second leg at home, when the competition resumes at the end of March. In contention from the other A-groups are Italy, France, Belgium; Netherlands, Greece, Germany; Portugal, Denmark, Norway. Share

2h ago 13.51 EST As for England, Thomas Tuchel plumps for the joy of a Konsa/Quansah centre-back pairing, with Dan Burn dropping out. Otherwise, Ben White is in at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, and the now-settled front six remains the same. Share

2h ago 13.49 EST Spain are still without Rodri, but Lamine Yamal, rested for the 2-0 win away to Czechia, returns in place of Yeremy Pino. Otherwise, Pedro Porro, so important at the World Cup, loses out to Marc Pubill; Dean Huijsen is replaced by Aymeric Laporte; Mikel Merino is in for Fermin Lopez; and Mikel Oyarzabal is at centre-forward, not Ferran Torres.
