Sports.title: The Antonelli you don't know: Inside the Mercedes garage with F1's new world champion
Sports.content:
Mercedes mechanics have learned to watch their backs. Not because of the dangers of a pitstop, but because of Kimi Antonelli. Formula 1's newly crowned world champion has a rather unusual habit. He approaches members of his crew, greets them and, when they least expect it, gives their nipples a pinch - so nobody appears to be safe!

It is just one of the many practical jokes through which the 20-year-old Italian has developed a special relationship with the people who work on his W17. But behind the mischief, seemingly so far removed from the image of a world champion, lies something much more significant.

Success has roots that are not always visible. To understand them, you sometimes have to look beyond what happens on the track. In Antonelli's case, that means listening to the people who share the work, pressure and emotions of a grand prix weekend with him.

Their accounts paint a picture of a young man who has earned something that even a world championship cannot guarantee: the trust and respect of those around him. It is a relationship that developed naturally, rooted in an attitude Antonelli learned long before reaching F1, when he accompanied his father Marco to races with his own team. Growing up around workshops and racing circuits taught him a valuable lesson: before becoming a racing driver, you have to learn how to be part of a team.

"When he comes into the garage, it's quite a show," said Nathan Tupper, who works on the power unit of Antonelli's car. "He grabs everyone, pinches people's nipples, slaps them all over and generally causes chaos. At the end of the day, he's 20 years old. That's just Kimi."

Ash Jones, the second senior mechanic on Antonelli's car, agrees: "There are so many practical jokes that it would be difficult to list them all. He comes over, says hello and then gives you a pinch. That's how he jokes around with us. He likes having a good relationship with everyone, laughing and having fun together."

The jokes do not even stop when the circumstances would seem to demand maximum concentration. Tom Mason, Antonelli's number one mechanic, has seen it countless times: "It always makes me laugh watching him getting ready to get into the car before qualifying. He's still joking around, grabbing the guys, tickling them. Even when the pressure is enormous, he's there having fun. He's incredibly relaxed."

The driver who has displayed such remarkable maturity on the track is the same young man who, the moment he walks into the garage, becomes a 20-year-old eager to have some fun. Birthdays are another occasion for the Mercedes mechanics to be on their guard, as Antonelli has introduced a tradition of celebrating his colleagues by covering their faces in whipped cream.

George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Hector Vivas / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Callum Wooldridge, who works on the front end of Antonelli's car, explained why the ritual has become so popular within the team. "When you work in Formula 1, you spend so much time away from home that sometimes you end up celebrating your birthday during a grand prix weekend,” he said.

"It's not always easy. Sometimes you really miss being at home. Kimi started this thing with whipped cream in people's faces, and I don't think there are many other garages in the paddock where something like that happens. It's funny. It happened to me on my birthday in September last year."

The practical jokes have helped create an environment in which the relationship between the driver and his crew has become unusually close. "It's one of the best atmospheres I've ever experienced working with a driver," said Jones. “With Kimi, you feel completely comfortable. It's like talking to one of the guys you work with every day. There's no awkwardness, no tension when you speak to him."

Antonelli's race engineer Peter Bonnington actively encourages that sense of familiarity. "Bono encourages us to interact with him, to have a laugh," Mason explained. "Kimi is very approachable and loves joking around with the guys. It's a really good environment to work in."

The early tests, the crashes and the kid in the blue cap

To discover another side of Antonelli, one must go back to 2024, when Mercedes began the testing programme designed to prepare him for his F1 debut. Franck Bougeard was one of the mechanics involved in those sessions and his first encounter with Antonelli came in the spring, during a test in Austria. Kimi was just 17, wearing a blue cap with a rather unruly head of hair sticking out from underneath.

"I remember all that hair coming out of his cap, looking a bit messy," said Bougeard with a smile. "He really looked like a little kid. And there he was, about to drive a Formula 1 car." Bougeard's memories also include Antonelli's early crashes, as the young Italian began exploring the limits of an F1 machine.

"At Abu Dhabi, he crashed and damaged the chassis. Luckily, we'd brought a spare one, which is something we hardly ever do at those tests,” he said. "I don't even know why we'd brought it, but thank goodness we had, because we needed it."

Antonelli crashed on his F1 session debut in Monza, 2024 Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

Then came Monza, and another accident: "At that point I was starting to think, ‘brilliant, every time this kid leaves the garage, we're going to end up changing a chassis!’ He was very quick, but sometimes he pushed too hard. He needed to learn where the limit of the car was, and a few crashes were part of that process. That's exactly why we were there, to give him the opportunity to learn."

After his accident at Monza, Antonelli returned to the garage visibly upset about the extra work he had caused. "He kept apologising," Bougeard recalled. "He was saying how sorry he was for having destroyed the car again. I told him it wasn't a problem and that the important thing was that he was OK. Then I asked him: 'What did your dad say?'"

Kimi's answer has stayed with the mechanic ever since.

"He gave me a telling-off for half an hour,” he said. Bougeard also wanted to know how Antonelli's mother had reacted. Kimi explained that she had been terribly frightened, to the point of tears. So here was a teenager already capable of driving an F1 car, yet still dealing with the sort of family situations familiar to countless young people.

His father telling him off, his mother worrying about him, and Kimi returning to the mechanics to apologise. But Marco Antonelli also features in another memorable episode, as during a test in Abu Dhabi, after learning that his son had crashed into the barriers, he rushed towards the scene of the accident, even crossing the circuit to reach him.

"Marco was on the other side of the track. When Kimi crashed, he immediately set off to get to him,” said Bougeard. "I had to speak to him afterwards. I said: 'Marco, there are professionals here, there are ambulances. The last thing I want is for you to get run over by an ambulance while you're crossing the circuit!'"

Marco admitted he had been wrong. But those early accidents are more than just amusing memories. Tom Mason recalled that when Antonelli joined the Mercedes race team at the beginning of 2025, one of the young driver's biggest concerns was creating too much work for his mechanics.

Antonelli endured many a tough lesson before becoming world champion Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

"Whenever he made a mistake, he felt incredibly bad about it,” said Mason. “He kept apologising for the damage to the car and for all the work he'd caused us. Eventually, I told him he needed to stop worrying about that."

Mason remembered exactly what he wanted the young driver to understand. "I told him: 'You don't need to apologise to us. If something goes wrong, you don't have to worry about the car or the work we have to do. We're happy to do our jobs. As long as you give everything you've got, we'll do exactly the same for you.'"

There had inevitably been some uncertainty before Antonelli arrived, as Mercedes was saying goodbye to Lewis Hamilton after a hugely successful partnership and handing his car to an 18-year-old rookie.

"We didn't really know what to expect," Mason admitted. "We'd worked with Lewis for so many years and knew his habits inside out. With Kimi, everything was going to be new. I wondered how many accidents he might have, how long it would take him to adapt and how much extra work he might create for us."

There were difficult moments, particularly during the 2025 season. But Mason stressed that even at his lowest points, Antonelli never brought tension into the garage. "Spa was particularly difficult for him,” he added. “But we weren't angry. If anything, we felt sorry for him because we could see how much he was suffering. He was so young and had an enormous amount of pressure on his shoulders."

But one quality has particularly impressed Antonelli's number one mechanic: his ability to move on quickly from disappointment. "He can have a terrible weekend, or a practice session where everything goes wrong,” he said. "When he gets out of the car, he's angry. You can clearly see it. But the next time you meet him, he's already completely different. He comes back into the garage full of enthusiasm, ready to start again. He doesn't carry that negativity around with him. It's almost as if he starts again from zero every time."

For Mason, that attitude makes a considerable difference to the way the team operates. "If a driver is constantly in a bad mood, the people working with him eventually end up feeling the same way,” he claimed. "With Kimi, it's the opposite. He's so positive that his enthusiasm rubs off on everyone. For me, having to coordinate the work of the guys, that's an ideal situation."

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Two days to learn everyone's name

There is another detail on which all five mechanics agree: Antonelli knows the people who work on his car personally, and he learned their names remarkably quickly. "That's one of the things that impressed me most," said Ash Jones. "He knows everyone in the garage. Not just their names, but details about their personal lives too. If you tell him something about yourself, he remembers it."

Tom Mason remembered an episode from the days before Antonelli officially joined the race team. "When we found out Kimi was coming, I spoke to Rosa, his press officer,” he said. “I suggested organising something so that we could all get to know him. Rosa told me Kimi was really enthusiastic about the idea, but first he wanted to do something with the guys who'd worked with him during testing."

Antonelli had no intention of forgetting the people who had accompanied him through the previous months. "He was very conscious of that," said Mason. "He wanted to make sure he met up with the people from the testing programme first, the guys who had been with him up to that point. Then he would get to know everyone else."

And when he finally arrived in the race team's garage, the introductions were remarkably quick. "After a couple of days, he already knew everyone's name,” added Mason. "And that's incredible when you think about how much he had to learn at the same time: a new car, how the team operated, all the procedures, working with the engineers. Yet he still found the time to get to know every single person."

It is an attitude that seems to run through the Antonelli family. Nathan Tupper explained that Marco had also developed a spontaneous, affectionate relationship with the mechanics. "You can be working away and suddenly someone comes up and gives you a hug from behind. You turn around and discover it's Marco,” he said. "That's just how he is. They're a very open, affectionate family. They make you feel part of their world."

Callum Wooldridge remembered the young driver he first met at the beginning of 2025: “He was still a little shy and needed time to settle in. As the months went by, he opened up more and more. Today he's not shy at all. He jokes with everyone.

"But really, he's still the same person. He's just learned to feel at home. He's part of the family now. He behaves exactly like the rest of us. And the nice thing is that his attitude doesn't change depending on the results. Whether he's had a good day or a bad one, he's always the same kid."

Antonelli's crash during FP3 in Melbourne Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

Melbourne: When the mechanics worked a miracle

Yet life in the Mercedes garage is not all jokes and laughter, as Jones recalled what happened in Melbourne at the start of the 2026 season. Antonelli had badly damaged his car during FP3, leaving the mechanics facing a race against time to get it ready for qualifying.

"After qualifying, I went to speak to him," Jones said. "He told me: 'I've no idea how you managed to get my car back on track.' He genuinely couldn't believe it!" So Antonelli's second place on the grid made the day even more special.

"He was incredibly grateful for what we'd done. He just kept thanking us,” he said. "That's something that has really stayed with me." It is an episode that helps explain just how personally the Mercedes mechanics have experienced Antonelli's journey to the world championship.

"When Kimi has a bad day, we feel bad too," said Wooldridge. "Whether the problem is down to him or the car doesn't really matter. We're so close that we all go through the same emotions together. It's like being on a rollercoaster."

For Jones, the turning point in believing Antonelli could genuinely win the world championship came at Monza, where the Italian sensationally fought his way to victory from 19th on the grid. Wooldridge, meanwhile, chose Austin, where Antonelli converted an unexpected pole position into a victory delivered with remarkable maturity.

Nathan Tupper's most vivid memory is the emotion of Antonelli's maiden grand prix win in China - the race after Australia - whereas Bougeard, who first met Antonelli when he was still a teenager taking his first steps in an F1 car, prefers to look at the entire journey.

"It's incredible to think how much he's grown in such a short space of time,” he said. "We knew he had talent, but I never imagined he'd come this far, this quickly."

Marco Antonelli talks with Simone Resta, Deputy Technical Director of Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

A world champion who is still a kid at heart

There is one remark from Bougeard that perhaps sums up Antonelli better than any other. "It's difficult not to like him,” he claimed. "Even if you woke up one morning thinking you really didn't want to put up with Kimi that day, the moment you see him, you change your mind. He's got a great sense of humour and loves teasing people. He gives you the feeling that he's genuinely enjoying what he does."

Antonelli's story is full of contrasts. The kid with the messy hair who turned up for his first F1 tests. The young driver that apologised profusely after destroying a chassis, while his father told him off and his mother worried about him. And the 20-year-old who is now the youngest world champion, but still wanders around the garage playing practical jokes on his mechanics.

Antonelli has grown up. He has learned to handle pressure and earned authority within the team, without losing the spontaneity that characterised him when he first joined the Mercedes programme. His mechanics have watched an extraordinary talent develop. They have rebuilt his cars after accidents, shared his disappointments, celebrated his first victories and experienced the tension of a championship battle that would have seemed impossible only a few months earlier.

Then, on Sunday evening in Mexico City, came the hugs and the tears. It was not simply the joy of a team celebrating a world championship. It was the emotion of people who had watched a young man grow up, got to know him and, somewhere along the way, become genuinely fond of him.

The world title is just the next step on that journey.

Sports.title: Tsolov lands reserve driver role for F1 2027
Sports.content:
Nikola Tsolov has been named as reserve driver for both Red Bull and Racing Bulls for the 2027 Formula 1 season having missed out on a full-time drive.

The 19-year-old Bulgarian had been linked to a step up from F2 to replace Liam Lawson at Racing Bulls in 2027, but after weeks of speculation the Faenza-based squad put rumours to rest by confirming the New Zealander would continue alongside Arvid Lindblad.

Tsolov has impressed in his first full F2 season, claiming six victories which include four feature races and a streak that saw him become the first in series history to claim three on the bounce.

Next year he will take on a reserve and development role that, alongside the potential to act as a substitute in case of emergency - as Yuki Tsunoda did at Racing Bulls when Lawson was called upon to replace the injured Isack Hadjar at Red Bull - Tsolov will undergo an extensive programme that will combine simulator work with on-track experience, gained through FP1 and TPC [Testing of Previous Car] sessions, as well as Pirelli tyre tests.

“Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years," said Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies.

"To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

"We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1.

Nikola Tsolov Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

“This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.

"For now, Nikola still has an important job to finish in F2. We wish him every success in the final two rounds and will be supporting him all the way as he fights for the championship."

Tsolov sits second in the F2 standings and is seven points behind leader Rafael Camara with two rounds remaining, though the Brazilian could yet miss those if continuing with Haas - who he will race for next year - having stepped up to make his debut at Interlagos following Esteban Ocon's departure.

Read Also: Formula 1 Why Camara should take heart from a tough F1 debut in Brazil

Tsolov added: "I’m incredibly happy and grateful to Red Bull for giving me this opportunity. Since joining the junior team, I’ve received amazing support and have developed so much, both as a driver and as a person. My career has progressed incredibly quickly, and I owe a lot to everyone who has believed in me and helped me get to this point.

"My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver. Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting. I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.

"I know there is still a lot to learn, but I’m ready to work hard, make the most of every opportunity and give everything I have to the team. For now, my immediate focus is on finishing the F2 season as strongly as possible.”

Sports.title: Russell partners with BRDC to launch karting academy
Sports.content:
Formula 1 star George Russell has launched a karting academy in partnership with Silverstone to make motorsport more accessible and discover the next young superstar.

The eight-time grand prix winner launched his GR63 Karting Academy on Thursday with it open to boys and girls aged eight to nine, based at the kart track in Silverstone.

It features a “four stage path to the top” and will start in December with an open-access format inviting every eligible driver to Silverstone, where 80 will be selected for stage two.

That will see the 80 drivers compete in the “GR63 Shootout” on 31 January to determine the 25 slots for an eight-round championship at Silverstone from March to November in 2027.

The championship is fully-funded for each driver and the top five will go head-to-head in stage four next December, where the winner will receive a fully-funded karting campaign in 2028.

“Karting is where it all started for me,” said Russell, who won titles on a national and international level before progressing into single-seater competition.

“It taught me everything I’ve relied on throughout my career. I know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight.

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT images via Getty Images

“With the GR63 Karting Academy, I want to give something back by finding those hidden talents and giving them the support and platform they need to reach their potential.

“I'm really grateful to Silverstone and the British Racing Drivers’ Club for helping make this happen."

The academy is designed for those who “may not have the budget required to progress through the sport” with the costs in motorsport, both at grassroots level and at the top, increasing.

So costs to enter the academy’s opening stage are £25 with that rising to £75 for the “GR63 Shootout”, before everything is fully-funded from stage three onwards.

BRDC president David Coulthard said: “As owners of Silverstone and guardians of British motorsport, the BRDC has always been committed to reinvesting in the sport and nurturing home-grown talent.

“That commitment has played a big part in Britain’s long record of success in motorsport, and it is a great source of pride for the Club and its Members.

“The GR63 Academy captures that ethos perfectly, and we are delighted to work with George to support the next generation of drivers here at Silverstone."

All drivers must be a citizen of a commonwealth country and to book oneself for stage one, an arrive and drive session, click the link for the Silverstone website here.

Sports.title: Lawson to stay in F1 as Racing Bulls announces 2027 driver pairing
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed Liam Lawson will stay with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 campaign, partnering Arvid Lindblad for a second, straight season.

They have formed a formidable duo this year having propelled Racing Bulls to fifth in the championship, which is set to be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result.

Despite sitting on 89 points, however, compared to 38 for rookie Lindblad, Lawson's future was in doubt thanks to junior driver Nikola Tsolov starring in F2 this year.

The 19-year-old Bulgarian is second in the standings and has been handed private testing opportunities and a rookie FP1 session in Mexico as part of his junior driver duties.

So Racing Bulls was weighing up its need for short-term performance against its explicit goal of training young drivers for parent team Red Bull.

But with Lawson rising to the occasion in recent weeks, performing some of his strongest races under constant pressure, the 24-year-old has effectively been too good for the team to ignore.

Nikola Tsolov Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Sources indicated to Autosport in Brazil last weekend that amid a big push for the company's top leadership to back Tsolov, the pendulum swung back towards Lawson's favour with his performances over the Americas triple-header.

Read Also: Formula 1 How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson

So the Kiwi has now signed a fresh deal for 2027 with team boss Alan Permane saying he had "no doubt" that the squad will field the strongest possible line-up next season.

"We’re delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," he said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we’ve seen the progress they’ve made, both individually and as a pairing.

“I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Next year is set to be Lawson’s third, full season in F1 having made his debut at Zandvoort towards the back end of the 2023 campaign - having another partial season in 2024.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

"I’m very happy to be continuing with Visa Cash App Racing Bulls next year,” he said. “We’ve had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I’ve loved driving.

“It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for P5 in the constructors' championship. It's a testament to the hard work of everyone both at track, and back at the factory.

"I’m looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027. We’re building something super positive and I’m excited by what we can achieve together.”

Lawson is currently eighth in the drivers’ standings with Lindblad in 11th ahead of the final three rounds: Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"Looking back on my first season in Formula 1, it's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test," said 19-year-old Lindblad.

"I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season. It's set to be an exciting year, and I look forward to continuing to drive alongside Liam."

Sports.title: Poll: How many F1 drivers could have won the championship in Antonelli’s car? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
In the last two seasons, drivers from at least two different teams could have won the world championship.

But in 2026 it seems no one was going to beat one of the Mercedes drivers to the world championship. Andrea Kimi Antonelli won the title with a 119-point lead over Verstappen, with 100 points still available. Even if he scores nothing between now and the end of the season, he is assured of the title by at least 36 points.

It’s always been an unavoidable fact of Formula 1 that every driver gets a different chance to win the world championship: often within the same team. George Russell has had more technical problems than his team mate.

But would Russell have beaten Antonelli to the title if they each had the other’s car? And which of the other 20 drivers are quick enough to have won the title in Antonelli’s car?

When the 2026 season began the grid featured 12 grand prix winners, four of which were world champions.

Which of them – plus their rivals – could have won the world championship in Antonelli’s car?

Does Fernando Alonso have a third world title in him? Was it just unreliability which cost Russell the crown? Could another driver who had never won a race before 2026 have claimed the title like Antonelli did?

I say

Although Russell has had the worse luck of the two Mercedes drivers this year, it doesn’t explain the 130-point gap between them at the time Antonelli clinched the title. Therefore I don’t think it’s realistic to say Russell would have beaten Antonelli had they spent the year in each other’s cars. So which of the other 20 drivers could have beaten Russell in Antonelli’s car, taking it as read that they would have enjoyed a slight reliability advantage? I’d confidently back the four existing world champions. Charles Leclerc certainly looks like a potential champion based on his form compared to Lewis Hamilton and past Ferrari team mate Sebastian Vettel. Carlos Sainz Jnr is another multiple race-winner who measured up well against Leclerc so he gets the nod too. I’d put Oscar Piastri on the list for the same reason, notwithstanding his tough campaign this year. Both Cadillac drivers are experienced and successful enough to be considered championship contenders. Ordinarily I wouldn’t pick either as being quicker than Russell, but he’s had such a difficult year I’m adding them to my list. Isack Hadjar has been extremely impressive in his second year in F1, and if Antonelli can win the title in his second season I see no reason to rule him out. Although Liam Lawson has been strong in the midfield, his brief stint at Red Bull did not persuade me he’s a champion in the making in quite the same way. Pierre Gasly got his chance at a Red Bull cockpit too soon and is now showing the kind of consistent speed that championship campaigns are made of. He makes the cut too. It’s tempting to add more names to the list, particularly the likes of Gabriel Bortoleto and Oliver Bearman, but at the moment I don’t feel confident to call either potential future world champions. How many drivers could have won the title in Antonelli’s car? I reckon half the grid. Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Sports.title: Ignore social media echo chamber and trust F1 over Middle East races – Wolff | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says Formula 1 is right to go ahead with its plans to race in the Middle East.

Many sports including other motor racing series cancelled events in the region due to the US-Iran war. However F1 commercial rights holder Liberty Media held its Moto GP event in Qatar last weekend, despite one manufacturer staying away due to concerns over the safety of travelling to the region.

F1 confirmed this week it has abandoned its back-up plan to relocate the final round of 2026 to Imola in Italy if its planned events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi cannot go ahead.

Wolff said those questioning the wisdom of racing in the Middle East should pay less attention to media coverage and listen to those in charge of the series.

“For me, with our social media feed, we are always at risk of seeing what we want to see,” he told the BBC. “I believe you need to trust what the authorities say. You need to rely on the commercial rights holder, that’s F1, and the FIA as our governing body.”

However Wolff said no staff will be forced to attend the final two rounds and anyone choosing not to could hand an opportunity to a replacement.

“I strongly support that if someone doesn’t want to go to Qatar or Abu Dhabi, personally doesn’t want to, then I’m very fine with that,” he said. “We don’t want to oblige anyone. There’s not going to be any sanctions, or so on, on teams.

“If you don’t feel right about going there, then I have respect for that, and don’t go. It gives an opportunity maybe to someone else to be tested and to see how another person would perform in the future. That’s how I would approach it.”

Sports.content:
Liam Lawson made it clear to anyone who was watching that Racing Bulls was helping a team which is supposed to be a rival when he let Max Verstappen overtaken him at Interlagos. Days later Racing Bulls announced Lawson had a new contract.

Sports.title: Spotlight: FIA pulls F1 reporter’s pass over column calling Leclerc a ‘sneaky b*****d’ | Brief
Sports.content:
The Daily Mail says the FIA has barred its Formula 1 reporter from attending the final three rounds of the world championship as a media representative.

It quotes a letter sent yestreday by FIA general manager Alberto Villareal regarding an article the newspaper published about Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc , whom its F1 correspondent Jonathan McEvoy called a “sneaky little b*****d”.

“The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula One World Championship,” said Villareal, quoted by the newspaper.

“Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Accreditation Guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect.”

Three rounds of the season remain in the USA, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Earlier this year Max Verstappen ordered the removal of another journalist, Giles Richards of The Guardian, from a Red Bull press conference. Verstappen was unhappy Richards asked him three months earlier whether he regretted colliding with George Russell during last year’s Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Update: The Daily Mail has now announced it will not cover the final three rounds of the championship

Sports.title: Grosjean admits his single-seater career is likely over after ending IndyCar season 19th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean, who survived a fireball crash six years ago in Bahrain, is preparing to call time on his single-seater racing career.

Grosjean raced in F1 between 2009 and 2020, then switched to IndyCar. He completed his fifth season in the series this year but the 40-year-old admits he is unlikely to return.

“The reality is, this is probably the end for me with single-seaters,” Grosjean told Racer.

Grosjean finished on the podium three times in his first season in IndyCar with Coyne, earning the attention of top team Andretti, who hired him for the 2022 season. The team replaced him after he finished 13th in the championship for two years running,

After spending one year at Juncos Hollinger, Grosjean lost his drive for 2025, but returned with Coyne this year. The season began promisingly when he reached the final round of qualifying in St Petersburg, but a string of finishes outside the top 10 followed.

The Coyne driver finished on the podium just once all year. He ended the season 19th in the standings ahead of just six other full-time drivers, including RLL’s Mick Schumacher, who replaced him at Haas in 2021.

Grosjean said it had been a “tough” season overall. “I had [a] few amazing moments. I got the chance to lead the Indy 500. I finished in the top 10. I ran [in] the top five most of the last 60 laps. Amazing! I got a podium in Markham, which was incredible with my ‘tractor.’

“But then we go to Milwaukee and Laguna Seca, and [at] Laguna Seca, I qualified dead last, almost. I know it’s one of my fastest tracks, so I’m like, ‘I don’t want that anymore.’ I’ve had enough of those moments where you just don’t have the tools to play.”

Grosjean was supposed to contest his final grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. However the burns he suffered in his Bahrain crash forced him out early. His former team Haas gave him the opportunity to test one of its cars at Mugello last year.

Sports.title: Court of Appeal to hear Audi’s case over Tsunoda decision on November 25th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has set a date to hear Audi’s appeal over the Italian Grand Prix stewards’ decision regarding Yuki Tsunoda.

Audi is challenging the decision not to penalise Tsunoda, who finished the race in 10th position, for triggering an extra formation lap before the start of the race.

The ICA will hear the case on November 25th at the FIA’s headquarters in Paris.

Tsunoda, who substituted for Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson at Monza, finished seven seconds ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto. Therefore the Audi driver could gain a point if Tsunoda is penalised.

Bortoleto previously said Audi’s case was “straightforward”.

F1’s sporting regulations state any driver who causes an extra formation lap must start the race from the pit lane and will receive a Stop-and-Go penalty if they fail to. As Tsunoda did not start from the pit lane, Audi believes he should receive a penalty.

The stewards ruled Tsunoda “was not the ’cause’ of the extra formation lap” and therefore did not have to start from the pit lane.

This is the second time this year the ICA has been asked to rule on a decision taken by the stewards at a grand prix. In September they reinstated two penalties which were originally issued to Pierre Gasly during the Monaco Grand Prix and later rescinded.

ICA hearing announcement

On 6th September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the race director ordered an additional formation lap Following the race, the stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (driver of car number 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the driver. In decision number 69, the stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9th September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Sports.title: Zerafa Misreads Yoenli Hernandez Fight Tape Ahead Of WBO Title Clash
Sports.content:
Michael Zerafa is talking like a fighter who thinks home-court advantage in Melbourne will erase the memory of his two-round collapse against Erislandy Lara. He is right about one thing: the WBO title is suddenly within reach. Whether he can survive twelve rounds with Yoenli Hernandez to actually claim it is a completely different matter.

The situation already looks bleak for the 34-year-old Zerafa (35-5, 23 KOs), because he has not beaten any notable opposition in the last seven years since stopping Jeff Horn in August 2019. His four wins since being blown out by Lara in March 2024 have come against lesser opposition in Tommy Browne, Besir Ay, Mikey Dahlman, and Alejandro Ortiz. Now he is going up against a fighter viewed as a future star of the middleweight division, the Cuba-born Hernandez (11-0, 9 KOs).

Still, the Melbourne contender told DAZN Boxing he expects the vacant WBO middleweight title fight to land in Australia after the sanctioning body stripped Denzel Bentley on October 30 and ordered Hernandez and Zerafa into negotiations.

“The world title is there. I’m now the man to fight against [Yoenli] Hernandez. He’s very beatable, very strong, and tough,” Zerafa said, crediting Matchroom’s Eddie Hearn and Frank Smith with pushing to bring the bout to his backyard.

Melbourne is the target, though a date and venue remain unannounced. First, Matchroom has to clear a major hurdle at the negotiating table before the November 23 deadline.

WBO Purse Bid Threat

The WBO gave Hearn’s team and Leon Margules of Warriors Boxing, who represents Hernandez, until November 23 to reach an agreement. If talks stall, the fight goes to a purse bid with a $200,000 minimum.

For Hearn, beating that clock is everything. Warriors Boxing already stepped up once to put money behind Hernandez during the Bentley cycle, and letting this go to an open bid risks shipping Zerafa back overseas. Zerafa only landed this opportunity because No. 2 Vito Mielnicki Jr. declared himself unavailable and No. 3 Tim Tszyu is tied up with a December WBA title shot against Lara. Winning the negotiating battle to keep the fight in Melbourne is the only way Zerafa gets the exact terms he wants.

Where Zerafa Sees Openings And Where He Gets Hurt

Zerafa’s confidence comes straight from watching Francisco Daniel Veron push Hernandez to a majority decision on August 22 in Las Vegas. On paper, that result looks like a blueprint for beating the unbeaten Cuban. In reality, anyone who actually watched the fight saw Veron eat vicious power shots in every round.

Veron threw 809 punches across ten rounds, yet connected on only 105 while most of his work bounced off gloves or missed entirely. Hernandez landed roughly 200 punches out of 649 thrown, tearing into Veron with heavy right hands and punishing body work that distorted his face long before the final bell. That is why two judges scored it wide at 99-91 and 98-92 for Hernandez, making the lone 95-95 card look completely out of touch with the damage inflicted in the ring.

Veron did manage to wobble Hernandez toward the ropes in the fifth round with a sharp check hook, and he exposed brief moments where the Cuban loaded up on single right hands instead of chaining combinations together. The catch is that Veron had to absorb a beating just to create that one opening, and Hernandez immediately tightened his guard, took back control in the sixth, and hurt him again in the eighth.

Zerafa does not have the chin to absorb that kind of punishment while waiting for Hernandez to load up. Against Lara in March 2024, Zerafa was folded in two rounds the moment clean left hands started landing. Even his January 2026 bout against Nikita Tszyu ended in a third-round no contest after Zerafa told the ringside doctor he could not see.

Since that night in Las Vegas against Lara, Zerafa has rattled off those four stoppage wins in Australia, capped by an eighth-round TKO of Ortiz in August. He insists his past failures had nothing to do with his talent.

“It was never my ability. It was always the people I surrounded myself with in the past. It always made me look bad,” Zerafa said, praising the professionalism of Hearn and Smith.

Blaming old handlers for getting knocked out in two rounds by Lara is a tough sell for a 40-fight veteran, especially when nobody outside the ropes can take a punch for him once the bell rings. If Zerafa uses his feet, stays off the ropes, and forces Hernandez to adjust his stance for twelve rounds, he has a path to an upset in front of his home fans. If he gets dragged into eating the vicious shots Veron absorbed, his second world title shot will end just as quickly as his first.

Sports.title: Darius Fulghum Shuts Down Pacheco Rematch, Challenges Terence Crawford to Wrestle
Sports.content:
Darius Fulghum wrecked Eddie Hearn’s super middleweight plans in Carson on Saturday night, handing Diego Pacheco his first professional loss and immediately demanding the spotlight Hearn had been saving for his own fighter.

Fulghum walked out of Dignity Health Sports Park with a 12-round unanimous decision in a WBA final eliminator, then made it clear in his post-fight press conference that he has zero interest in giving Pacheco an immediate do-over.

“I think Diego will bounce back for sure,” Fulghum said when asked about a second fight. “I want to target some of the other big names.”

Canelo, Martínez, and the Rematch Clause Problem

Before Saturday, Pacheco was the name constantly floated for future fights against Canelo Álvarez and WBC interim champion Lester Martínez. Fulghum took that spot by taking away Pacheco’s reach and beating him up on the inside, and he made sure to remind Hearn of his pre-fight predictions.

“You heard what Eddie said in the press conference on how high he was on Diego. Diego is going to be the future in 168,” Fulghum said. “And I wanted to leave a message that, yeah, Eddie, you said that. So now you got to say the same thing about me.”

Hearn told reporters afterward that Pacheco’s contract includes a rematch clause, creating an immediate tug-of-war over what happens next. Matchroom needs Pacheco back in the win column to keep him in the Canelo sweepstakes, while Fulghum wants Golden Boy Promotions to cash in his WBA eliminator status for a shot at the division’s biggest names.

The WBA belt currently belongs to Jaime Munguía, who has 30 days to negotiate a mandatory defense against Bektemir Melikuziev. That timeline could force Fulghum to wait for the winner, leaving Golden Boy with a window to stage a major showcase fight in the meantime. Fulghum already picked the venue, lobbying for a homecoming card in Houston.

“We trying to bring big-time boxing back to Houston,” Fulghum said. “We need it bad. Houston wants it.”

Fulghum’s Wrestling Challenge to Terence Crawford

Fulghum also threw out an unexpected challenge to Terence Crawford during the post-fight media session, though he wasn’t asking the retired champion to put the gloves back on. Asked about the TNT broadcast, Fulghum joked about settling some Texas and Nebraska bragging rights on a wrestling mat.

“I ain’t going to call Bud to come out of retirement, but yeah, Bud, I got to see you in wrestling for sure,” Fulghum said. “First takedown wins.”

Fulghum actually has the credentials to back up the trash talk, and he holds a massive size edge over the retired former champion. While Crawford wrestled growing up in Omaha and uses that leverage in the clinch, he was never a decorated state tournament contender, leaving it to his son, Terence Crawford Jr., to capture a Nebraska Class A state championship earlier this year. Fulghum, meanwhile, qualified for the Texas state tournament as both a junior and senior at Ellison High School in Killeen, according to Killeen ISD records. He entered the 2015 Class 6A tournament with a 39-3 record at 195 pounds after placing third in his region, People Newspapers reported at the time.

Sports.title: Pacheco Exposed: Fulghum Hands Prospect First Loss in Carson
Sports.content:
Darius “DFG” Fulghum handed Diego Pacheco his first professional loss by unanimous decision Saturday at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California. Two judges scored the 12-round main event 115–112, and the third had it 114–113 for Fulghum. On the same Matchroom Boxing card, Anthony Olascuaga retained his WBO flyweight title with a unanimous decision over Yuberjen Martinez.

Darius Fulghum vs. Diego Pacheco

Fulghum (16–1–1, 13 KOs), the WBA’s No. 4 contender from Houston, took the WBC Silver and WBO International super middleweight titles from Pacheco (26–1, 19 KOs) in a bout that also served as a WBA final eliminator.

Fulghum opened a cut under Pacheco’s right eye with a left hand midway through the third. His left hand gave Pacheco trouble throughout the first four rounds. Pacheco did better in the fifth until Fulghum caught him on the chin with a right in the final minute. They traded clean right hands midway through the sixth, by which time Pacheco also had swelling around his left eye.

Referee Ray Corona deducted a point from Fulghum in the ninth for hitting behind the head. Fulghum drew blood from Pacheco’s nose with a right hand late in the round. He outworked Pacheco in the 11th and rocked him with a right to the chin midway through the 12th.

Anthony Olascuaga vs. Yuberjen Martinez

Anthony “La Princesa” Olascuaga (13–1, 9 KOs) retained his WBO flyweight title by unanimous decision over Colombia’s Yuberjen Martinez (7–1, 7 KOs), a two-time Olympian and 2016 silver medalist. The judges scored it 115–112 twice and 114–113.

Martinez landed several punches with Olascuaga against the ropes in the second before the champion hurt him with a counter. Olascuaga caught him with a counter right early in the third, but Martinez rallied over the third and fourth and shook the champion twice with uppercuts in the sixth.

Olascuaga hurt Martinez with a body shot in the seventh and went back downstairs with a combination in the eighth. The two traded in the tenth, when Olascuaga went down after their feet caught. Referee Thomas Taylor ruled it a slip. With the fight still close in the final round, Olascuaga dropped Martinez with a short right to the chin in the closing seconds.

Undercard Results

Charlie Sheehy def. Jose Matias Romero, 10 rounds. Sheehy (14–0, 8 KOs) won the WBA Continental North American lightweight title by decision over Romero (31–5–1, 11 KOs). Sheehy rocked Romero with a right in the second, trapped him on the ropes with a flurry in the eighth, and buckled his knees with a right uppercut late in the ninth. Romero was still returning right hands in the tenth. Gerard White was the referee.

David Adeleye def. Alexander Flores, UD 10. Adeleye (15–2, 13 KOs) won the WBA International heavyweight title by scores of 100–89 on all three cards. He dropped Flores (21–7–1, 13 KOs) with a jab midway through the third. Adeleye controlled the middle rounds and repeatedly used his forearm against Flores at close range. Flores landed a right hand in the final exchange. Ray Corona was the referee.

Zaquin Moses def. Manuel Lerma, TKO 4. The southpaw Moses (9–0, 5 KOs) controlled the first three rounds of the scheduled eight-round super featherweight bout. Lerma’s corner called a halt between rounds, and referee Thomas Taylor stopped it at 0:01 of the fourth. Lerma fell to 5–4–1.

Nishant Dev def. Sona Akale, KO 3. Dev (8–0, 6 KOs) dropped Akale (10–6, 5 KOs) with a right hand in the third round of their scheduled eight-round junior middleweight bout. Referee Robert Hoyle counted Akale out at 2:52.

Federico Pacheco Jr. def. Jack May, KO 5. Pacheco (12–0, 9 KOs) dropped May (11–2, 8 KOs) in the fourth and again in the fifth of their scheduled eight-round heavyweight fight. Referee Thomas Taylor waved it off at 2:59 of the fifth.

Frank Espinoza def. Abisai Torres Diaz, TKO 2. Espinoza (6–0, 6 KOs) dropped Torres Diaz (5–3–2, 1 KO) with a right to the chin in their scheduled six-round middleweight bout. Referee Gerard White stopped it at 0:50 of the second.

David Diamante was the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Darius Fulghum Upsets Diego Pacheco in Carson
Sports.content:
Darius Fulghum handed Diego Pacheco his first professional loss by taking away the space the taller man needed to box. Fulghum walked Pacheco down behind his jab and landed the cleaner punches inside to win a 12-round unanimous decision at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California.

Two judges scored it 115–112, and the third had it 114–113 for Fulghum, who improved to 16–1–1. Pacheco fell to 26–1. Fulghum won the WBC Silver and WBO International super middleweight titles in a bout that also served as a WBA final eliminator.

Fulghum’s Jab Keeps Pacheco Backing Up

Pacheco landed a clean right hand and a body shot in a close second round, but Fulghum was already making him work at a distance he didn’t want. Fulghum pressed inside and landed left hands to the body and head as Pacheco tried to tie him up. In the third, a stiff Fulghum jab opened a cut below Pacheco’s right eye.

Fulghum kept Pacheco from getting set in the fourth, using feints and changing angles to get his jab through. He followed with one of his best rounds in the fifth, catching punches on his gloves and coming back with right hands that landed flush on Pacheco’s chin. Pacheco could still get through with his right hand, but he spent too much time backing up to build on those shots.

Pacheco had a better finish to the sixth, forcing Fulghum back after spending much of the round giving ground. That spell was brief. Fulghum was back on the front foot in the seventh, finding Pacheco’s swelling left eye with the jab. By the eighth, Fulghum was again staying close enough to keep Pacheco from extending his punches.

Fulghum Finishes Strong After Deduction

The closest the fight came to turning late was in the ninth. Referee Ray Corona deducted a point from Fulghum for punches to the back of the head, a call some observers questioned because Pacheco was dipping as the punches came in. Pacheco picked up his pace and won the round on the Boxing News 24 card, making it a 10–8 round and cutting Fulghum’s lead to two points.

Fulghum took the initiative back in the tenth. Pacheco’s face was swollen and his mouth was bleeding as Fulghum backed him up and landed cleanly. The same pattern held through the final two rounds. Pacheco never put together the sustained rally he needed, and the fight went the distance without a knockdown.

Boxing News 24 scored it 116–111 for Fulghum. The point deduction made the official result especially tight on the 114–113 card, but Fulghum gave the judges three strong rounds after it. Whenever Pacheco found a little room to punch, Fulghum went back to his jab and made him give it up again.

Sports.title: Diego Pacheco vs Darius Fulghum Live Results: Round-by-Round Updates
Sports.content:
WBO flyweight champion Anthony Olascuaga (13-1, 9 KOs) retained his title by unanimous decision over Yuberjen Martinez (7-1, 7 KOs). The scores were 115-112, 115-112, and 114-113. Olascuaga landed hard shots to the head and body early.

Martinez picked up the pace in the middle rounds and traded with the champion. Olascuaga hurt him with a body shot in the eighth, forcing him to back away. Martinez stayed on his feet in that round and kept firing back down the stretch. Olascuaga dropped him in the final seconds of the 12th.

Lightweight Charlie Sheehy (14-0, 8 KOs) defeated Jose Matias Romero (31-5-1, 11 KOs) by unanimous decision over 10 rounds to win the WBA Continental North America title. All three judges scored the fight 100-90 for Sheehy. The unbeaten Bay Area prospect controlled the distance with his jab and built a clear lead through six rounds.

Romero found more opportunities at mid-range as the fight became more competitive in the later rounds. Both fighters landed clean right hands to the head in the eighth. Romero took Sheehy’s best shots without going down and kept firing back through the final rounds. Sheehy’s steadier work earned him every round on all three cards on the Diego Pacheco vs. Darius Fulghum undercard.

David Adeleye (15-2, 13 KOs) defeated Alexander “The Great” Flores (21-7-1, 19 KOs) by unanimous decision over 10 rounds to win the WBA International heavyweight title. All three judges scored it 100-89 for Adeleye. The British heavyweight dropped Flores with a jab in the third round, sending him backward onto the canvas.

Flores outweighed Adeleye by more than 26 pounds but rarely came forward after the knockdown. Adeleye appeared to hurt his biceps midway through the fight but continued to press as Flores offered little in return. The win came in Adeleye’s first fight in the United States and his debut with Matchroom Boxing. It was his first victory since losing a unanimous decision to Filip Hrgovic.

Zaquin “Zaybop” Moses (9-0, 5 KOs) stopped Manuel “El Tomate” Valentine Lerma (5-4-1) when Lerma’s corner kept him on his stool after three rounds. The official time of the TKO was 0:01 of the fourth round. The junior lightweight bout was scheduled for eight rounds.

Moses controlled the fight from his southpaw stance and broke Lerma down with steady pressure over the first three rounds. Both fighters are 21, but Lerma spent much of the bout on the defensive. Moses, a Matchroom prospect from Newark, is the younger cousin of Shakur Stevenson. He spoke with the DAZN broadcast team after the win.

Nishant Dev (8-0, 6 KOs) dropped and stopped Sona “Slink Proper” Akale (10-6, 5 KOs) in the third round of a scheduled eight-round junior middleweight bout. The 6-foot-1 southpaw controlled the action against Akale, who gave up six inches in height. Dev scored the knockdown in the third and finished the fight before the end of the round.

Akale, 38, had previously faced Nico Ali Walsh. Dev, 25, was coming off a first-round stoppage of Cesar Diaz in July, when he scored three knockdowns. The unbeaten Matchroom prospect has now stopped six of his eight professional opponents. Dev discussed the win with the DAZN broadcast team after the fight.

Frank “Knuckles” Espinoza (6-0, 6 KOs) stopped Abisai “El Talisman” Torres Diaz (5-3-2, 1 KO) by second-round TKO in a scheduled six-round middleweight bout. Espinoza hurt Torres Diaz with a barrage of punches in the second. Referee Gerard White stepped in at 0:50 to end the fight.

Torres Diaz came in with more professional experience, but he couldn’t withstand the 21-year-old’s power and pressure. The Sacramento prospect has now stopped all six of his professional opponents. It was Espinoza’s second stoppage win on a Diego Pacheco card this year, following his July victory over Luis Caraballo Ramos. Espinoza celebrated the quick finish with fans at ringside.

Heavyweight Federico Pacheco Jr. (12-0, 9 KOs) stopped Jack “The Outlaw” May (11-2) with a left hook to the body in the fifth round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Pacheco took his time early against the taller, heavier May, who outweighed him by nearly 18 pounds. Both landed punches in a busier second round, with Pacheco catching May with a solid right hand.

Pacheco dropped May with an overhand left late in the fourth. May beat the count, but he was still hurt when the bell rang. Pacheco stalked him in the fifth and folded him with a left hook to the body for the second knockdown. May stayed down through the count.

Sports.title: Anthony Olascuaga Drops Yuberjen Martinez Late to Retain Title
Sports.content:
Anthony “Princesa” Olascuaga needed all 12 rounds and a knockdown in the final seconds to keep his WBO flyweight title Saturday night. Olascuaga (13-1, 9 KOs) beat Yuberjen Martinez (7-1, 7 KOs) by unanimous decision, with scores of 115-112, 115-112, and 114-113 in the co-feature of Diego Pacheco vs. Darius Fulghum at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California.

The one-point card showed how much was still at stake when Martinez went down. The Colombian beat the count and made it to the final bell after spending much of the fight trading with the champion. It was Olascuaga’s sixth successful defense and his first professional bout in the Los Angeles area.

Olascuaga’s Body Work Slows Martinez

Olascuaga landed hard punches to the head and body early, but Martinez began letting his hands go more freely in the middle rounds. The challenger was willing to trade when Olascuaga came forward, and he landed enough of his own power shots to make the champion work for the rounds.

Martinez came into the fight with seven stoppages in seven professional outings, and he was still firing back after Olascuaga had carried him deep into his first world title fight.

The eighth was one of Olascuaga’s best rounds. A body shot hurt Martinez and sent him retreating, giving Olascuaga a chance to follow him and keep the pressure on. Martinez stayed upright and kept the fight competitive into the championship rounds, but the champion had found a target he could return to when the challenger stood his ground.

CompuBox counted 67 body shots among Olascuaga’s 203 landed punches, nearly a third of his total. Only eight landed power punches separated the two men over 12 rounds. That narrow margin spoke to how often Martinez answered back, while Olascuaga’s work downstairs gave him one of the clearest moments of the fight before the knockdown.

Olascuaga, 27, won the vacant WBO belt by knocking out Riku Kano in three rounds in July 2024 and had already beaten former champion Hiroto Kyoguchi by decision. The Carson bout was his Matchroom Boxing debut, with Teiken co-promoting him, and brought him home after a title run fought mostly in Japan.

Martinez, 35, brought two Olympic appearances and a silver medal from Rio to his first world title challenge. His seven professional wins had all ended inside the distance, including a WBO Latino title win, so this was his first time hearing the final bell as a pro. He was still in the fight when the 12th round was almost over.

Olascuaga sent him to the canvas with seconds left, and the narrowest card came back with just one point between them. Before the knockdown, Martinez was getting the better of Olascuaga and looked to be on his way to victory. The ending kind of shows you how important it is to stay dialed in. Martinez looked like the better fighter.

Sports.title: David Adeleye Drops Flores and Wins Wide Decision
Sports.content:
David Adeleye (15-2, 13 KOs) dropped Alexander Flores (21-7-1, 19 KOs) with a jab in the third round and won a unanimous decision to claim the WBA International heavyweight title on Saturday night in Carson, California. All three judges scored the 10-round fight 100-89 for Adeleye, and fans booed at the lack of action on the Diego Pacheco vs. Darius Fulghum undercard.

The knockdown was the clearest moment of a fight that rarely opened up. Adeleye caught Flores with a jab that sent him backward to the canvas, where he tried to prop himself up with an arm. Flores got up and made it through the round, but he seldom came forward after that, leaving Adeleye to do most of the pressing.

Adeleye Controls the Fight After the Knockdown

Flores weighed 266.8 pounds to Adeleye’s 240.5, a difference of more than 26 pounds. The heavier man spent long stretches on the defensive. With Flores rarely pressing forward, Adeleye could keep working at his own pace and bank rounds without having to fight his way out of much trouble.

Adeleye appeared to hurt his biceps midway through the bout and continued to press. Flores was still there at the final bell, but he offered little sustained offense to make the later rounds competitive. The crowd let the fighters hear its frustration as the bout went the full distance at Dignity Health Sports Park.

The three identical cards reflected how little the balance of the fight changed after the third. The judges gave Adeleye every round, with the knockdown accounting for the extra point in the margin. For Flores, the rounds lost early left him needing to take more chances in the second half. He rarely did, and Adeleye had little reason to abandon a pace that was winning him every round.

For Adeleye, the result was a return to the win column after his unanimous decision loss to Filip Hrgovic in August 2025. The former British heavyweight champion was making both his United States debut and his first appearance with Matchroom Boxing. Flores, a 36-year-old veteran from Southern California, entered with 19 knockouts, but he spent too much of the fight backing off to give himself many chances to use that power.

Adeleye had stopped 13 of the 14 opponents he had beaten entering Saturday. This time he had to go 10 rounds against a heavier man who was content to give ground after getting dropped. The third-round jab showed how quickly Adeleye could hurt Flores. The rest of the bout showed how rarely Flores was willing to risk getting caught again, even as the rounds slipped away and the boos came from the crowd.

Sports.title: Diego Pacheco Seeks To Outshine Darius Fulghum
Sports.content:
Diego Pacheco (26-0, 19 KOs) returns to the War Grounds in Carson, California to get one step closer to his aspirations of becoming a world champion. He’s delayed a world title fight, wanting to ensure he’s fully prepared for what is coming.

He turned down a title fight against Hamzah Sheeraz during a time he was changing trainers and did not want to commit to the fight under those conditions. He wanted to have more time and become acclimated to his new trainer, Buddy McGirt. In his first fight under Buddy in July of this year, a much-improved Diego stopped the very tough and gritty Immanuwel Aleem in the eleventh round. Pacheco controlled the range and utilized his jab well, connecting on 44.2 percent of his total punches (Compubox).

The Spit Bucket Podcast asked Pacheco about the recent changes Darius Fulghum (15-1-1, 13 KOs) has experienced, changing his training from Houston, Texas, and relocating to the Brickhouse Gym in North Hollywood under co-trainer Julian Chua. Diego said of Darius, “I’ll be honest with you I’ve never seen Darius before. I didn’t see not one fight, not one tape, you know so…I’m not worried about him. I’m worried about me and what I have to do and making sure I’m ready and I’m good money.”

This is surprising considering Fulghum is an opponent who can present many challenges within the ring. He gave Bektemir Melikuziev all he could handle, fighting him on the inside and giving him a bloody nose.

At Thursday’s Press Conference, Darius made it known that he believes team Pacheco made a mistake in choosing him as an opponent, as he is a dangerous opponent and believes he can surprise many and score the upset. Fulghum is a boxer who can box at range or on the inside. He has good size and power and does present stylistic challenges. Darius has his own world title aspirations and knows another loss will set him back a few steps. Although Diego himself may not have watched tape, his trainer Buddy would have done his homework and prepared him for what will be a tough match. If Pacheco can continue on the improvements from his previous fight, he can demonstrate improved skills, which will be boxing at range, utilizing the jab, and using a controlled attack that uses timing and precision to counter his opponents.

Fulghum struggled against David Stevens, demonstrating difficulties on the inside when given the right amount of pressure. Diego must exploit this weakness. He’s always performed well at the War Grounds and must shine bright tonight if he intends to gain that super championship title match he’s been seeking. Promoter Eddie Hearn would like to pin Pacheco against the WBA super middleweight champion Jaime Munguia in a Los Angeles super fight or against the WBC super middleweight titleholder Canelo Alvarez. Huge title fights are on the horizon for Diego, but he must first perform great against the very game Fulghum.

Ghana News.title: Ghana calls for urgent climate finance delivery to support Africa’s climate ambitions
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has called for the urgent delivery of climate finance commitments to support African countries in addressing the growing effects of climate change.

Speaking at the Ministerial Meeting of the African Ministerial Conference on the Environment (AMCEN) in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister of Environment, Science, Technology, and Innovation, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, stressed the need for increased adaptation funding and a fair approach to climate action.

She noted that although Africa contributes only about 4 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions, the continent continues to bear a disproportionate share of the effects of the climate crisis.

Dr Agyeman-Rawlings called for a just energy transition, fair carbon markets and increased investment in Africa's green industrialisation as part of efforts to secure a sustainable future for the continent.

She also reaffirmed Ghana's commitment to advancing Africa's common position on climate justice, climate finance and sustainable development.

The Minister reiterated Ghana's support for the African Group of Negotiators, emphasising the importance of African countries speaking with one united voice in international climate negotiations.

She maintained that Africa must secure concrete commitments and tangible outcomes from global climate discussions rather than leave negotiating tables with promises that are not fulfilled.

Her remarks form part of Ghana's broader push for equitable climate financing and greater recognition of Africa's needs in global efforts to address climate change.

Ghana News.title: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 ends in vibrant celebration of Ghanaian enterprise after three days of business, shopping and entertainment
Ghana News.content:
The 2026 Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair has successfully concluded after three exciting days of business exhibitions, product displays, shopping bargains, networking, cultural performances and live music, transforming Ghud Park at Accra Mall into a vibrant marketplace for Ghanaian entrepreneurs and consumers.

The three-day event, which ran from Friday, November 13, to Sunday, November 15, brought together more than 80 businesses and brands across various sectors, giving small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) an opportunity to showcase their products, attract customers, generate sales and establish valuable business connections.

From locally processed foods, spices and refreshing beverages to fashionable clothing, beauty products, electronics, agricultural produce, household essentials and innovative technology solutions, the fair offered patrons an extensive range of products and services to explore and purchase.

Organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank and powered by JoyPrime, the exhibition combined business promotion with entertainment, creating an engaging experience for exhibitors, shoppers, families and other visitors.

Three days of business, music and unforgettable experiences

The opening day on Friday, November 13, set the pace for the exhibition, with participating businesses welcoming patrons and displaying products across different categories.

Ghud Park quickly became a bustling shopping destination, with colourful exhibition stands, product demonstrations and vendors engaging visitors eager to discover new brands and take advantage of attractive offers.

Joy Prime's KMJ and popular content creator Quecy Official added excitement to the opening-day activities, interacting with exhibitors and patrons and bringing additional visibility to the businesses participating in the fair.

Nkyimkyim Band also featured among the musical acts, adding to the live entertainment and giving patrons more reasons to remain at the exhibition and enjoy the atmosphere.

Patrons sang along, danced and captured memorable moments, while vendors who had spent hours promoting their products also joined the celebrations.

The atmosphere was characterised by the aroma of freshly prepared meals, colourful fashion displays, beauty products, electronic gadgets and household essentials, as shoppers moved from one stand to another exploring the offerings.

Saturday, November 14, brought another dimension to the event as Ghanaian music duo Lali X Lola and King Jerry delivered energetic performances that transformed the exhibition grounds into a lively celebration.

Patrons sang along, danced and captured the moments on their phones, while vendors who had spent hours promoting their products also joined the entertainment.

In some memorable scenes, exhibitors carried their merchandise onto the dance floor as they danced, creating an unusual but exciting blend of business promotion and musical entertainment.

The second-day performances demonstrated the fair's ability to attract visitors beyond conventional shopping activities, allowing businesses to connect with customers in a relaxed and entertaining environment.

The excitement continued on Sunday, November 15, with the Kekeli Borborbor Group bringing the traditional rhythms and energetic dance traditions of the Volta Region to the exhibition.

The cultural performance was complemented by a live-band appearance from Shakers Band, giving patrons another opportunity to enjoy music and dancing while exploring the various exhibition stands.

The Borborbor display brought a distinctive cultural touch to the final-day activities, while Shakers Band maintained the entertainment atmosphere, providing a fitting conclusion to three days of business, culture and celebration.

Food lovers treated to an impressive variety

One of the biggest attractions throughout the fair was the wide selection of food products, beverages and agricultural produce presented by participating businesses.

Wilmar Africa showcased its Fortune Spread brand, while Kivo, Didi Shito, Corki Ventures, Adjoor Ventures, Manellah Foods, Gold Coast Foods with its Sankofa Spices, and Yaapee Royal Foods were among the businesses displaying food products and locally processed goods.

Other food exhibitors included NutriSmart Ventures, Golden Parani Company Limited, G-Way Investments Africa Limited, Ikam Plus Company Limited and ESBONY Food Package, which specialises in repackaging finished goods.

For beverage enthusiasts, Koa Impact Commerce showcased natural cocoa juice, Delsoy Ltd presented soy milk, Orave Juices offered fruit juice, while Pinnacle Coco Limited displayed coconut juice.

Jussvina Drinks (Global 500), Green Cup, which featured beetroot, guava and pawpaw teas, and Myst Natural Water also added to the beverage selection.

BB Brothers and Mushroom General were among other exhibitors, with the latter showcasing processed mushroom products.

Agricultural businesses, including Farm Mate, Orrab Farms, T&C Farms and Atohfield, presented agricultural and fresh-produce offerings.

Those looking for freshly prepared meals were also catered for, with Flourish Foods Africa showcasing grilled chicken and poultry products, MamsiJoy Ventures offering rice, Ellie Catering Services presenting fufu, Martha's Yam Trading specialising in yam, and Selis Satisfactory displaying kenkey.

The food section was further enriched by Di Dwa Foods, Bliss Pop, 97 Bakes, Aladdin Bakery, Evive Delight Ltd and Desco Ltd, which showcased snacks, baked products, popcorn and processed foods.

Fashion, beauty and lifestyle take centre stage

Fashion enthusiasts had plenty to explore, with Haute Xklusive, La Robe Classique, Asangenta, Utonez Clothier, Kofikyere Klothing, Regy Couture Ltd, Kims Foods and Clothings, and JAT Couture showcasing clothing, dresses, bags and accessories.

Shoes Ts3 presented footwear for different sizes, while Kinky Love Crochet displayed hair products and wigs.

Beauty and personal-care brands were also well represented, with Haus of Lush, RNS Beauty, Leepoku Ventures, Atlas Prime Merchantile Ltd and Chocho showcasing their products.

Mist and Strands presented bath and body products, while Reed Diffusers Ghana Ltd and Esquicet Scents exhibited home-fragrance products, including diffusers and scented candles.

Liz Imports showcased perfumes and home appliances, Kemz Ceramics displayed ceramic products, and Eldem Floral Services presented fresh-cut flowers.

Businesses catering for mothers, children and families also participated, including Roses Enterprise, Mothercare and Prestige Children's Palace.

The variety gave shoppers opportunities to explore fashion, beauty and lifestyle products while interacting directly with the businesses behind the brands.

Technology, electronics and household solutions

The exhibition also provided a platform for technology companies and businesses offering practical solutions for homes, offices and commercial activities.

Galop Sea Limited showcased laptops and accessories, while Xfromo Hypermart displayed mobile phones and accessories, including Google Pixel devices.

Katon 360 Technologies presented a digital platform designed to support SMEs, while Solid Connect showcased an application for artisans.

We Shop Africa and Ayuda represented the e-commerce sector, offering visitors opportunities to explore digital shopping solutions.

Atlantic Meridian EV showcased electric vehicles, while Vital Vendors presented car essentials.

For household and construction needs, Sintex Tank exhibited water-storage solutions, DBS showcased housing and roofing products, and MGIG Suppliers presented powdered soap.

Worafam Group of Companies displayed safety wear, while Greenhaul Solutions showcased waste-management and scrap-procurement services.

Other participating businesses included Vaal Real Estate, Advantage GH Premium Apparel, Blessed 3 Ventures, Gorgeous Vie Event Hub, Grandeur Consult Travel and Tour, Astolinks and Afram Publication.

BB Chemist also participated with its Relax Liver Salt product, while Golden Pride (Yao Consult) represented the liquor retail sector.

Major institutions strengthen participation

Established institutions and major brands also featured prominently, adding to the diversity of the exhibition.

Ecobank, MTN, the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), Glico Life and Central University were among the participating institutions.

Their presence provided opportunities for visitors to explore banking, telecommunications, insurance, export promotion and educational services, complementing the wide range of products and services offered by smaller businesses.

The participation of established institutions alongside emerging enterprises demonstrated the fair's ability to bring different players in Ghana's business ecosystem together.

A significant platform for Ghanaian SMEs

Beyond the entertainment and shopping experience, the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair provided participating businesses with an opportunity to increase brand visibility, introduce new products, engage potential customers, generate sales and establish commercial relationships.

For many exhibitors, the direct interaction with consumers offered an opportunity to explain their products, receive feedback and demonstrate the value of their offerings.

Patrons, on the other hand, benefited from having access to a wide range of products in one location, with opportunities to compare offerings, explore promotional deals and purchase directly from business owners.

The 2026 edition builds on the maiden fair held in October 2025, which attracted more than 160 exhibitors and recorded over 1,000 visitors on its opening day.

The latest exhibition's participation by more than 80 businesses and brands across food and beverages, fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, finance, real estate and lifestyle sectors further highlighted the diversity of Ghanaian enterprise.

The event also demonstrated how entertainment can complement business exhibitions by attracting audiences, keeping patrons engaged and creating memorable experiences around participating brands.

A vibrant celebration of enterprise

As the curtains came down on the 2026 edition, the three-day exhibition had offered a compelling combination of commerce, culture and entertainment.

From KMJ and Quecy Official's opening-day engagements to the musical performances of Lali X Lola and King Jerry, and the traditional Borborbor rhythms of the Kekeli Borborbor Group alongside Shakers Band's live performance, each day brought a distinct attraction to the fair.

The enthusiastic participation of vendors, the diversity of products on display and the entertainment programme helped make the exhibition a memorable meeting point for businesses and consumers.

For the participating SMEs, it was an opportunity to take their brands directly to the marketplace, reach potential customers and explore new commercial opportunities.

For patrons, it was three days of shopping, discovery, entertainment and support for Ghanaian businesses.

It was a vibrant celebration of Ghanaian creativity, innovation, entrepreneurship and the growing potential of small and medium-sized businesses.
