How Sports Betting Became Legal in the US

For decades, the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act of 1992 (PASPA) barred most states from authorizing sports betting. Nevada was exempt. Delaware, Montana and Oregon kept limited carve-outs for older lottery-style products.

New Jersey challenged the law, and on May 14, 2018, the US Supreme Court ruled in Murphy v. NCAA that PASPA was unconstitutional. The decision left each state free to set its own rules, and Delaware took the first legal single-game bet outside Nevada weeks later.

Here is when each state took its first legal bet:

Before 2018: Nevada

2018: Delaware, New Jersey, Mississippi, West Virginia, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island

2019: Arkansas, New York, Iowa, Indiana, Oregon, New Hampshire

2020: Illinois, Michigan, Montana, Colorado, Washington DC, Tennessee

2021: Virginia, Arizona, Wyoming, Connecticut, South Dakota, Washington, Louisiana, Florida, Wisconsin, North Carolina, North Dakota, Maryland

2022: Kansas

2023: Ohio, Massachusetts, Kentucky, Maine, Nebraska

2024: Vermont

2025: Missouri

States With Legal Online Sports Betting

These 31 states and Washington, DC, allow online sports betting. Each listing covers the launch date, the state regulator, the minimum age, college betting rules and which of our featured sportsbooks are available.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Arizona?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online and retail September 2021

Regulator: Arizona Department of Gaming

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: College player props not offered; in-state teams allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Arizona launched online and retail betting on the same day in September 2021, timed to the start of the NFL season. It is one of the largest markets in the West, and all six of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Arkansas?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail July 2019; online March 2022

Regulator: Arkansas Racing Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No restrictions

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel

Arkansas opened casino sportsbooks in 2019 and added mobile betting in 2022, with the state's casinos running the apps. FanDuel entered in March 2026 as a partner of a casino licensee, which must keep at least 51% of the revenue.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Colorado?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online and retail May 2020

Regulator: Colorado Division of Gaming

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: College player props not offered; in-state teams allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Colorado voters approved sports betting through Proposition DD in 2019, and online and retail books opened in May 2020. It has one of the deepest app markets in the country.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Connecticut?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail September 2021; online October 2021

Regulator: Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection, Gaming Division

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on Connecticut college teams, except tournament outcome bets; props on Connecticut college athletes not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, Fanatics

Connecticut runs a three-operator market built on agreements with the Mashantucket Pequot and Mohegan tribes and the Connecticut Lottery. Only three operators are licensed online, including FanDuel and Fanatics.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Delaware?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail June 2018; online December 2023

Regulator: Delaware Lottery

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on Delaware college teams, including tournament games

Featured Online Sportsbooks: None of our featured sportsbooks

Delaware took the first legal single-game sports bet outside Nevada on June 5, 2018. Online betting runs through a single lottery-contracted platform, so none of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Florida?

Legal Status: Online and retail (Seminole Tribe)

Launched: Brief launch November 2021; relaunched November 2023

Regulator: Florida Gaming Control Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: Florida college teams allowed; no college prop bets of any kind (Seminole compact)

Featured Online Sportsbooks: Hard Rock Bet

Florida's market is controlled by the Seminole Tribe under a 2021 gaming compact, which makes Hard Rock Bet the only legal online sportsbook in the state. After a federal court fight over the compact paused the 2021 launch, Hard Rock Bet relaunched statewide in late 2023.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Illinois?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail March 2020; online June 2020

Regulator: Illinois Gaming Board

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on Illinois college teams, online or in person; props on out-of-state college athletes generally available

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Illinois is one of the largest markets in the country by handle. Since July 2025 operators have paid a per-wager tax on top of a graduated revenue tax, and Chicago began taxing sportsbook revenue in January 2026.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Indiana?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail September 2019; online October 2019

Regulator: Indiana Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: In-state teams allowed; pregame college player props allowed, in-game college player props not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Indiana launched mobile betting in October 2019, one of the first states in the Midwest to do so. In September 2026 the Indiana Gaming Commission declined an NCAA request to ban college player props, leaving the question to lawmakers.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Iowa?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online and retail August 2019

Regulator: Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: In-state teams allowed; props on athletes at Iowa schools not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Iowa launched online and retail betting together in August 2019. In-person registration was required at first, but that rule ended in January 2021.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Kansas?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail September 1, 2022; online September 8, 2022

Regulator: Kansas Racing and Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No restrictions

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Kansas launched online betting in September 2022, with the Kansas Lottery as the operator of record. Current sportsbook contracts run through August 2027, and a 2025 budget provision barred the lottery from negotiating new ones, so the market's long-term structure is an open question.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Kentucky?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail September 7, 2023; online September 28, 2023

Regulator: Kentucky Horse Racing and Gaming Corporation

Minimum Age: 21 (raised from 18 on July 15, 2026)

College Restrictions: In-state teams allowed; bets on Kentucky college athletes falling short of a stat line (unders) not allowed since July 15, 2026

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Kentucky launched in September 2023 with an 18 and older minimum age. In April 2026 lawmakers overrode Gov. Andy Beshear's veto of HB 904, which raised the betting age to 21 effective July 15, 2026, and banned under-style player props on athletes at Kentucky colleges.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Louisiana?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail October 2021; online January 2022

Regulator: Louisiana Gaming Control Board

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: In-state teams allowed; college player props not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Louisiana legalized sports betting by parish-level vote in 2020, and online betting works only in the 55 of 64 parishes that approved it. The state raised its online tax rate to 21.5% in August 2025.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Maine?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online November 2023; retail September 2024

Regulator: Maine Gambling Control Unit

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on Maine college teams, wherever they play

Featured Online Sportsbooks: None of our featured sportsbooks

Online betting in Maine is reserved for the state's Wabanaki Nations, which partner with national operators. None of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Maryland?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail December 2021; online November 2022

Regulator: Maryland Lottery and Gaming Control Agency

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: College player props not offered; in-state teams allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Maryland voters approved sports betting in 2020, and mobile apps launched just before Thanksgiving 2022. The state raised its online tax rate from 15% to 20% in 2025.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Massachusetts?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail January 2023; online March 2023

Regulator: Massachusetts Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: College player props not offered; no bets on Massachusetts college teams, except in tournaments

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Massachusetts launched mobile betting in March 2023, just ahead of March Madness. Lawmakers have debated stricter rules, including limits on props and live betting, though none had become law as of October 2026.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Michigan?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail March 2020; online January 2021

Regulator: Michigan Gaming Control Board

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No restrictions; in-state teams and college player props allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Michigan launched online sports betting and online casino games on the same day in January 2021. bet365 became the latest major sportsbook to enter the state in April 2026.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Missouri?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online and retail December 1, 2025

Regulator: Missouri Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: In-state teams allowed; no player props on any athlete in a game involving a Missouri college team

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Missouri voters approved Amendment 2 in November 2024, and online and retail betting launched together on December 1, 2025. It is the newest legal market in the country.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Missouri sports betting guide .

Is Sports Betting Legal in Nevada?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail since 1949; mobile apps since 2010 (in-person registration required)

Regulator: Nevada Gaming Control Board

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No restrictions

Featured Online Sportsbooks: BetMGM (operated with Nevada registration rules)

Nevada was the only state with full-scale legal sports betting before 2018, thanks to an exemption in federal law. Mobile apps are run by Nevada casino companies, and national brands such as FanDuel do not operate there.

Is Sports Betting Legal in New Hampshire?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online December 2019; retail 2020

Regulator: New Hampshire Lottery Commission

Minimum Age: 18

College Restrictions: No bets on New Hampshire college teams or college games played in the state; props on New Hampshire college athletes not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: None of our featured sportsbooks

New Hampshire runs a single-operator market through the state lottery, which keeps about half of the revenue, and none of our featured sportsbooks operate there. It is one of the few states where adults 18 and older can bet.

Is Sports Betting Legal in New Jersey?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail June 2018; online August 2018

Regulator: New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on New Jersey college teams, including tournament games, or on most college games played in the state; props on New Jersey college athletes not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

New Jersey brought the case that ended the federal ban, Murphy v. NCAA, and opened its first sportsbooks in June 2018. The state raised its online sports betting tax rate to 19.75% in 2025.

Is Sports Betting Legal in New York?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail July 2019; online January 2022

Regulator: New York State Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on New York college teams, including tournament games; college player props not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, Fanatics, theScore Bet

New York is the largest legal betting market in the country by handle, with mobile apps live since January 2022. Operators pay a 51% tax on online revenue, one of the highest rates in the country.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our New York sports betting guide .

Is Sports Betting Legal in North Carolina?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail (tribal) 2021; online March 2024

Regulator: North Carolina Lottery Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No restrictions

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

North Carolina launched mobile betting in March 2024, days before the ACC Tournament and March Madness. The state's July 2026 budget raised the online tax rate from 18% to 23%.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our North Carolina sports betting guide .

Is Sports Betting Legal in Ohio?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online and retail January 1, 2023

Regulator: Ohio Casino Control Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: College player props not offered (since March 2024); in-state teams allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Ohio launched online and retail betting together on January 1, 2023, during college football bowl season. A 2026 bill (HB 971) would sharply restrict online betting, but it had not advanced as of October 2026.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Ohio sports betting guide .

Is Sports Betting Legal in Oregon?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail August 2019; online October 2019

Regulator: Oregon Lottery

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No college betting on the state's online app; tribal casinos set their own rules

Featured Online Sportsbooks: None of our featured sportsbooks

The Oregon Lottery runs the state's online market through a single-operator partnership, and no college betting is offered on the app. Tribal casinos offer in-person betting.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Pennsylvania?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail November 2018; online May 2019

Regulator: Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: College player props not offered; in-state teams allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

Pennsylvania legalized sports betting in 2017, before the federal ban was struck down, and launched online in May 2019. Its 36% tax rate on sportsbook revenue is among the highest in the country.

For a full breakdown of the state's legal sportsbooks, see our Pennsylvania sports betting guide .

Is Sports Betting Legal in Rhode Island?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail November 2018; online September 2019

Regulator: Rhode Island Lottery

Minimum Age: 18

College Restrictions: No bets on Rhode Island college teams or college games played in the state; props on out-of-state college athletes allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: None of our featured sportsbooks

The Rhode Island Lottery runs the state's only sportsbook, available in person and through a single statewide app. None of our featured sportsbooks operate there.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Tennessee?

Legal Status: Online only

Launched: Online November 2020

Regulator: Tennessee Sports Wagering Council

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: College player props not offered; in-state teams allowed

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Tennessee was the first state to launch online-only betting with no retail sportsbooks. It taxes operators on the total amount wagered rather than revenue, which is unique among legal states.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Vermont?

Legal Status: Online only

Launched: Online January 2024

Regulator: Vermont Department of Liquor and Lottery

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on Vermont college teams, except tournament games; college player props not offered

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, Fanatics

Vermont launched online-only betting in January 2024 with three operators, including FanDuel and Fanatics.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Virginia?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online January 2021; retail July 2022

Regulator: Virginia Lottery

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on Virginia college teams, including tournament games; no college prop bets of any kind

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet, Hard Rock Bet

Virginia launched mobile betting in January 2021, and casino sportsbooks followed in 2022. A 2026 law (HB 515) banned credit card deposits for sports betting starting July 1, 2026.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Washington DC?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Online May 2020; retail 2020

Regulator: DC Office of Lottery and Gaming

Minimum Age: 18 under DC law (some sportsbooks, including BetMGM, require 21)

College Restrictions: No bets on DC college teams (Georgetown, George Washington, American, Howard) or on college games played in DC

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

The District launched the lottery-run GambetDC app in 2020 and replaced it with FanDuel in 2024. A 2024 law change let private sportsbooks operate citywide, and bet365 became the latest to enter in September 2026.

Is Sports Betting Legal in West Virginia?

Legal Status: Online and retail

Launched: Retail August 2018; online August 2019

Regulator: West Virginia Lottery

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No restrictions

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, bet365, Fanatics, theScore Bet

West Virginia legalized sports betting before the Supreme Court ruling and opened its first sportsbook in August 2018. bet365 launched in the state in August 2026.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Wyoming?

Legal Status: Online only

Launched: Online September 2021

Regulator: Wyoming Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 18

College Restrictions: No restrictions

Featured Online Sportsbooks: FanDuel, BetMGM, Fanatics

Wyoming offers online-only betting with no retail sportsbooks, and adults 18 and older can bet. The state places no cap on the number of sportsbook licenses.

States With Retail-Only Sports Betting

These eight states allow sports betting only in person, usually at commercial or tribal casinos. Some offer apps, but they work only on casino property.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Mississippi?

Legal Status: Retail only

Launched: Retail August 2018

Regulator: Mississippi Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: In-state teams allowed; college player props not offered

Online Betting: Not available statewide

Mississippi opened casino sportsbooks in August 2018, and apps such as BetMGM work only on casino property. A bill to allow statewide mobile betting passed the House for a third straight year in 2026 but died in the Senate.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Montana?

Legal Status: Retail only

Launched: Retail March 2020

Regulator: Montana Lottery

Minimum Age: 18

College Restrictions: No restrictions

Online Betting: Not available statewide

Montana's betting runs through the state lottery's Sports Bet Montana, available at licensed bars and taverns. The lottery app works only on those premises, so there is no statewide mobile betting.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Nebraska?

Legal Status: Retail only

Launched: Retail June 2023

Regulator: Nebraska Racing and Gaming Commission

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on college games played in Nebraska; no props or live bets on any game involving a Nebraska college team; props on out-of-state college athletes allowed

Online Betting: Not available statewide

Nebraska allows sports betting at its licensed racetrack casinos. Voters decide don November 3, 2026, whether to legalize online sports betting through a constitutional amendment (Initiative Measure 440) and a companion statute. At the time of writing, it looks as if the vote will reject online sports betting.

Is Sports Betting Legal in New Mexico?

Legal Status: Retail only

Launched: Retail (tribal) October 2018

Regulator: New Mexico Gaming Control Board (tribal compacts)

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: Varies by casino; some ban bets on New Mexico college teams

Online Betting: Not available statewide

New Mexico's tribal casinos began taking bets in October 2018 under existing gaming compacts, without new state legislation. Online betting is not available.

Is Sports Betting Legal in North Dakota?

Legal Status: Retail only

Launched: Retail (tribal) December 2021

Regulator: Tribal gaming commissions (North Dakota Attorney General, Gaming Section)

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: Varies by casino

Online Betting: Not available statewide

Sports betting in North Dakota is limited to a few tribal casinos. A 2025 proposal to put the question to voters failed, and the legislature does not meet again until 2027.

Is Sports Betting Legal in South Dakota?

Legal Status: Retail only

Launched: Retail September 2021

Regulator: South Dakota Commission on Gaming

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on South Dakota college teams; no college prop bets of any kind

Online Betting: Not available statewide

South Dakota voters approved betting in Deadwood casinos in 2020, and bets can be placed only in person or on casino property. A 2026 plan to put statewide mobile betting on the ballot died in a House committee.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Washington?

Legal Status: Retail only

Launched: Retail (tribal) September 2021

Regulator: Washington State Gambling Commission

Minimum Age: 18 or 21, depending on the casino

College Restrictions: Bets on in-state college games allowed since June 2026; props on athletes at Washington schools not offered

Online Betting: Not available statewide

Washington's tribal casinos offer sportsbooks and apps that work only on casino grounds. A 2026 law (SB 6137) began allowing bets on in-state college games while banning props on athletes at Washington schools.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Wisconsin?

Legal Status: Retail only (online legal, not yet live)

Launched: Retail (tribal) November 2021; online legalized April 2026, not yet live

Regulator: Wisconsin Department of Administration, Division of Gaming

Minimum Age: 21

College Restrictions: No bets on Wisconsin college teams; props on Wisconsin college athletes not offered

Online Betting: Not available statewide

Wisconsin legalized online betting through its tribes in April 2026, but apps have not launched because each tribal compact needs federal approval. A lawsuit filed in August 2026 challenges the law under the state constitution.

States Where Sports Betting Is Not Legal

Sports betting is not legal in 11 states. Here is where each one stands.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Alabama?

Legal Status: Not legal

Alabama has no lottery or commercial casinos. A 2026 constitutional amendment covering a lottery, casinos and mobile betting died in committee, the third straight year a gambling bill failed.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Alaska?

Legal Status: Not legal

Alaska has no legal sports betting. A mobile betting bill (HB 145) remains in committee and has never received a vote.

Is Sports Betting Legal in California?

Legal Status: Not legal

California voters rejected two sports betting measures in 2022, and no measure is on the 2026 ballot. Most observers point to 2028 as the next realistic attempt, which would likely need the support of the state's tribes.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Georgia?

Legal Status: Not legal

A constitutional amendment fell short of the two-thirds House vote it needed in March 2026, and the companion framework bill never reached a floor vote. Georgia's next chance comes in the 2027 session.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Hawaii?

Legal Status: Not legal

Hawaii and Utah are the only states that ban all forms of gambling. Several 2026 bills stalled, and a state tourism and gaming working group is expected to report in late 2026 or early 2027.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Idaho?

Legal Status: Not legal

Idaho's constitution limits gambling, and lawmakers have not seriously considered sports betting.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Minnesota?

Legal Status: Not legal

Minnesota has debated sports betting for years. A tribal-run mobile betting bill failed again in 2026 amid a long-running dispute between tribes and racetracks.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Oklahoma?

Legal Status: Not legal

A bill to allow tribal retail and mobile betting failed in the state Senate in April 2026. Supporters plan to try again in 2027, when a new governor takes office.

Is Sports Betting Legal in South Carolina?

Legal Status: Not legal

A bill to create a state sports wagering commission received a hearing in February 2026 but did not advance.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Texas?

Legal Status: Not legal

Legalization requires a constitutional amendment approved by two-thirds of both chambers and then by voters. The legislature next meets in January 2027, and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick remains opposed.

Is Sports Betting Legal in Utah?

Legal Status: Not legal

Utah's constitution bans all forms of gambling, and there is no effort to change it.

Which States Could Legalize Sports Betting Next?

Several states have active legalization efforts heading into 2027. These are the ones to watch.

Nebraska: Voters decided on online sports betting on November 3, 2026. If approved, regulators must adopt rules by June 1, 2027.

Wisconsin: Online tribal betting is legal, but launch depends on federal approval of amended compacts and the outcome of an August 2026 lawsuit.

Texas: The legislature returns in January 2027. Any change requires a constitutional amendment and a public vote.

Georgia: A 2026 amendment fell short in the House. Supporters are expected to return in 2027.

Oklahoma: A tribal betting bill failed in the Senate in April 2026. A new governor takes office in 2027.

Mississippi: Statewide mobile betting has passed the House three years in a row but keeps dying in the Senate.

Minnesota: Tribes and racetracks remain divided, which has stalled every bill so far.

Alabama: A lottery, casino and sports betting amendment has failed three straight years.

California: No 2026 ballot measure. 2028 is the most likely next attempt.

Legal Sportsbooks by State

Not every sportsbook operates in every legal state. Here is where each of our featured sportsbooks is live online as of November 2026.

FanDuel (24 states plus DC): Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wyoming, Washington DC

BetMGM (21 states plus DC): Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia, Wyoming, Washington DC. BetMGM also operates in Nevada under that state's casino-based rules and offers on-property mobile betting in Mississippi

bet365 (18 states plus DC): Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Missouri, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia, Washington DC

Fanatics (23 states plus DC): Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wyoming, Washington DC

theScore Bet (20 states plus DC): Arizona, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia, Washington DC

Hard Rock Bet (10 states): Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, New Jersey, Ohio, Tennessee, Virginia

Florida is the only state where Hard Rock Bet is the sole legal online option. Delaware, Rhode Island and Nevada run their own state or casino-based platforms.

Prediction Markets vs Legal Sports Betting

Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket let users trade contracts on the outcome of sporting events. They operate under federal oversight from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) rather than state gaming licenses, which is why they are available in some states where sportsbooks are not legal, including California and Texas.

Many states argue these contracts are sports betting and should require a state license. Federal appeals courts have split. The Third Circuit sided with Kalshi against New Jersey in April 2026, while the Ninth Circuit (Nevada, August 2026) and the Sixth Circuit (Ohio and Tennessee, September 2026) ruled that states can regulate sports event contracts. New Jersey has asked the US Supreme Court to take up the issue.

Prediction markets are not the same as a licensed sportsbook. They are not overseen by state gaming regulators, and state responsible gambling protections may not apply. FanDuel also runs a separate product, FanDuel Predicts, which offers sports contracts only in states where FanDuel Sportsbook is not available.

Is Offshore Sports Betting Legal?

Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed or regulated by any US state. They often advertise to bettors in states without legal betting, but they offer no protection if a site refuses to pay, freezes an account or shuts down.

Licensed sportsbooks must verify your identity and location, keep player funds separate, follow state advertising rules and offer responsible gambling tools. If a sportsbook is not listed by your state regulator, it is not legal where you live.

Sports Betting Rules Every Bettor Should Know

What Is the Legal Age to Bet on Sports?

The minimum age is 21 in most states. Adults 18 and older can bet in New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Wyoming, Montana and Washington DC, though some sportsbooks in DC, including BetMGM, set their own minimum of 21. In Washington, the age depends on the tribal casino. Kentucky raised its minimum age from 18 to 21 on July 15, 2026.

Do You Have to Live in a State to Bet There?

No. You only need to be physically located inside a legal state when you place a bet. Sportsbook apps use geolocation to confirm your location, so visitors can sign up and bet while they are in the state.

Can You Bet From a State Where Sports Betting Is Not Legal?

No. If you travel into a state without legal betting, your app will block wagers until you return to a legal state. You can usually still log in, view your account and withdraw funds.

What Are College Betting Restrictions?

Many states limit college betting. The most common rules ban bets on in-state college teams, ban player props on college athletes, or both. Restrictions are listed in each state's section above.

How to Start Betting Legally

Confirm sports betting is legal online in your state using the list above. Choose a sportsbook licensed by your state regulator. Create an account with your name, date of birth, address and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Enable location services so the app can confirm you are inside a legal state. Make a deposit using a supported payment method, such as a debit card, online banking or PayPal. Claim any welcome offer you qualify for and place your first bet.

Responsible Gambling

Sports betting should always be entertainment. If gambling stops being fun, these free and confidential resources can help.

Every legal sportsbook also offers deposit limits, time limits and self-exclusion tools, and most state regulators run their own self-exclusion programs.

Where Is Sports Betting Legal FAQs

How many states have legal sports betting?

Sports betting is legal in 39 states and Washington, DC, as of November 2026. Online betting is live in 31 of those states plus DC, while eight states allow only in-person betting.

Is online sports betting legal in my state?

Online betting is live in Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, Wyoming and Washington DC.

Which states do not allow sports betting?

Sports betting is not legal in Alabama, Alaska, California, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Minnesota, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas and Utah.

When did sports betting become legal in the US?

The Supreme Court struck down the federal ban (PASPA) on May 14, 2018. Delaware took the first legal bet outside Nevada on June 5, 2018, and New Jersey followed days later.

What is the legal age to bet on sports?

The minimum age is 21 in most states. New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Wyoming, Montana and Washington DC allow betting at 18, though some sportsbooks set a higher minimum.

Can I bet on sports if I am visiting a legal state?

Yes. You do not need to be a resident. You only need to be physically located in a legal state when you place your bet.

Which state will legalize sports betting next?

Nebraska voters decided on online betting on November 3, 2026, and Wisconsin has legalized online betting but not yet launched. Texas, Georgia and Oklahoma are the largest states expected to revisit legalization in 2027.

Are prediction markets like Kalshi legal sports betting?

Prediction markets operate under federal CFTC oversight rather than state gaming licenses, so they are not licensed sportsbooks. Several states are challenging them in court, and their legal status in some states remains unsettled.

World.title: Democrat Mary Peltola is likely to win Alaska’s Senate race, as vote counting continues
World.content:
Former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola is likely to win Alaska’s Senate race, according to an NBC News Decision Desk analysis, as vote-counting continues in the state.

Peltola has expanded her narrow lead over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan with each new batch of votes reported this week. A “likely” characterization indicates that the NBC News Decision Desk has at least 95% confidence that Peltola will win the race.

See live results here.

Alaska’s is the only remaining 2026 Senate race in which the NBC News Decision Desk has not yet made a projection.

If Peltola wins, Democrats will have a 56-44 majority in the Senate next year.

The race remains uncalled a week after polls close as votes continue to be counted. Alaskans vote heavily by mail and ballots postmarked by Election Day are counted as long as they arrived by Nov. 13 — and a few days later than that for valid overseas voters.

In a race with such a narrow margin, these final votes are important, especially given Alaska’s ranked-choice rules.

If no candidate wins a majority of the vote on the first ballot, the lowest-placed candidate is eliminated and second-choice votes from that candidate’s supporters are counted. The process then repeats until someone gets a majority.

World.title: Women with autoimmune diseases often misdiagnosed for 4 years or more
World.content:
Women with autoimmune diseases such as lupus or rheumatoid arthritis are more likely to be misdiagnosed or get delayed treatment compared with men, with their symptoms often dismissed as “psychological.”

An online survey by British researchers found that it took women with an autoimmune disorder about four years to get a diagnosis, while it took men around three months to less than a year.

It adds to previous research showing disparities in diagnosis between men and women with autoimmune disorders.

“Women in particular felt not listened to or not heard or not believed by their medical professionals,” said Sydnae Taylor, a doctoral researcher at the University of Oxford in the U.K. and co-author of the study published recently in eClinicalMedicine.

Autoimmune diseases — including Type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis — occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body. More than 23 million people in the U.S. have an autoimmune disease, and most of them are women.

Autoimmune thyroid disease, which includes Hashimoto’s, was the most common type reported by women in the survey. It typically causes fatigue, unexplained weight gain and sensitivity to cold, among other symptoms.

Autoimmune conditions can affect anyone but are more common in women than in men, according to the federal Office on Women’s Health. For example, around 90% of people with lupus are women, according to the Lupus Foundation of America.

It’s not clear why women are more at risk. Research from the Mayo Clinic has suggested differences in the microbiome, sex hormones and that women’s bodies produce higher levels of antibodies that are associated with autoimmune disorders. A 2024 Stanford Medicine study found clues in a molecule connected to the X chromosome.

Because many of the disorders share similar symptoms in the early stages — fatigue, dizziness, low-grade fever, as well as stress, anxiety and depression — they can be difficult to diagnose.

Women and men have similar symptoms, but with women specifically, “they develop over time, so it’s often hard to recognize right at the beginning,” said Dr. Saira Z. Sheikh, the director of the UNC Rheumatology Lupus Clinic in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. Symptoms can appear during childhood and last throughout adulthood.

The survey was conducted through social media, patient support groups and community groups of underserved populations such as religious groups and the homeless population. It was translated into five languages as a way to reach diverse communities.

Participants shared data about symptom onset, how many clinicians were consulted and misdiagnosis. The data was then compared between men and women. Out of the 6,607 participants, 91.2% were women and the majority of them were from the United Kingdom.

Misdiagnosis is more likely when symptoms are “invisible,” meaning they aren’t detected in a blood test or involve pain, fatigue and neurological symptoms such as tingling, Taylor said.

In these situations, accurate diagnoses rely on doctors listening and believing the patient.

“We shouldn’t assume that women’s symptoms are psychological simply because the initial investigations are inconclusive,” Sheikh said.

World.title: Bowen Yang returns to ‘SNL’ to spoof Jensen Huang amid Nvidia spy scandal
World.content:
Former “Saturday Night Live” repertory player and writer Bowen Yang returned to help open the show this weekend with his portrayal of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

In the cold open, the nation’s most prominent tech-industry CEOs, including Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, are at a CIA gathering devised to teach them how to identify when a woman may be duping them.

“America needs you to learn the difference between a woman who would actually want to have sex with you and a woman who is clearly a spy,” said a CIA guide, portrayed by comedian John Mulaney, the night’s host.

Mulaney, a former “SNL” writer, used the story of Huang, who resigned from Nvidia on Thursday following reports that he had extramarital relationships, including one with a suspected spy for China.

“What do you think the lesson is here?” Mulaney asked.

Zuckerberg, portrayed by Andrew Dismukes, answered: “Never date a human woman.”

Mulaney dismissed the response and those of a few of the other tech titans in the room, prompting PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel, portrayed by James Austin Johnson, to defend the group.

“Show us some respect,” he said. “We do a lot for this country. Name one time technology has let us down.”

Mulaney answered by mentioning Friday’s nationwide flight ground stop and Thursday’s global Microsoft glitch.

He tried to empathize, however, noting that it’s a rare time in human history when men “as pale and as strange as you” even survive, let alone possess “all the world’s wealth and power.”

Mulaney asked the group to remember the people they dated before they were rich and famous. “Now all of a sudden someone very beautiful is interested in you. Why do you think that might be?” he said.

Zuckerberg chimed in. “Because she’s comforted by my Meta glasses recording her at all times.”

“No,” Mulaney said.

He later introduces someone “who learned this lesson the hard way.”

Enter Huang.

“It’s me, Jensen ‘Hide Your Wife’ Huang,” Yang said.

He explained that he’s into BDSM — “breakin’ da stock market” — and urged the men not to be like him.

“Women don’t like guys like us,” he said. “That’s how we became guys like us.”

"No way it’s taking less than two hours,” Bowen Yang's Mary Todd Lincoln tells prospective Lincoln Tunnel travelers. NBC

Yang appeared in a subsequent sketch, “Little Park of Horrors,” a spoof of Broadway musicals, that centered on the city outlawing horse-drawn carriages and the two men (Marcello Hernández and Kam Patterson) who want to ride in one.

Eventually realizing the dangers and limitations, the pair opt for a vehicle ride in the Lincoln Tunnel only to be confronted by Yang’s Mary Todd Lincoln, who sings about the pitfalls of such a subterranean journey.

“No way it’s taking less than two hours,” Lincoln sings. “And it won’t be for free. I’m sayin,’ I’m sayin’ that you and you and you — you’re going to pay me.”

A fan favorite, Yang started as a writer in 2018 and joined the cast the next year. He left “SNL” in December 2025, and made his Broadway debut in September as Lincoln in playwright Cole Escola’s “Oh, Mary!”

The night’s musical guest was Phoebe Bridgers.

“SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

World.title: Could a viral teen comedy be Netflix’s answer to YouTube?
World.content:
LIVERPOOL, N.Y. — Inside a make-believe pizza shop overlooking Onondaga Lake, a team of digital creators, filmmakers and young actors spent months cooking up a show that they hope will serve Netflix something it craves: a fresh audience.

“Minimum Wage,” a mockumentary that follows teens who work at a pizza shop, has garnered more than 30 million views across YouTube, TikTok and Instagram since launching in May 2024.

Now, Netflix is betting that Gen Z audiences will watch the viral hit in its expanded form on the streaming giant — and pay to view it.

The media company’s decision to acquire the show reflects a broader shift in Hollywood’s battle for younger viewers, as streamers increasingly turn to internet creators and their built-in fan bases to drive subscriptions and engagement.

Of course, it’s not a new strategy. For years, the industry has tried to tap into YouTube’s massive roster of creators. Sometimes, it’s a success: Amazon Prime’s reality competition series with YouTuber MrBeast, for example, became the platform’s most streamed unscripted series of all time. Other times, however, it’s more of a bust — like Netflix’s “Haters Back Off,” a comedy series with former YouTube star Colleen Ballinger, aka Miranda Sings, which was canceled after just two seasons.

But there has been a noticeable uptick in creator content across streaming in 2026. According to data from London-based market research firm Ampere Analysis, first published in Puck, creator-led programming across 16 U.S. streaming services surged more than 300% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier.

“YouTube is not just UGC [user-generated content] and cat videos anymore,” Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said during the 2025 fourth quarter earnings call. “They are TV. So we all compete with them in every dimension for talent, for ad dollars, for subscription dollars and for all forms of content.”

With “Minimum Wage,” showrunner writer and executive producer Will Phelps said his agent at UTA “called up all the different streamers, and a couple different streamers wanted it … so we got multiple offers.”

He did not disclose which streamers were vying for the show’s rights. But in the end, Phelps said, Netflix emerged as the strongest partner for American High Shorts, the production company behind the project.

“We wanted to do it the way we were doing it on YouTube, but just on a bigger scope,” said Phelps, who co-showruns with Jeremy Garelick and Axelle Azoulay.

“And rather than pushing us to do something glossy and different, Netflix let us do what we do best,” Phelps added. “Except for now, we have a huge platform.”

Phelps, Garelick and Azoulay were able to retain creative control over the writing and directing.

And Netflix allowed the original cast of largely unfamiliar faces to stay on — including Grace Reiter, who recently joined “Saturday Night Live.”

Comedian Randall Park was also added to the ensemble, playing Terry Sylvester, founder, CEO and franchise owner of the struggling Slice Club pizzeria chain.

Hyde Healy, Randall Park and Julia Dicesare in Minimum Wage. Netflix

Episodes are typically between 12 and 20 minutes in length, as opposed to the traditional 30-minute sitcoms that populate network television.

Phelps, a veteran of the entertainment industry, said he believes the key to making a quality show is maintaining the elements of a strong story, while tailoring the format to the viewer’s attention span.

Recent data from UCLA’s Center for Scholars & Storytellers (CSS), a nonprofit research center, supports his assertion.

Nearly 4 in 5 of the 1,500 survey respondents ages 10-24 said short-form videos can tell a story, according to the fifth annual “Teens and Screens” report, which was published in October.

While older generations identify storytelling with books, TV and movies, the same boundaries do not exist for younger generations, the report found.

“This is the first generation to grow up on video-first platforms, so for them short, creator-driven video simply is television,” Yalda T. Uhls, founder and CEO of CSS, told NBC News in an email.

For shows like “Minimum Wage” to succeed on streaming, young audiences have to find it authentic.

Thus far, the show has picked up buzz among viewers. The week the show launched, it was in the global top 10 of shows on Netflix, placing sixth behind Season 11 of “Love is Blind.”

Critics have also praised it — helping it notch a fresh score of 81% on the Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer. One reviewer described the series as Gen Z’s version of “The Office,” NBC’s hit mockumentary sitcom that was set at the fictional Dunder Mifflin Paper Company in Scranton, Pennsylvania.

“A show like ‘Minimum Wage’ arrives with proof that an audience already loves it,” Uhls said. “The key is to bring over what made it work, meaning the creator’s voice and its authenticity, instead of polishing it into something generic.”

World.title: 2 injured after taxiing planes collide at Miami International Airport
World.content:
Two taxiing planes collided at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, officials said, a day after a nationwide ground stop disrupted flights across the country.

At about 9 p.m. ET Saturday, the wing tip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767 as both aircraft were taxiing, according to a statement from the Federal Aviation Administration.

The Copa plane was taxiing to the gate, while the UPS plane was departing for Bogota, Colombia, the FAA said. The Copa flight had six crew members and 166 passengers aboard at the time of the collision, according to a statement from the airline.

Greg Chin, a spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Aviation Department, said in a statement that two people were treated at the scene for minor injuries and were not hospitalized.

The FAA said air traffic controllers had told the UPS crew to give way to the Copa flight.

UPS said in a statement that it was aware of the incident and “committed to working with authorities to determine what happened.” “The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority,” the company said.

The collision came a day after the FAA issued a rare nationwide ground stop because of a widespread air traffic control telecommunications issue. The ground stop lasted more than four hours and led to thousands of flight cancellations and delays. Officials believe a router problem during routine work was the cause of the outage.

As of 10:20 a.m. ET Sunday, 1,583 flights within, into or out of the U.S. had been canceled, and another 2,944 were delayed.

Last year, 15 people were killed when a UPS cargo plane crashed just outside of Louisville, Kentucky’s Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport.

World.title: We want to hear your experience with changes to student loan repayment plans
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” has transformed the sprawling federal student loan system — and student borrowers are feeling the effects of the most consequential changes.

This year, the approximately 7.5 million student borrowers under the Biden-era Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, plan had to select a new one. So far, about 2 million borrowers have done so, after the Education Department warned that the SAVE plan was “illegal” and would be discontinued. The remaining borrowers who did not select a new plan were set to start receiving notices this month informing them that they missed a final deadline and were automatically moved to a new plan.

The Trump administration has said ending the SAVE plan would help streamline repayment programs while ensuring borrowers are paying off what they owe to the federal government. But student advocacy groups fear lower-income borrowers who had benefited from smaller monthly payments — or even qualified to make no payments at all based on their income — will end up with significantly higher bills under the other available plans.

We want to hear from you, whether you’re in this situation or are facing another challenge related to the recent student loan changes. Please share your experience by filling out the form below.
