World.title: Iraq plans to build new airport in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Investment Commission (NIC) announced that it is moving to build a new airport in Baghdad with an annual capacity of 20 million passengers.

Adel al-Yasiri, the chairman of the NIC, said that the commission is currently preparing a site spanning approximately 20 square kilometers near the capital, Baghdad, for the development of one of the largest airports.

With an operating capacity of up to 20 million passengers annually, the project is expected to be managed by large multinational companies and developed through an investment-based strategy.

The project is anticipated to be constructed using an investment-based strategy and operated by major international corporations, with an operational capacity of up to 20 million passengers annually.

According to al-Yasiri, the NIC has put forward proposals for both the development of Baghdad International Airport and the enhancement of Mosul International Airport.

The plans are part of broader efforts to develop infrastructure and enhance Iraq’s capacity to accommodate air traffic, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The Iraqi cabinet announced in late October that it awarded a contract to develop and operate Baghdad International Airport to a consortium comprising Corporacion America Airports and Amwaj International.

The $764 million contract includes the construction of a new terminal designed to handle up to 15 million passengers annually, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The consortium’s plan was chosen as the best offer, with 43.05 percent of the airport’s annual revenue flowing to the national treasury throughout the concession period.

World.title: Iraq crowned Asian Bodybuilding Champions in Thailand with 41 medals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s national bodybuilding team clinched the overall team title at the IFBB Asian Championships in Pattaya, Thailand, on Sunday, November 15, 2026, dominating the continent with a commanding 41-medal haul and 518 total points.

Iraqi Bodybuilding and Fitness Federation President Faez Abdul-Hassan confirmed that Iraq’s delegation—comprising over 40 athletes—secured the top podium spot across the continental standings. The team’s medal tally broke down as follows:

Gold Medals: 9

Silver Medals: 16

Bronze Medals: 16

Iraq finished far ahead of its closest regional rivals in the overall team standings, topping runner-up Oman (174 points) by a margin of 344 points, while the United Arab Emirates secured third place.

Abdul-Hassan praised the technical caliber and preparation of the Iraqi athletes, emphasizing that the victory adds another milestone to Iraq’s sporting record—building directly on the squad’s recent 35-medal showing at the Mr. Universe International Championship in Beirut—and underscores the national team’s sustained regional dominance on international podiums.

World.title: Hajime Moriyasu demands direct talks with IFA chief Younis Mahmoud over Iraq coaching role
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Japanese manager Hajime Moriyasu has set a strict condition for entering negotiations with the Iraqi Football Association (IFA) to take over as head coach of the Iraqi national team, stipulating that all discussions must be conducted directly with him, completely bypassing intermediaries and sports marketing agencies.

IFA President Younis Mahmoud is considering traveling to Japan to hold direct face-to-face talks with Moriyasu to explore reaching a formal agreement, pending final executive approval to initiate the official mission.

The 58-year-old tactician is one of Asian football’s most accomplished coaches, having led Japan’s national squad since 2018. Under his tenure, Japan compiled a record of 78 wins and 15 draws across 112 matches, achieving several major milestones:

2019 AFC Asian Cup: Guided Japan to a runner-up finish.

2022 FIFA World Cup (Qatar): Reached the Round of 16 after securing upset group-stage victories over Germany and Spain.

2023 AFC Asian Cup: Advanced to the quarterfinals.

2026 FIFA World Cup: Led Japan to the Round of 32.

Recent Landmark Victory: Claimed a historic 3–2 friendly win over Brazil in Singapore on November 14, 2026.

Moriyasu is scheduled to conclude his eight-year tenure with the Japan Football Association following their upcoming friendly match against Paraguay on November 17, 2026, having brought forward his departure date in light of the postponement of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup.

World.title: Vodafone Qatar, Iraq’s ITPC sign deal on digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Vodafone Qatar and Iraq’s state-owned Informatics and Telecom Public Company (ITPC) signed a cooperation agreement during Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026.

The deal establishes a framework to explore cross-border telecommunications and digital infrastructure projects.

The agreement was signed last week during the presence of Iraq’s Minister of Communications, Mustafa Sanad.

The framework outlines areas for technical and commercial evaluation rather than immediate, confirmed capital investments. Any resulting projects will require separate binding contracts and full regulatory compliance.

Both entities will evaluate data transit projects running through Iraq alongside fiber infrastructure opportunities.

The partnership seeks to evaluate the joint development of internet exchange points, which will enhance both regional and international internet connectivity.

Both firms will study linking their respective networks to optimize resource usage and streamline cross-border data traffic.

Additionally, technical teams will exchange knowledge on network management and operations to identify commercially viable joint ventures.

ITPC aims to leverage Iraq’s strategic geography to modernize its domestic telecom sector and serve as a major regional hub for data traffic.

The agreement aligns with wider regional infrastructure efforts, including recent partnerships between ITPC and Ooredoo to build digital transit corridors linking Asia, the Gulf, and Europe.

World.title: Zaidi gives Kata’ib Hezbollah end-of-week deadline to vacate Jurf Al Nasr
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi has issued a final ultimatum giving Kata’ib Hezbollah until the end of this week to hand over full security and military control of the Jurf al-Nasr (Jurf al-Sakhar) subdistrict in northern Babylon Governorate to federal forces, warning of an impending military intervention led by the Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) if mediation fails.

According to informed government and political sources, Al-Zaidi conveyed the non-negotiable deadline through intermediaries from the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) and the ruling Coordination Framework.

The Prime Minister warned that if the faction refuses to withdraw peacefully, elite CTS units will be deployed in the coming days to assert full state authority across the entire subdistrict, emphasizing that any party obstructing federal forces will be prosecuted under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law with full backing from the judiciary.

The standoff escalated sharply after Al-Zaidi received the formal findings of the government commission investigating crude oil smuggling in Jurf al-Nasr. The report confirmed extensive pipeline breaches and clandestine oil-refining facilities inside the closed zone, noting that armed elements actively blocked federal investigators from inspecting several restricted sectors.

In immediate response to the commission’s report, the Commander-in-Chief ordered sweeping judicial referrals and administrative dismissals:

Judicial Referrals: Referred all suspects implicated in the smuggling network directly to the judiciary.

Security & Administrative Dismissals: Relieved multiple senior security, military, and administrative officials in Babylon Governorate—including the Provincial Police Chief and senior officers across intelligence agencies, National Security, the Hashd al-Shaabi, Energy Police, and the Oil Pipelines Company.

Maximum Alert Status: Placed military and security formations on Alert Level “C” (Indhar Jim)—Iraq’s highest state of operational readiness—accompanied by troop movements toward northern Babylon and additional Federal Police deployments tightening perimeter checkpoints.

Over recent days, Al-Zaidi held intensive crisis consultations with senior Coordination Framework and Hashd al-Shaabi leaders—including Badr Organization Secretary-General Hadi Al-Amiri, PMF Commission Chairman Falih Al-Fayyadh, and PMF Chief of Staff Abdul-Aziz Al-Muhammadawi (“Abu Fadak”)—who are attempting to broker a peaceful handover to avert an armed clash between state forces and Kata’ib Hezbollah.

Sources also revealed that an earlier federal contingency plan—which had envisioned deploying three brigades from the Shrine Brigades (Quwat al-Atabat), the Third Division of the Federal Police, and CTS detachments—was shelved after its operational axes were leaked, prompting Baghdad to formulate an alternative operation centered directly on elite Counter-Terrorism Service units to retake the entirety of Jurf al-Nasr rather than merely reinforcing outer perimeters.

World.title: 9 Iraqi officials dismissed following investigation into oil smuggling network
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security and administrative officials on Saturday following an investigation into an oil smuggling network in the Jurf al-Sakhr area, ordering those involved to be referred to the judiciary.

The dismissals targeted senior provincial police, intelligence, the National Security Service, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), Energy Police, and Oil Ministry pipeline officials in Babil province. The Babil governor also resigned following earlier denials of the illicit activity.

An official committee confirmed illegal refineries and pipeline tampering via geospatial data.

Reports mentioned that the operation siphoned fuel from strategic pipelines south of Baghdad, accumulating up to $30 million monthly since 2021.

The Jurf al-Sakher area is a key stronghold of the Iran-backed group Kataib Hezbollah.

According to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), intelligence documents with satellite images showed crude oil and oil-derivatives smuggling activities carried out by an armed faction in Jurf al-Sakher. The faction was accused of tapping into a pipeline in the area.

According to Iraq’s military spokesman Sabah al-Numan, the investigating committee confirmed the accuracy of the information.

World.title: Iraq’s oil shipments to Syria’s Baniyas port hit 150,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is transporting between 120,000 and 150,000 barrels of crude oil per day by tanker trucks from its southern oil fields to the Syrian port of Baniyas on the Mediterranean Sea, according to Basim Abdul-Karim, head of the state-owned Basra Oil Company (BOC).

The transport operations began on October 26, using a land route that had seen little use for decades. This move comes as Iraq seeks alternative outlets for its oil exports following disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Qatar-based UCC Holding is handling the transport of the crude under a deal with Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO), according to Abdul-Karim. The daily volume transported depends on the number of tanker trucks available.

UCC Holding has transported approximately 1.6 million barrels from the Tuba field depot near Basra since the agreement went into effect, with hundreds of trucks lining up at the facility to load crude oil before heading toward the Syrian border.

Tanker trucks wait at the Syrian border until they can form a convoy of 100 to 150 vehicles each before continuing their journey to Baniyas, a round trip taking between four and five days.

In Baniyas, the crude oil is loaded onto vessels and transported to refineries across the Mediterranean—including those in Greece, Italy, and Turkey.

Reports indicate that the group plans to load between five million and 14 million barrels of heavy crude over a three-month period, at a discount of $38 per barrel. Under the agreement, the group receives $12 per barrel to cover the costs of trucking and transit across Syria.

World.title: US accuses Iran of plundering Iraq’s resources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Department of State has accused Tehran of employing Iraqi militias—including Kata’ib Hezbollah—to steal Iraq’s resources.

The declaration was made in response to allegations of petroleum product smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakhr area, according to Sky News Arabia.

A spokesperson for the US State Department told the news outlet that Iran has a long history of using Iraqi militias to plunder the country’s resources.

The spokesperson accused these groups of undermining Iraq’s sovereignty and weakening its economy, noting that they use the funds of corruption to serve their interests and those of the regime in Tehran.

Washington has placed sanctions on Kata’ib Hezbollah and designated it as a foreign terrorist organization.

The United States will continue to target entities that generate illicit revenue, as well as those who facilitate their financial transactions, as part of a pressure campaign led by President Donald Trump against Iran.

A document issued by the office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces revealed that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered the formation of a committee to investigate the smuggling of petroleum products in Jurf al-Sakhr—referred to in the document as Jurf al-Nasr.

World.title: Govt healthcare spend up 3x since 2013-14 to 4.1L cr
World.content:
Representative image

Where does the money go

NEW DELHI: Govt spending on healthcare has more than tripled from Rs 1.3 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 4.1 lakh crore in 2023-24, while the share of medical expenses borne directly by households has fallen from 64.2% to 42.7% of total health expenditure over the decade. Despite the decline, families continue to shoulder a substantial burden, paying Rs 4 lakh crore out of their own pockets in 2023-24, according to the latest National Health Accounts (NHA) estimates.The share of govt health expenditure (GHE) in total health expenditure increased from 28.6% to 43.5% during the same period. Per capita govt health spending also rose more than two-and-a-half times, from Rs 1,042 to Rs 2,959, according to NHA 2023-24, which is the eleventh round of health expenditure estimates.The report, which tracks financial flows across the country's healthcare system, estimates India's total health expenditure at Rs 9.52 lakh crore in 2023-24, equivalent to 3.29% of GDP, or Rs 6,801 per person. Of this, current health expenditure accounted for Rs 8.37 lakh crore (87.9%), while capital expenditure stood at Rs 1.15 lakh crore (12.1%).State govts continued to be the largest contributors to public health spending, accounting for nearly 68% of total govt health expenditure, compared with around 32% contributed by Centre.GHE amounted to 1.43% of GDP during 2023-24, said the report prepared by NHA Technical Secretariat under National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC).The estimates also show an increase in social security expenditure on health, which includes govt-funded health insurance schemes, medical reimbursements for govt employees and social health insurance programmes. Its share in total health expenditure rose from 6% in 2013-14 to 11% in 2023-24.Private health insurance expenditure stood at Rs 97,167 crore, accounting for 10.2% of total health expenditure. Expenditure under all govt-financed health insurance schemes combined was Rs 33,385 crore.An analysis of where healthcare money is spent shows that private hospitals accounted for 31.91% of current health expenditure, against 16.77% for govt hospitals. Pharmacies accounted for another 20.6%, with expenditure amounting to Rs 1.72 lakh crore.Pharmaceutical expenditure, including prescribed and over-the-counter medicines and drugs supplied during inpatient and outpatient treatment, accounted for 30.2% of current health expenditure.Primary care accounted for around 46% of current health expenditure, followed by secondary care at around 35% and tertiary care at 14%.

World.title: Kashmir film fraternity trains guns on Bollywood’s ‘AK-47 & skullcap’ stereotype, seeks own industry
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Kashmiri movie veterans have shined a harsh light on Bollywoodâs trite scripts confining J&Kâs depiction to âscenic beauty, skullcaps that few in the Valley actually wear and AK-47s carried under pherans and long beardsâ, while calling for strengthening indigenous filmmaking.

Speakers reeled off such gripes at a seminar organised in Srinagar on Saturday by Kashmir Music Club, run by popular singer Waheed Jeelani.

âWe have stronger stories here and there is a need to develop them,â actor Umar Imtiyaz said as he took potshots at Bollywood for dishing out its familiar fare of âskullcaps, long beards and AK-47s under pherans (long, loose-fitting garments worn by Kashmiris in winter)â. Imtiyaz argued that it was time to challenge such stereotypical representations.



Echoing the sentiment, filmmaker Ayash Arif called for a focus on regional cinema that blends local concerns with a broader global outlook. He criticised J&K govtâs film policy, arguing it was more of a tourism blueprint aimed at encouraging filmmakers from elsewhere to shoot in the region due to its scenic beauty. What is needed, Arif said, is a roadmap aimed at promoting local productions.

The 2022 policy offers several initiatives, including a single-window portal for shooting permissions and subsidies.





It recalls the heady 1960s when blockbusters like Kashmir Ki Kali, Jab Jab Phool Khile, Himalay Ki God Mein and Janwar were shot in Srinagar and Gulmarg, followed by some international productions such as The Razorâs Edge in the 1980s.

At the seminar, however, many felt the policy does not address requirements back home. âThere is a lot for outside filmmakers in the policy but not much for local makers,â Arif said.

World.title: Kishtwar BJP leader questions Shagun Parihar’s mosque claim, Muslim body seeks public apology
World.content:
Shagun Parihar, BJP candidate from Kishtwar.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Kishtwar BJP leader Jahanzaib Sirwal on Sunday questioned party MLA Shagun Parihar's claim that announcements were made from a mosque before two SPOs were killed in Kishtwar's Dachhan area, calling the allegation "deeply unfortunate and factually unsubstantiated".The Islami Markaz-e-Majlis Shura Kishtwar, headed by Jamia Masjid Imam Maulana Farooq Ahmad Kichloo also rejected the MLA's claim as baseless and demanded a public apology. The organisation said unverified allegations against religious institutions could disturb communal harmony in the sensitive district.SPOs Babi Chand, 57, and Rashpal Kumar, 45, both residents of Kishtwar, were found dead in a forest area in Dachhan early Thursday. They had gone missing a day earlier while travelling to a security post at Basnand in the adjoining Marwah tehsil.Parihar made the claim in a video recorded on the sidelines of a wreath-laying ceremony for the two slain personnel. She questioned why those responsible had not been arrested and alleged that information was being leaked from the area."Why have those involved not been apprehended yet? Announcements were made from a mosque.Someone must be passing on information, and leaking intelligence from here. Our people are being selectively targeted and killed," the MLA alleged, PTI reported.Objecting to the remarks, Sirwal said religious institutions should not be linked to provocative announcements or slogans without credible evidence."As a proud member of the Muslim community, I strongly object to attempts to bring religious institutions into narratives that can create mistrust and suspicion among communities. Mosques are centres of faith, worship and spiritual guidance, and their sanctity must be respected," he said.Sirwal also criticised a recent statement by leader of opposition in the J&K Assembly Sunil Sharma, who linked the killings to alleged attempts at the ethnic cleansing of a particular community."Such an alarming assertion, without credible substantiation, risks creating unnecessary fear and insecurity among people. Communities in the region have been living together peacefully, and statements of this nature can undermine that trust."Using such sensitive issues to generate political mileage and deepen communal divisions is deeply unfortunate and must be avoided," Sirwal said.He urged public representatives to exercise caution while commenting on sensitive issues, saying sweeping allegations against religious institutions or communities could deepen divisions."Terrorism has no religion, and violence cannot be given a religious identity. Our collective fight must be against those who perpetrate violence, not against any particular community."Political discourse must be guided by facts, responsibility and mutual respect rather than statements that risk alienating communities," he added.Kichloo said Kishtwar was a sensitive region and attempts to create mistrust between communities through unverified allegations were irresponsible and unacceptable.He said the organisation had always condemned terrorism and violence, including attacks on the Amarnath Yatra."We have always condemned terrorism and every act of violence, including the attacks on the Amarnath Yatra. We have never supported any killing or act of violence, irrespective of who the victim or perpetrator may be," Kichloo said after a meeting of the Majlis.He said the administration and security agencies were capable of investigating the incident and establishing the facts. He urged Parihar not to make statements that could disturb peace in the district."If the MLA has concrete evidence, she should clearly identify the mosque from where the alleged announcement was made or disclose who made it. The administration and several security agencies are working on the ground. Are we to believe that none of them had any knowledge of such an incident?" Kichloo asked.The organisation also called for a thorough and impartial investigation and strict action against anyone found guilty."We consider her (Perihar) our daughter and respect her. However, levelling allegations without substantiating them is neither responsible nor acceptable. She should withdraw these allegations and tender a public apology," Kichloo said."We do not wish to prolong or politicise this issue. Our only concern is that peace, brotherhood and communal harmony in Kishtwar must not be compromised for the sake of unverified claims," he added.

World.title: Launching new anti-anaemia strategy without enough evidence could waste public funds, warn experts
World.content:
Experts are questioning India's push for double-fortified salt to fight anaemia, citing limited evidence and the risk of overlooking wider causes of iron deficiency. (AI-generated image)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

From fortification of rice with iron, as the focus shifts to double fortification of salt (DFS) with iron and iodine in a bid to tackle high incidence of anaemia, several public health experts have sounded a warning against introducing any intervention without enough evidence. The new national anaemia prevalence data is yet to be made public though the survey was completed in November 2025.In response to an RTI application, the National Institute of Nutrition had stated in September that the analysis of the data from the Diet and Biomarkers Survey of India (DABS-I) launched in December 2022 and completed three years later is still under progress. The DABS-I survey, now renamed Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), has used venous blood samples or samples drawn from veins, said to be the gold standard to estimate anaemia. DABS-I, which covers only 2.6 lakh people in the survey, will give state level prevalence, unlike NFHS with a sample size of seven lakh, which gives district-level data.However, with the data from the survey not being made public, India has no anaemia data since the last NFHS survey in 2019-21. That NFHS survey showed an increase in anaemia over the last survey in 2115-16. The government rejected the anaemia data from the 2019-21 survey on the grounds that it used blood samples drawn from the tip of the finger, which studies have shown to be unreliable.The Comprehensive National Nutrition Survey (CNNS) of 2016-18 used venous blood samples. It showed lower prevalence of anaemia than the 2019-21 survey which was attributed to using venous blood samples. DABS-I/SAMPADAâs anaemia data, comparable to the CNNS survey data, is expected to show even lower prevalence. It could show whether areas where distribution of iron fortified rice was done successfully have witnessed significant reduction in anaemia prevalence.Tamil Nadu was a pioneer in distributing DFS through the school midday programme starting from 2004. Within a few years, it was expanded to include the public distribution system (PDS) and Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS). Yet, the NFH surveys of 2015-16 and of 2020-21 showed that more than 50% children and women of all ages in the state were anaemic. Over a quarter had moderate anaemia, while 3.5% of women and 1.8% of children up to 5 years were severely anaemic. While Tamil Naduâs anaemia incidence is low compared to many northern states, it is much higher than in states like Odisha, Jharkhand, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh, according to the CNNS survey. Almost 41% of children in the 1-4 year age group and over 20% in the 5-9 year age group were iron deficient in TN, which is higher than the national incidence, showed the CNN survey.In 2017, DFS distribution started in Uttar Pradesh. A study funded by the Gates Foundation was conducted in May 2020 to ascertain evidence of effectiveness in use of DFS in large-scale programmes. It found that only two (Etawah and Auraiya) of the five intervention districts met the evaluability threshold of 50% DFS utilization. The study found that there was no difference in anaemia and iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) prevalence or in mean haemoglobin concentration between women of reproductive age in intervention and comparison districts. It concluded that DFS was effective in reducing risk of iron deficiency, but not anaemia or iron deficiency anaemia, among women of reproductive age. Some of the modest efficacy was attributed to supply chain interruptions over the course of the implementation period.Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat introduced DFS in PDS and ICDS in 2018. Despite an impact evaluation claiming high DFS uptake exceeding 90% in the two states, the NFHS-5 survey, which took place from January 2020 to April 2021 in Madhya Pradesh, two years after introduction of DFS in June 2018, found that the overall prevalence of anaemia in children (aged 6 months to below 5 years) had increased from 69% in the previous NFHS survey to 73%, of which 42% were moderately anaemic, while 3% were severely anaemic. About 27% of adult women had moderate anaemia, and 2% had severe anaemia. However, a survey in March 2021 to gauge the impact of DFS introduction commissioned by an international NGO, Nutrition International, which supports the introduction of DFS, claimed that there was a six-percentage point reduction in anaemia prevalence in the districts where baseline prevalence had been measured in 2018. Nutrition Internationalâs website states that it is working with state governments âto increase the availability of fortified foods in social safety net programsâ which means publicly funded programmes, where poor purchasing power of the consumers would not be a hurdle to DFS uptake.There is enough evidence to show that only about half the cases of anaemia are due to iron deficiency. Anaemia can also be caused by malaria, hookworms and other such worm infestation, other nutritional deficiencies, chronic infections, and genetic conditions. Apart from these, it can be caused by socio-economic factors such as underage or early marriage, adolescent pregnancy, untreated excessive blood loss during menstruation and under-nutrition.Even the governmentâs targeted intervention to address anaemia among pregnant women by ensuring consumption of iron folic acid, distributed for free as supplements, has done poorly. Over half the pregnant women in India consumed iron and folic acid for 100 days and less than 38% consumed it for 180 days, according to the 2023-24 NFHS. In high fertility states like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, the share of pregnant women who took iron and folic acid was even smaller.âVery little is being done to address food availability, diversity and affordability; minimum wages; equitable land distribution; better employment and job opportunities; or even to make nutrient dense foods available at low costs or as subsidies. Fortification will only increase food costs and dependence on corporations, while reducing the shelf life of foods and taking away food sovereignty from communities,â said Dr Sylvia Karpagam, a public health expert, and Dr Veena Shatrugna, former deputy director of the National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) and Steering Committee Member of the Right to Food Campaign, in a statement flagging the problems with the universal use of DFS in social safety net programmes such as ICDS and the midday meal scheme.The government has already spent about Rs 2,700 crore on rice fortification every year for several years. Public health experts cautioned against one more universal scheme that could waste thousands of crores of rupees of public funds, which could be utilised for more localised evidence-backed interventions.

World.title: Punjab BJP forms manifesto, 'chargesheet' committees; Raghav Chadha, Harbhajan Singh among members
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Sunday constituted two committees ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, naming senior leaders to panels tasked with preparing the party's manifesto and a "chargesheet".

and former cricketer Harbhajan Singh are among the members of the manifesto committee, which will be headed by senior BJP leader Avinash Rai Khanna.

The panel also includes Manpreet Singh Badal, Ashwani Sharma, Manoranjan Kalia, Som Parkash, Rana Gurmeet Singh Sodhi, Ashwani Sekhri, Satnam Singh Sandhu, Rajinder Gupta, Parampal Kaur and HS Phoolka, according to a party statement.

Former Punjab chief Sunil Jakhar will lead the chargesheet committee.



Its members include Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Vijay Sampla, Shwet Malik, Maharani Preneet Kaur, Ravneet Singh Bittu, Dinesh Babbu, Sushil Rinku, Geja Ram, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Ashok Mittal, Sandeep Pathak, SS Channi and Jagmeet Singh Brar.

The BJP said the manifesto committee brings together experienced leaders from different fields to contribute to drafting its election document. Senior leaders in the chargesheet panel have also been assigned specific responsibilities.

World.title: 'Well-planned conspiracy': BJP refutes reports of 209-candidate list for upcoming UP elections
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Uttar Pradesh unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (

) on Sunday rejected reports claiming that a list of 209 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections had been prepared and sent to the party's central leadership, calling them fabricated and part of a "well-planned conspiracy".

"For the past few days, certain media outlets, individuals, and institutions have been continuously circulating news regarding an alleged list of 209 candidates of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Uttar Pradesh, being prepared and sent to the central leadership in the context of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. This is completely untrue, baseless, imaginary, and fabricated. The BJP outrightly refutes this fake and false news," news agency ANI quoted the statement as saying.



Describing the reports as a "well-planned conspiracy", the statement alleged that some people were spreading rumours to create confusion, uncertainty and fear among party workers. It urged office-bearers, workers and the public not to rely on unverified reports and to follow information shared through authorised party platforms.

The party said its candidate selection process had not yet begun. It added that the BJP follows a structured organisational process for choosing candidates for assembly and other elections.





The joint statement was signed by chief minister Yogi Adityanath and state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary.

Earlier on Sunday, Chaudhary had also denied that the BJP had finalised names for 209 constituencies. Speaking to reporters, he said he had not held any meetings to prepare such a list.

âI do not know the source of this news... As the State President of the Bharatiya Janata Party, I have not held any such meetings with anyone,â Chaudhary said.

He outlined the party's candidate selection procedure, saying inputs are first collected at the district and regional levels before being discussed by the state core committee and election committee. The recommendations are then sent to Delhi, where the Parliamentary Board takes the final call.

âThe BJP is not a family-run party where a single individual can make such decisions; rather, the process is entirely collective,â he said.

Chaudhary added that the party had followed the same organisational approach for the past 50 years, with decisions taken through consultation and consensus.

World.title: Chhath Puja: Despite politics over Yamuna, Delhi stretch of river continues to be polluted
World.content:
Despite the political slugfest over the Yamuna during yet another Chhath Puja, official data show that the river’s Delhi stretch remains heavily polluted for most of the year, with water quality improving during the monsoon, when floodwaters flush out pollutants.

According to official data, the faecal coliform level (microbes from human and animal excreta) in the Yamuna at Asgarpur, where the river leaves the Capital, was 660 times the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) desirable limit for bathing water quality in May, before the monsoon. The water quality improved in September, as it does every year after the monsoon. The Delhi government has yet to make the October data public.

Religious significance

The Yamuna holds religious significance for people from Purvanchal (residents of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar), who constitute a significant voter base in Delhi. Many observe Chhath Puja by taking a dip in the river.

Scores of devotees offered prayers at Kalindi Kunj in south Delhi on Sunday evening, standing knee-deep in the river as toxic froth floated on the water — a familiar sight during Chhath Puja.

Since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in February 2025, an ambitious plan to divert water from the Ganga to flush out pollutants from the Delhi stretch of the Yamuna has been under discussion. However, it has yet to yield any concrete results.

The proposal formed part of a broader plan to clean the river, which was presented to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in April last year. Following his approval, Union Home Minister Amit Shah has held several review meetings on the plan, according to sources.

“Even if the plan is finalised, it will take about two to three years for Ganga water to reach Delhi. A detailed project report (DPR) has been submitted to the government, but it will be hard to give a deadline to the project at this time,” an official told The Hindu, requesting anonymity.

Under the current plan, the government proposes to divert about 500 cusecs of Ganga water from the Upper Ganga Canal (UGC), the largest canal carrying Ganga water through western Uttar Pradesh, into the Delhi stretch of the Yamuna at Wazirabad.

This is the second Ganga water diversion plan being considered by the Delhi government, after the initial proposal was dropped following objections from its counterpart in Uttar Pradesh, according to officials.

Addressing the issue

Experts have long maintained that cleaning the river requires both increasing its flow and curbing the sources of pollution entering it. To address the latter, Mr. Shah, after chairing a review meeting on the Yamuna clean-up plan in July last year, directed the Delhi government to nearly double its sewage treatment capacity to 1,500 MGD by 2028.

To augment sewage treatment capacity, the government this year awarded contracts for the construction of 29 decentralised sewage treatment plants (DSTPs). The plants are targeted for completion by January 2028. However, a Delhi Jal Board (DJB) official said, “All 29 of them are estimated to be completed by January 2028, and some of them will be finished even before this. The construction of the sewer network for these DSTPs is expected to be completed by June 2028.”

Crucial role

DSTPs are considered crucial to cleaning the Yamuna, as they are expected to treat sewage generated in several unauthorised colonies that currently flow into the river because of the lack of sewer networks.

The DSTP work has been pending for years, with the non-availability of land emerging as a major hurdle. The issue was compounded by a tussle between the previous Aam Aadmi Party government in Delhi and the BJP-led Centre, as much of the required land is under the Centre’s control.

“Other projects are under way to increase the treatment capacity of sewage and all of them are expected to be completed before December 2028. It will definitely improve the water quality,” the above-cited official said.

Cleaning the Yamuna was one of Mr. Modi’s key promises in the lead-up to the 2025 Delhi Assembly election, which the BJP won after 27 years.

This year, too, in the run-up to Chhath Puja, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) traded charges over the Yamuna’s pollution. The BJP government inaugurated a cruise service on the river’s upper stretch in Delhi, where the water has traditionally been cleaner, and accused the AAP of doing little to clean the river.

AAP hit back, saying the discovery of dead fish in the river showed that it remained polluted and accusing the BJP of misleading people by claiming that it had cleaned the Yamuna.

History of missed warnings

The Yamuna originates in the Yamunotri glacier in the Himalayas and flows through Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh before joining the Ganga.

In 1994, the Supreme Court took cognisance of a newspaper article titled “Quiet Flows Maily (dirty) Yamuna” and summoned the CPCB to explain the river’s condition. Later, various stakeholders, including the Delhi government, the DJB, civic bodies, and the governments of Uttar Pradesh and Haryana, became parties to the case.

In a landmark judgment on January 13, 2015, in a case filed by Manoj Misra, a former Indian Forest Service officer, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) formulated the ‘Maily se Nirmal Yamuna Revitalisation Plan, 2017’, which was to be completed by March 31, 2017. But that did not happen.

In July 2018, the NGT formed a monitoring panel headed by two retired bureaucrats, primarily to implement its 2015 judgment. The NGT dissolved the committee in January 2021 and directed the Chief Secretaries of various States to monitor progress.

In 2023, the BJP-led Central government appointed a committee headed by the then Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, V.K. Saxena, to clean the river, but it made little progress.

World.title: Eight injured as building collapses during hotel construction in Delhi’s Paharganj
World.content:
Eight people were injured after a portion of a building collapsed while the roof slab of its second floor was being laid in central Delhi’s Paharganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

The incident took place at property numbers 3992–3993 in Kasheruwalan, Sangatrashan, opposite Government Girls Senior Secondary School. The injured were taken to Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital. Some have suffered fractures, while others sustained minor injuries.

Preliminary inspection found that the supporting columns were wet and the building appeared to have tilted. Police are examining the circumstances leading to the collapse.

World.title: CIAL sets up facilitation centre for Sabarimala pilgrims
World.content:
Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL) has set up a dedicated pilgrim facilitation centre at the airport for Sabarimala pilgrims. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the centre on November 17.

Spread across 5,000 sq. ft., the centre is located near the police aid post, adjacent to the domestic arrival terminal and will remain open round the clock. KSRTC bus services are available to and from the airport from here, with a booking counter set up at the centre. Pilgrims can also book chartered bus services on demand. A dedicated counter for helicopter service bookings has also been arranged.

The other facilities at the centre include a Devaswom help desk, prasadam coupon counter, prepaid taxi booking facility, vegetarian food outlet, and a rest area. A flight information display system has also been installed to provide real-time flight updates. Its proximity to the domestic terminal makes the centre easily accessible to pilgrims, says an official release.

Around 11,000 pilgrims made use of the facilitation centre last year, including those from Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Malaysia, and Singapore, it says.

World.title: Boy electrocuted by snapped stay wire in Malappuram; Minister orders probe
World.content:
A 13-year-old boy died of electrocution after coming into contact with a snapped stay wire attached to an electric pole in a paddy field in Malappuram on Sunday (November 15).

The deceased, identified as Junaid, son of Shihabudheen of Cherumukku in Tirurangadi, had gone to the field with friends to watch a tractor plough the land, the police said.

Residents said Junaid’s friends tried to rescue him, but the tractor driver stopped them from approaching the wire, saving them from a similar fate. They alleged that officials of the Keralam State Electricity Board (KSEB) took time to disconnect the power supply despite repeated calls for help.

The incident triggered protests by residents who accused KSEB officials of serious negligence.

Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph ordered an immediate inquiry into the incident and directed officials to ensure compensation for the bereaved family.

In a statement, Mr. Joseph said that he had directed the Deputy Chief Engineer of KSEB, Tirurangadi, to submit a factual report immediately. “Strict disciplinary action will be taken against those found responsible for any lapse,” he added.

The Minister said safety inspections would be intensified across the State to prevent the recurrence of such incidents.

Meanwhile, the KSEB, in a statement, apologised for the incident and said that an impartial and detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the accident would be conducted.

The KSEB urged consumers to report electricity-related safety hazards by sending photographs and details through WhatsApp to 94960-10101.

World.title: 18-year-old woman murdered in Moti Nagar store trial room; brother-in-law arrested
World.content:
An 18-year-old woman was found murdered inside the trial room of a clothing store in west Delhi’s Moti Nagar on Saturday evening. Delhi Police has arrested her 23-year-old brother-in-law following an overnight operation involving multiple teams.

The deceased, identified as Shabnam, worked at Vastraa Mahal in Moti Nagar and was alone inside the store when the accused, Suraj, entered. An argument broke out between them, following which he allegedly pushed her into the trial room, around 10–15 feet from the counter, and attacked her with a sharp-edged weapon, the police said. Her throat had been slit, and a blood-stained knife was recovered near the body.

Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (West) Saurabh Chandra said the incident was reported around 5.30 p.m., though a PCR call was received only at 8.50 p.m. The call was made by the owner of a store opposite Vastraa Mahal, where Shabnam had allegedly worked before joining the clothing store around three months ago.

The police examined CCTV footage from inside the showroom and the surrounding area to identify the accused. Eight to 10 teams, led by the Station House Officer and assisted by the ACP Operations team, were deployed to trace him.

“An intensive operation was conducted throughout the night. The teams worked on developing technical surveillance and manual intelligence, based on which we apprehended the accused from Delhi. Further interrogation will help establish the motive behind the murder,” Mr. Chandra said on Sunday.

Shabnam was the youngest of three sisters. Her two elder sisters were married to two brothers from the accused’s family. Suraj is the younger brother of their husbands.

The victim’s father alleged that the two families had been embroiled in a dispute for around 18 months. He said that although they had reached a compromise in May, relations remained strained, with the accused’s family stopping communication with them.

“We found out at 9 p.m. that our daughter had been killed in the shop. Suraj killed her. We demand that all six people in the family be punished. There was a fight between the families one-and-a-half years ago. After the compromise in May, we signed a settlement as our two daughters were married into that family. However, they stopped talking to us,” he said.

The police are questioning the accused to ascertain the motive and circumstances leading to the murder.

World.title: My entire life has been a struggle, says Bilkis Bano at GIO conference in Kochi
World.content:
“My entire life has been a struggle,” Bilkis Bano, the Gujarat riots survivor who has emerged as an icon of resilience with her prolonged legal battle for justice, said in Kochi on Sunday (November 15).

Ms. Bano made the compelling remark as she inaugurated the International Conference on Women organised by the State committee of the Girls Islamic Organisation (GIO) in the city.

“Everyone knows my life story, don’t they? There is no need to say anything more about it,” she said in a brief address. Ms. Bano was gang-raped and lost seven members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, in the 2002 riots.

Thanking those who invited her, she said, “May we continue to live with such love and peace every day, staying together all our lives.”

Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage. “The family had to relocate several times, and her rights were denied. They had to repeatedly bring instances of injustice to the attention of those in positions of power. What happened to Bilkis is now known to the entire world. May her struggle inspire every woman to find the strength to raise her voice for her rights,” he said.

The conference was presided over by GIO State president K. Shifana. Jamia Millia Islamia student leader Nousheen Farooq was the chief guest.

Saria Cheruvallil, Professor at Coventry University, UK; Dalia Saleh, researcher at the University of Cambridge; Reem Mahmoud Al Haddad, Palestinian writer and journalist; Jamaat-e-Islami national secretary A. Rahmathunnisa; and Jamaat-e-Islami Keralam ameer P. Mujeeb Rahman were among those who spoke at various sessions.

World.title: Prince William, Princess Kate to meet Modi in New Delhi this week
World.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Katherine (Kate), are due to arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening (November 17) at a ceremony in the city. The couple will stay in Mumbai for the duration of their visit, which ends on Wednesday night (November 18, 2026).

Also read: Royal couple take guard, Mumbai bowled out

The visit will involve events focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly,​ Brian Lara and England captain ​Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by Prince William in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crores) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.

India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s (November 17, 2026) event .

When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest of 15,000 schools across 24 States.

This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India and Princess Kate’s first major overseas trip since she was treated for cancer in 2024 and had to step back from official duties.

World.title: Guest teachers in Haryana hold mock Assembly, demand regularisation
World.content:
Guest teachers in Haryana schools held a mock Assembly at the Mini Secretariat in Kurukshetra on Saturday, demanding regularisation under the three-year policy notified in 2014 in accordance with court orders.

Organised on the call of the Rajkiya Anubandhit Adhyapak Sangh, the symbolic Assembly passed a resolution seeking regularisation of guest teachers by an overwhelming majority. The resolution will be submitted to Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini at his camp office in Kurukshetra on November 29. The teachers will also hold a rally in Delhi on December 12 and submit the resolution to the President.

Teachers said guest teachers had been serving in government schools for the past 21 years and contributing to the State’s education system, but the government continued to keep them in temporary employment arrangements instead of regularising their services. Following the court orders, the Haryana School Education Department issued speaking orders denying regular status to the guest teachers.

They said the mock Assembly was organised to raise questions concerning the regularisation of guest teachers, judicial decisions and the government’s accountability on a public platform.

The event was attended by educationists, intellectuals, employee union leaders from various departments, School Management Committee representatives, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, student and youth organisations, advocates’ unions, writers’ associations, university professors, the Jan Sangharsh Manch, Kurukshetra, and social activists.

These teachers, appointed between 2005 and 2008, are working as junior basic teachers, trained graduate teachers, and post graduate teachers.

World.title: Asif hopeful of consensus on new provinces, says it will bring 'progressive' change in political landscape
World.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Sunday said the country’s political landscape would change in a progressive way if a consensus was reached on the matter of creating new provinces.

The defence minister made the remarks in an interview on Geo News programme ‘Naya Pakistan’ with Shahzad Iqbal. He was asked about reports that discussions were taking place on generating a broader consensus for creating new provinces, referring to two recent high-level meetings involving the president.

Asif replied that he had no inside information on the matter and “even if there was, obviously I cannot spill it on a show”. However, he said his personal assessment was that all the consultations were heading in the direction suggested by the anchor — consensus on new provinces.

“Consensus is being developed on the issue,” the minister said, adding that the process had been ongoing for the past several weeks.

“In my opinion, the political landscape will change very progressively if this consensus is built and these [new] provinces are created,” he added.

On Thursday night, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had called on President Asif Ali Zardari, who then met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday. The Presidency had refuted reports that President Zardari and Naqvi spoke about matters related to provinces.

While an official statement from the meeting between the president and premier said the country’s political situation came under discussion, official sources privy to the development told Dawn that both leaders agreed to “strictly adhere to constitutional provisions” governing the creation of new provinces or administrative units.

The sources said President Zardari and PM Shehbaz also held a brief one-on-one meeting to discuss a message reportedly conveyed to the president by Naqvi during his Nawabshah visit.

Speaking on Sunday, Asif said he believed it would not take long to reach a consensus and the process was “moving towards culmination”.

He added that he did not know the method of this culmination, declining to comment on whether there was likely to be a referendum on the subject in the National Assembly as it could create “complications”.

According to sources, President Zardari and PM Shehbaz have agreed that the Parliament could not be bypassed in deciding whether a referendum should be held and what questions should be put to the public. Naqvi, who ignited the political storm on new provinces in July, has termed holding a referendum as the solution to the debate.

Asked about impressions that the push for new provinces was coming from certain quarters, Asif stated that this was not true as far as his advocacy for new provinces was concerned.

“I have been saying for years that there should be a robust local governance system,” he said. “How long will we avoid this?”

He added, “I think this will be good for all provinces, for Pakistan […] this is a very healthy thing. In all changes that have come before (in previous governments), there was never so much effort to build consensus on major changes.”

On the lack of clarity regarding the situation, he added that until a direction on several matters was indicated, he did not want to share the details in the public realm.

He also expressed his personal opinion that “the new year will see the new system, God-willing”, adding that the process will “take some shape in 2026”.

‘Space can be given to create consensus’

Asif further remarked that there was “no need for anyone to feel politically threatened” by the idea of new provinces, as political ethos was not static and continued to change.

He further regretted that the changes brought by the 18th Amendment regarding local governments had not been implemented.

The PPP leadership has appeared unwilling to soften its position on new provinces, particularly in Sindh. The party has consistently invoked a unanimous resolution passed by the Sindh Assembly opposing the province’s division, maintaining that it reinforces its position against any such move.

Commenting on this, Asif gave his opinion that consensus was still being developed on the situation and it should not be cast in a negative light.

He also said that space would be given in minor matters to political parties in order to create this consensus in a “quid pro quo” sense and no one would have the decision “forced” on them.

Asked whether such an effort was being made for PTI founder Imran Khan, Asif alluded to the possibility that, if he were to agree to the new system, the developments could create a “window of opportunity” for the jailed ex-PM to return to mainstream politics afterwards.

Providing his “political advice”, the PML-N leader said Imran should not resist the idea as he did not have any “fundamental objection” to new provinces.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah has voiced opposition to the division of Sindh into smaller provinces — although, he said on Wednesday, the PPP had no objection to the creation of new provinces in other parts of the country if their people so desired.

He stated that the division of Sindh was “neither legally nor politically acceptable, as the people of the province had repeatedly rejected the idea through their elected representatives”.

The defence minister recently argued that Pakistan could have as many as 12 provinces if the exercise was guided by administrative requirements rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations.

He maintained that the country’s growing population necessitated smaller administrative units capable of delivering public services more efficiently.

However, the PML-N has so far refrained from articulating a formal policy, saying it will present its position when the matter comes before Parliament.

World.title: In call with Fazl, Bilawal condemns 'govt actions, political vengeance' against JUI-F
World.content:
SWABI/CHARSADDA: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday spoke to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

The telephone conversation comes as tensions have remained high between the JUI-F chief and the PML-N-led federal government over the past month. On Sunday, Fazl’s party also held street protests in several cities of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa against “propaganda” directed toward the party and its leadership.

According to a statement issued by PPP, Bilawal and Fazl exchanged views on the country’s political situation.

The Bhutto scion — whose PPP is an ally of the ruling coalition — “condemned the government’s actions and political vengeance” targeting the JUI-F.

“The government should tolerate the opposition’s criticism,” Bilawal was quoted as saying in the statement. He highlighted that the opposition had an “extremely important role in democracy and a parliamentary system”.

Speaking to Fazl, Bilawal said the “government should refrain from such actions that weaken democracy and the Parliament”.

The PPP chairman has recently been calling for political unity in the country, urging the prime minister to take measures to build trust with the government’s allies and the opposition.

“Via this reset, political parties will have to work together instead of fighting,” he said on Nov 10, days after he urged the federal government to engage all political and social stakeholders rather than “fighting everyone”, including Fazl.

The past month has witnessed exchanges of harsh remarks between Fazl and federal ministers, after the JUI-F chief accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

These developments came after Fazl joined the opposition in criticising the Centre’s imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in the PTI-ruled KP. He also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

On its part, the Centre has repeatedly cited the KP government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the counterterrorism fight for its decision, following which the PPP’s governor now heads the provincial administration.

On Oct 16, without naming anyone, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had claimed that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship”.

The next day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry rebuked Fazl directly, who later clarified his criticism was aimed at policies, not state institutions.

The row played out in the Parliament as well, where Fazl questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at a meeting of the Makkah pact countries and Iran in Tehran.

In his response the next day, the interior minister explained his participation and went on to assail the JUI-F for “continuously crossing the line” and accused it of “extracting wealth from the state”.

JUI-F holds protests across KP

JUI-F has decried “baseless and fake propaganda” against Fazl, accused the federal government of resorting to cheap tactics, and questioned actions being taken as part of the anti-encroachment drive in KP.

To protest the actions, the party took to the streets in various KP cities, sharing purported videos of its gatherings in Peshawar, Lower Dir, Shangla, Hangu, Swabi, Battagram and Lakki Marwat.

In Swabi, JUI-F workers staged a protest at Karnal Sher Khan Chowk despite a fresh ban on gatherings imposed under Section 144 across the district.

JUI-F district leader Maulana Fazal Ali contended that the ban was imposed by the district administration soon after midnight to scuttle the party’s plan to hold the planned protest demonstrations.

“We demand from the government that Maulana Fazlur Rehman, our beloved leader, madressahs and religious individuals should not be targeted. The browbeating tactics used by the government should be immediately given up,” he stressed.

A demonstration also took place at Maulana Hassan Jan Shaheed Chowk in Charsadda, where local party leaders alleged that drone surveillance was being carried out of Fazl’s residence.

The demonstration was attended by party workers and local leaders. However, the absence of the district leadership from the protest also became a subject of discussion among participants.

JUI Charsadda tehsil president Maulana Hashim, Maulana Tahmeedullah and other leaders addressed the gathering.

Late last month, the Directorate of Building Control (City) of the Capital Development Authority issued a warning notice to remove the guards’ room set up outside Fazl’s residence in Islamabad’s G-6 sector within 15 days.

Fazl’s son Asad Mehmood claimed the notice was retaliatory and expressed concern over the “transformation of political differences into personal revenge”.

Earlier this month, the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoned Mehmood, a former federal minister for communication, for alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 term. Mehmood skipped two NAB summons notices and did not appear before its investigation team.

On Nov 6, the JUI-F staged protests in different parts of Sindh and Balochistan, decrying what it called a “coordinated character assassination campaign” against its chief.

World.title: Islamabad hosts foreign dignitaries for two-day ECO ministerial meeting
World.content:
Foreign dignitaries arrived in Islamabad on Sunday as Pakistan hosts the two-day 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers, starting today.

Currently, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyz Republic and Uzbekistan are part of the ECO.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar hosted a welcome dinner in honour of the foreign ministers and heads of delegations of the member states in Islamabad ahead of the meeting, the Foreign Office (FO) said on social media.

He warmly welcomed the delegates and wished them productive deliberations while highlighting the close bonds among ECO member states, the FO said.

Addressing the gathering, DPM Dar also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to “regional cooperation and advancing shared aspirations for peace, progress and prosperity”.

Alongside the visiting delegations, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Parliamentary Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhary, representatives of the ECO secretariat, members of the diplomatic corps, and senior officials of the foreign ministry were also in attendance, FO added.

Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Turkish Deputy Foreign Minister Musa Kulaklikaya, and Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy FM Kairat Erkinovich Tursunkulov are among those in Islamabad for the meeting.

Azeri Deputy FM Elnur Mammadov, Kazakh Deputy FM Arman Issagaliyev, and Turkmenistan’s FM Rashid Meredov also arrived in the federal capital today.

At night, Iran’s FM Abbas Araghchi also landed in Islamabad for the moot, Iran’s state media reported.

Upon his arrival, Meredov, who is also the deputy chairman of Turkmenistan’s cabinet of ministers, was received by Pakistan’s Ambassador to Turkmenistan and other officials, the FO said.

The foreign minister of Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Tahsin Ertugruloglu, had landed in Pakistan on Saturday for the meeting.

According to APP, incumbent ECO Secretary General Asad Majeed Khan chaired a meeting on the draft agenda of the 30th ECO-COM.

This gathering of senior officials from ECO member states was set to review the organisation’s activities and programmes, assess the work of its subsidiary bodies and finalise the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the ministers.

Monday’s ministerial meeting will be chaired by DPM Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies.

Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, will seek to advance the organisation’s objectives under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”, the FO said in a statement on Saturday.

It said Pakistan’s chairmanship would focus on strengthening regional connectivity and integration, deepening partnerships and promoting collective efforts for economic prosperity and sustainable development.

The chairmanship would also provide an opportunity to strengthen the ECO’s role as a platform for regional cooperation, dialogue and economic collaboration, it added.

According to the FO, Pakistan also aims to position itself as a regional connectivity hub, facilitate logistics supply chains and help shape the agenda for regional trade.

The efforts would help unlock the region’s economic potential and translate the benefits of regional cooperation into tangible improvements in the lives of people in ECO member states, the statement said.

Dar meets ECO, OIC, CICA heads

On the sidelines of the meeting, DPM Dar met Ambassador Majeed, FO said.

Dar underscored the importance of strengthening “regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration” within the ECO region. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to hosting the ECO Summit in 2027, the FO said.

He also appreciated the ECO secretariat’s efforts in advancing the agenda of the organisation, and its support for Pakistan’s priorities during its chairmanship.

“The secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s excellent arrangements, hospitality and coordination for the 30th ECO-COM and congratulated Pakistan on its upcoming chairmanship and hosting of the ECO-COM and ECO Summit in 2027, reflecting the importance Pakistan attaches to regionalism and multilateral cooperation,” the statement said.

It added that both sides reaffirmed the importance of close coordination during Pakistan’s chairmanship “to ensure effective implementation of agreed initiatives and advance shared goals of regional development and prosperity”.

DPM Dar also held a meeting with the OIC secretary general, welcoming him on his first visit to Islamabad since assuming office this year, the FO said.

He “reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening the OIC as a unified and effective voice of the Muslim Ummah” and assured Ahmed of Pakistan’s continued support and cooperation in advancing the OIC’s objectives.

“The secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts during the Iran-US conflict to promote peace and stability in the region. He also commended Pakistan’s active role in the OIC, including its contributions through COMSTECH to promoting scientific and technological cooperation among member states,” the FO said.

Both sides agreed to maintain close cooperation within the OIC, while also reiterating “their steadfast support for the peoples of Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir and the realisation of their right to self-determination”, it added.

The deputy premier also met with the secretary general of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), Ambassador Sultan Hajiyev, where he reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for CICA and its efforts to promote peace, security and stability in Asia through dialogue and confidence-building measures.

Hajiyev appreciated Pakistan’s constructive efforts in promoting dialogue and de-escalation. He also thanked Pakistan “for its warm hospitality and excellent arrangements” for the council meeting, the FO said.

Separately, the ECO secretary general also met Deputy FM Tursunkulov to discuss Kyrgyzstan’s “contributions and ECO’s work in a range of areas including trade, energy, industry and tourism cooperation”, he said.

World.title: Trump admin warns US air travellers of another messy day
World.content:
The Trump administration said on Sunday that the air travel havoc triggered by a no-takeoff order could drag on for another day, pushing back its timetable for a return to normal.

Hundreds more flights were cancelled and questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess.

Officials blame Friday’s huge snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables.

United States President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle.

Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system.

“The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration.

“Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted.

FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said on Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday. He also apologised for the disruption, adding that the system remains stable.

But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travellers to where they need to be.

“So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News.

“We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.”

‘I’m the secretary’

Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffic control infrastructure, such as, he said, radar equipment that dates back to the 1960s.

“So when we do work and things go wrong, of course I’m the secretary. But I also have to acknowledge what was delivered to me,” Duffy said in an interview on CNN.

As of Sunday morning, 1,460 flights within, into or out of the United States had been cancelled, according to the travel monitor site FlightAware.

The Trump administration has blamed Friday’s ground stop — meaning no planes can take off — on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines.

Friday’s disruption was only the second time such a ground stop had been issued in US airspace, which is among the busiest in the world, since the 9/11 attacks.

The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos, but it also raised serious concerns about the country’s ageing infrastructure.

Cancellations and chaos

As of 9:35pm on Saturday ET (7:35am Sunday PKT), airlines had cancelled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000, according to FlightAware, an aviation website.

That followed about 9,200 flights cancelled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications.

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. It was the longest nationwide halt to air travel since the attacks of Sept 11, 2001, and one of the single worst US travel days ever.

The issue prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday and federal agencies to scramble to determine if it was a cyberattack. But the problem was traced to FAA contractor L3Harris’ installation of at least one new router at a remote facility, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday.

“We’re working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven’t determined what the fault was,” Duffy said at a press conference.

The Professional Aviation Safety Specialists, a union representing FAA safety employees, said the issue was isolated to two routers that were updated on Friday. An official told Reuters it was believed the routers were in Arkansas and Texas.

An FAA official said the agency conducted a safety assessment before the work. The union said PASS-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop.

L3Harris said it took the issue seriously and is supporting the FAA in its investigation. Its shares last traded down about four per cent after hours on Friday.

The Trump administration previously blamed the mess on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines.

Though the FAA lifted the ground stop — meaning no planes can take off — on Friday evening, the disruption for passengers was far from over, with tens of thousands of people stranded in airports. Airlines were trying to get flight crews and other personnel in position to resume flights.

It sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before they were due to depart by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.

“Tired. Exhausted. Frustrated. Yeah, you know, it’s just a mess, right?” Lisa Beraid, 48, who works for an insurance company, told AFP as she waited for a flight on Saturday morning at New York’s La Guardia airport.

Duffy said Friday’s four-hour ground stop was declared after maintenance work to upgrade an old copper wire to a high-speed fibre cable had caused “issues” with communication with airplanes and radar feeds.

“Either through contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment… it started flooding other routers in our air traffic control system,” Duffy told reporters.

In another embarrassment, Saturday’s news conference — where administration officials also appealed for more funds to upgrade outdated systems — was delayed due to technical problems with the audio feed.

Overloaded communications centres

Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when air traffic control centres experienced instability in radar and communications systems. The router issue led to data overloading other communications centres, officials said.

“We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was [it] gave us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar,” Duffy added.

The issue affected communications at 17 of the FAA’s 22 en route centres, which control aircraft during the cruise portion of a flight.

Bedford said the FAA ordered the ground stop in case a centre lost all communications. “No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost,” Bedford added.

The FAA said it was doing additional testing with L3Harris to see if there are any additional risks.

Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and American Airlines all cancelled about 25pc of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45pc. Airlines have issued travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook flights for later dates without cost.

Funds sought to fix system strain

Friday’s disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by ageing technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers.

Duffy called on Friday for $50 billion in funding to upgrade air traffic control systems, up from his earlier request of $30bn after Congress approved $12.5bn last year.

House Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News on Saturday that he supports approving more funding for air traffic this year. Johnson’s Republicans control Congress until next year, when Democrats will take over because of their gains in the Nov 3 midterm elections.

US Representatives Rick Larsen and Andre Carson, Democrats slated next year to chair the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and aviation subcommittee, respectively, said in a joint statement Saturday that their panels will “hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again.”

Since receiving $12.5bn last year, the Transportation Department has awarded contracts worth $4.3bn but only spent $1bn, Larsen and Carson said.

Responding to Duffy’s appeal for funds, Illinois state governor and prominent Democrat, JB Pritzker, retorted, “Cut the crap”.

He wrote on X, “Trump and Republicans have controlled Congress and could have funded the system.”

New York Governor Kathy Hochul called on Duffy to resign or be fired by Trump, writing on X: “We’re fortunate no lives were lost.”

US lawmakers called for investigations into what caused the massive disruption and whether the country is adequately secure from cyber criminality.

“If today proves anything, it’s that we need to update our air traffic control system and rebuild our airport infrastructure,” Republican Senator Eric Schmitt said on X.

World.title: FIA books 8 Pakistanis deported from Turkiye for violating immigration laws
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) said on Sunday it has registered a case against eight Pakistanis deported from Turkiye for allegedly violating immigration laws.

FIA Islamabad registered the case against the eight deportees, who had travelled to Turkiye on work visas but allegedly started working elsewhere illegally instead of joining the companies concerned. Turkish police arrested them, took them to jail and later deported them to Pakistan.

The case has been registered under Sections 3 and 4 of the Passport Act, 1974. The involvement of other individuals or agents, if any, will be determined during the investigation.

The FIA Islamabad Zone reiterated its resolve to continue action against those involved in human smuggling and violations of immigration laws.

Separately, the FIA Anti-Human Trafficking Circle Rawalpindi recovered Rs3.8 million allegedly defrauded from a citizen on the pretext of providing a work permit in Portugal.
